title: Money You May Collect at the Start of a Guam Lease
bodyText:
Guam limits what you may collect when the lease begins: only the first month's rent and the security deposit, including a pet deposit where there is a pet.

So you may not take last month's rent, a second deposit, a key or remote deposit, a non-refundable move-in, cleaning or administrative fee, or a pet fee other than the pet deposit at the start of the lease.

The deposit is capped at one month's rent, and the pet deposit must be reasonable and no more than $500 per pet. The tenant may not use the deposit as the last month's rent unless you agree in writing.

Charges that arise later under the lease (a re-key cost when a key is lost, a returned-payment charge) are not affected by the start-of-lease limit. An application fee taken before the lease begins is outside the words of the limit; keep it to your actual screening cost and don't take it at signing.

If the lease starts mid-month, the cautious course is to collect only the rent for the first rental period, and the next month's rent when it falls due. Guam's statute names no penalty for collecting too much at the start.

title: Security Deposit and Pet Deposit Limits in Guam
bodyText:
In Guam the total security deposit may not be more than one month's rent. You may also charge a separate, reasonable pet deposit of no more than $500 for each pet.

Any money a tenant gives you to be held against unpaid rent, damage, unreturned keys or items, cleaning at move-out, or the loss if the tenant wrongfully leaves counts as the security deposit, whatever you call it, so it falls under the one-month cap.

At the start of the lease you may collect only the first month's rent and the deposit (with any pet deposit). An assistance animal is not a pet under federal fair-housing law, so no pet deposit is charged for one. The limits apply to every residential rental in Guam under the Rental Act, written or oral, for a fixed term or month to month.

title: Late Fees in Guam
bodyText:
No Guam statute sets a maximum late fee for residential rent or requires a grace period.

The limit comes from Guam's contract code instead: a sum fixed in advance as damages for a breach (a late fee is one) is void unless, from the nature of the case, actual damage would be impracticable or extremely difficult to fix. The library's Guam late-charge clause says so in the parties' agreement, but whether a court enforces a particular charge depends on the facts and on case law.

To reduce the risk, keep the charge to a reasonable estimate of what a late payment actually costs you, charge it once per late payment, and don't add interest on it.

Guam defines rent as every payment due under the lease, but the cautious course is to leave late charges out of the amount you demand in a nonpayment notice and never to start an eviction for an unpaid late charge alone. A prompt-payment discount from a stated full rent is an alternative some landlords use.

title: Fixed Charges for a Breach (Liquidated Damages) in Guam
bodyText:
Guam's contract code makes a sum fixed in advance as damages for breaking a contract void, except where, from the nature of the case, actual damage would be impracticable or extremely difficult to fix; then the parties may agree on an amount presumed to be the damage.

This rule reaches lease terms such as late charges, early-termination or lease-break fees, stipulated holdover charges and any fixed cleaning or re-letting charge stated as damages. It does not reach a charge for a service at its actual cost, or rent itself.

The library's Guam clauses that use a fixed amount (`late-fee-gu`, `early-termination-gu`) state the parties' agreement in the statute's terms; a court still decides whether the facts support it. Keep any fixed amount to a reasonable estimate of the loss, and don't stack it on another remedy for the same loss.

title: Notice Before Ending a Guam Lease for Unpaid Rent
bodyText:
Two Guam laws govern a nonpayment notice, and the safe course is to satisfy both.

The Rental Act requires a written notice of the nonpayment and of your intention to end the lease if the rent isn't paid within 5 working days; if it isn't paid, you may end the lease 30 working days after the tenant receives the notice (working days exclude weekends and federal and Guam government holidays).

The eviction chapter separately requires, before an unlawful-detainer case for rent, a written notice of at least 5 days requiring payment, stating the amount due, or possession, served on the tenant and on any subtenant in occupation, within one year after the rent fell due; if you want the court to declare the lease forfeited, the notice must say you elect to do so.

One notice can do both: state the rent due (leave out late charges), demand payment within 5 working days or possession, say you will end the lease and elect forfeiture if it isn't paid, and hand it to the tenant personally, which satisfies both laws' delivery rules. Don't file until 30 working days after the tenant received it.

On a property with a federally backed mortgage, also give the federal 30-day notice to vacate.

title: How an Eviction Works in Guam
bodyText: In Guam you recover possession through the Superior Court in an unlawful-detainer case; you may not lock the tenant out or remove belongings yourself. The complaint must be verified and describe the premises; for unpaid rent it must state the amount. The summons gives the tenant 5 days to appear and answer. If the tenant doesn't appear, the court still hears your proof before entering judgment. If you win, the judgment restores possession, assesses your damages and the rent found due, and the court may in its discretion enter judgment for three times that amount; the lease is declared forfeited only if your notice stated that election. An appeal doesn't stop enforcement unless the judge orders it, but under the general civil rules no execution issues until 10 days after a judgment is entered, so plan for that wait. Within 30 days after a forfeiture judgment, the tenant may ask the court for relief against forfeiture in case of hardship, on condition of paying the rent due in full. These cases get priority on the court's calendar. The Small Claims Division may also hear rent and landlord-tenant disputes up to $10,000, may stop an eviction pending a bona fide rent dispute, and may order an eviction. Guam's court rules have no eviction-specific rules or forms; the general civil rules apply. Renting property in Guam is a licensed business, and a person doing business without a required business licence may not maintain a court proceeding until it gets one, so keep your rental business licence current before you file.

title: Grounds for Eviction and Chances to Cure in Guam
No General Just-Cause Rule in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library sets a general just-cause eviction rule for written leases. A fixed-term written lease ends at the end of its term, and a periodic tenancy can be ended by the notice Guam law sets, without giving a reason. The exceptions: an oral (unwritten) lease of a tenant's primary residence, entered after January 1, 1988, runs for an initial year during which the tenant may be evicted only for nonpayment of rent or damage to the premises; after that year you must give 90 days' notice (except for nonpayment or damage), may not end it just to raise the rent, and may raise the rent no more than 5% a year. A signed written lease avoids these rules. You may not evict a tenant because of an incident of family violence, criminal sexual conduct or stalking against them, or refuse to renew solely because the tenant is a victim; and from October 1, 2026, you may not refuse to rent, or set different terms, because of a tenant's lawful source of income. Federal programs (public housing, vouchers, some federally financed properties) carry their own good-cause rules.

title: When a Guam Tenant Stays After the Lease Ends
bodyText:
If a tenant stays after the lease ends without your consent, you may bring an unlawful-detainer action for possession. If the holdover is willful and not in good faith, you may also recover an amount equal to the rent owed, your eviction costs and reasonable attorney's fees, and in any unlawful-detainer judgment the court may award your damages and rent due, or three times that amount in its discretion.

If you accept rent after the term ends, Guam law presumes the lease renewed on the same terms for the rental period (a month, where rent is monthly), so accepting rent turns the holdover into a periodic tenancy that you must end by notice.

Guam sets no daily holdover charge, and the library doesn't offer one (`edu-holdover-rate-gu`). The tagged holdover clause, `holdover-ca`, recovers actual damages and allows a month-to-month continuation.

title: Stipulated Holdover Charge: Not Offered for Guam
bodyText: Some states' libraries offer an optional daily holdover charge. For Guam the library doesn't. A charge fixed in advance for staying past the lease is a sum fixed for a breach, which Guam's contract code makes void unless actual damage would be impracticable or extremely difficult to fix, and a holdover's main loss (the rental value of the days held over) is usually easy to fix. A court may also treble the damages it finds in an unlawful-detainer judgment, and for a willful bad-faith holdover you may recover the rent owed, eviction costs and fees, so a stipulated charge would add risk without a clear gain. You may still recover the actual rental value and other actual damages (`holdover-ca`). A landlord who wants a stipulated holdover charge may add one, after taking legal advice.

title: How Notices Must Be Delivered in Guam
bodyText:
Under Guam's Rental Act, a notice to the tenant counts as received when it is handed to the tenant personally or mailed by registered or certified mail to the tenant's known residence; a notice to you counts as received when delivered at your place of business or where the lease was signed.

Notices before an unlawful-detainer case follow the eviction chapter's service rules: personal delivery; or, if the tenant is absent from home and work, leaving a copy with a person of suitable age and discretion there and mailing a copy; or, if neither place can be found, posting a copy on the property, delivering one to a person living there, and mailing one. Personal delivery satisfies both laws.

Guam's electronic-transactions law keeps any method another law specifies, so e-mail or text can't replace these methods for a required notice, even by agreement; you may send an e-mail copy as a courtesy (`electronic-notice-ma`). Federal law also doesn't validate electronic default or eviction notices for a primary residence.

title: Ending a Periodic Tenancy in Guam
bodyText: Guam's Rental Act has no section on ending a month-to-month tenancy, so the older hiring chapter supplies the rule. A rental with no agreed term is presumed to run for the period by which rent is counted (a month, where rent is monthly; monthly if nothing is agreed), and it renews at the end of each period unless one party gives notice at least as long as the period, but no more than one month, before the period ends. So for a month-to-month tenancy, give written notice at least one month before the end of a rental month, ending the tenancy at the end of that month. A fixed-term lease ends at the end of its term without notice, unless you accept rent afterward (which renews it for a period). Different rules apply to an oral lease of a primary residence (90 days' notice after its first year), to a tenancy at will (at least 30 days' written notice), to a federally backed property (the federal 30-day notice to vacate), and to federal housing programs. These periods are calendar periods; Guam's working-day definition applies only to the Rental Act.

title: Tenancy at Will in Guam
bodyText: A tenancy at will (an occupancy with no agreed term or rent period, terminable by either side) may be ended by your written notice to the tenant to leave within a period of at least 30 days stated in the notice. Only after that period expires may you re-enter or go to court for possession, and an unlawful-detainer case for a tenancy at will requires that it first be ended by this notice. Guam's statute says the notice is served as a section of the eviction chapter prescribes, but the section it names is the complaint-verification section; the eviction chapter's service section is the one that fits, so serve the notice personally or by that section's substitute methods. Most residential rentals with monthly rent are month-to-month tenancies rather than tenancies at will (`edu-termination-notice-gu`).

title: Abandonment and Property Left Behind in Guam
bodyText:
If a tenant abandons the unit, you must make reasonable efforts to re-rent it at a fair rental. If you re-rent for a term starting before the old lease ends, the old lease ends when the new tenancy begins; if you don't try to re-rent, or you accept the abandonment as a surrender, the lease is treated as ended by you on the date you learned of the abandonment.

For a tenant who abandons with no intention of returning, you may recover the lesser of the rent for the rest of the term, or the daily rent for the time needed to re-rent plus a reasonable commission plus any shortfall between the old rent and the fair rental value.

Property left behind that you judge in good faith to be of value may be stored at the tenant's expense, or sold or donated after you mail notice and wait 15 working days; sale proceeds, after rent and costs, are held in trust for 30 working days. Property of no value may be discarded.

The apartment-keeper's lien on a tenant's belongings is a separate route with its own exemptions (see `edu-landlord-lien-gu`). Don't remove a tenant's property while the tenant is still in possession; that is a lockout.

title: Ending a Guam Lease Early
Entering a Tenant's Unit in Guam
bodyText:
Guam's entry rule is built on the tenant's consent. A tenant may not unreasonably refuse you entry to inspect, make necessary or agreed repairs, decorations, alterations or improvements, supply agreed services, or show the unit to prospective buyers, lenders or tenants.

Except in an emergency or where it is impracticable, you must give at least 24 hours' notice and enter only at reasonable hours, and you may not abuse the right of entry or use it to harass.

You have no other right of entry except by court order, when the tenant appears to have abandoned the unit, or during the tenant's extended absence (over 7 working days) for inspection, maintenance and safe-keeping.

If a tenant refuses lawful access, you may get a court order compelling access or end the lease, and recover damages, costs, lost rent and attorney's fees. If you enter unlawfully or make repeated harassing demands, the tenant may get an injunction or end the lease and recover damages and fees.

These rights can't be waived in the lease, so don't shorten the 24-hour notice by agreement.

title: Changing Rent or Terms in Guam
bodyText:
In a month-to-month tenancy you may change the terms, including the rent, by written notice at least 30 days before the end of a rental month; the change takes effect at the end of that month if the tenant stays. If the lease that created the month-to-month tenancy says so in writing, the notice may be as short as 7 days before the end of the month (`term-change-notice-gu`).

During a fixed term you can't change the rent or terms unless the lease provides for it (`rent-escalation-la`, `tax-insurance-escalation-la`) or the tenant agrees. New rules follow a separate procedure (`rules-gu`).

Two Guam limits apply to any increase: raising rent on the basis of a shortage caused or anticipated by a disaster is an unfair trade practice, and after a major disaster the Governor may freeze residential rents for up to 120 days. An oral lease of a primary residence may not be increased more than 5% a year. Guam has no other rent control.

title: Which Guam Laws Govern a Residential Lease
bodyText:
Guam's main landlord-tenant law is the Guam Landlord and Tenant Rental Act of 2018 (21 GCA Chapter 48). It covers every rental agreement for a dwelling unit in Guam, written or oral, and applies only to residential leases. It counts its deadlines in working days (weekends and federal and Guam government holidays excluded).

The older Hiring of Real Property chapter (18 GCA Chapter 51), which covers commercial and residential leases, still applies where the Act is silent (for example, the presumed length of a periodic tenancy, renewal by accepting rent, notice to end a periodic tenancy, the ban on renting part of a room, and the rules for oral leases), but the Act wins in any conflict (for example, the tenant's repair-and-deduct right in the old chapter yields to the Act's ban on self-help repairs).

Evictions run under the forcible entry and detainer chapter (21 GCA Chapter 21), which the Act doesn't displace. General contract, property and consumer laws also apply.

Articles 5 (Guam Safe Housing Act) and 6 (source-of-income discrimination, from October 1, 2026) can't be waived or modified by agreement.

title: Rent Payment Methods in Guam
bodyText:
No Guam statute tells a private landlord which rent payment methods to accept, bars requiring electronic payment, or caps a fee for paying by a particular method; you set the methods in the lease (`acceptable-payment-methods`).

Guam's business-tax laws still matter, because renting real property is a licensed business. It is unlawful to offer a lower price when a transaction is paid in cash, so don't give a cash discount on rent. A higher price that only recovers charges assessed to you, such as a card processor's fee, is allowed, so a card charge should be no more than the processor actually charges you (`card-payment-charge-gu`).

A business that does more than ten taxable cash transactions a day must give receipts, and refusing checks and electronic payment is one sign Guam's tax regulators use to target cash-based businesses, so keep a non-cash method available and give a receipt for cash.

Don't add a processing charge to the money collected at the start of the lease, which Guam limits to the first month's rent and the deposit. From October 1, 2026, you may not set payment terms that treat a tenant differently because rent comes from a housing-assistance program.

title: No Algorithm-Specific Rent Rule in Guam; Antitrust Law Applies
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations or the court rules searched for this library bans or regulates setting rents or lease terms with algorithmic pricing or revenue-management software. Guam has created an Artificial Intelligence Regulatory Taskforce to study AI and recommend rules, but it regulates nothing yet. Guam's general antitrust law does apply: a contract, combination or conspiracy between two or more persons in restraint of trade in a relevant market, or one that controls or attempts to control the price of any goods or services in restraint of trade, is unlawful and a felony; contracts that break it are void, and an injured person may sue for up to three times the damages plus fees, with large civil penalties available to the Attorney General. Setting your own rent with a pricing tool is not addressed by any Guam statute; agreeing with competing landlords on rents, directly or through a shared tool that pools their nonpublic rent data, is the risk. Federal antitrust law also applies in Guam. Take advice before using a shared pricing service.

title: Application and Screening Fees in Guam
bodyText: No Guam statute caps a landlord's rental application or screening fee, requires a refund of an unused fee, or requires a written screening-criteria notice before you take one. The limit on money collected when the lease begins (first month's rent and the deposit only) speaks of money taken at lease commencement, so an application fee taken before then is outside its words; keep the fee to your actual screening cost, say in writing whether it is refundable, and never take it at signing. A real estate licensee who charges a prospective tenant a fee to find a rental or furnish rental information must give a contract or receipt promising to repay everything above a $10 service charge if the applicant doesn't obtain a rental (demand within 10 calendar days after the service period ends), and the full fee if the information was not current or accurate. From October 1, 2026, a credit check is protected under Guam's source-of-income law only if you check every prospective tenant's credit, so check everyone or no one, and you may not refuse an applicant because of a lawful source of income, such as a housing voucher. You may not refuse an applicant solely because the applicant or a household member is a victim of family violence, criminal sexual conduct or stalking, or ended an earlier lease under Guam's Safe Housing Act. FEDERAL: the Fair Credit Reporting Act's adverse-action notice and fair-housing law also apply.

title: How Payments Are Applied in Guam
bodyText:
Guam's contract code sets a default order for applying a payment that could go toward more than one debt.

If the tenant says, when paying, which debt the payment is for, you must apply it that way. If the tenant says nothing, you may choose, within a reasonable time, which debt then due to apply it to, and once you have chosen you can't change it without the tenant's consent. If neither of you chooses, the law applies it to interest due, then principal due, then the debt that fell due earliest, then unsecured before secured debts, ratably within a class.

The library's clause for Guam (`application-of-payments`) applies each payment to the oldest unpaid Monthly Rent first unless the tenant directs otherwise for that payment, which fits this rule and protects you from a nonpayment dispute: applying a rent payment to late charges first could leave rent "unpaid" in a way a court may not accept, and the cautious course is to keep late charges out of a nonpayment notice anyway (`edu-late-fee-gu`).

Housing-assistance payments made for a tenant should be applied to the tenant's share of rent they are meant to cover.

title: Collection Fees on Unpaid Rent in Guam
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library sets, caps or bans a fee a landlord or a collection agency may add to a past-due rent or damage debt, and none is a collection-agency fee rule of the kind some places have.

Two general rules shape what a lease can say. First, a fixed collection fee stated in advance (for example, a flat $100 or 25% of the debt whatever the cost) is a sum fixed in advance for a breach, void unless actual damage would be impracticable or extremely difficult to fix, and collection costs usually can be fixed; a clause that reimburses the reasonable costs you actually incur avoids that problem (`collection-costs-gu`).

Second, Guam makes every lease provision for costs or attorney's fees mutual, so a collection-cost clause also lets the tenant recover costs in the reverse case; write it as mutual.

Interest on an unpaid amount is a separate question (`edu-unpaid-amount-interest-gu`). Federal debt-collection law governs third-party collectors (FEDERAL).

title: Fee Disclosure and All-In Pricing in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library is a rental all-in pricing or junk-fee law, requires every mandatory fee to appear on the lease's first page, or sets a verbatim fee-disclosure sentence. Guam's Deceptive Trade Practices Act does make it unlawful to charge a consumer for goods or services not provided, or to charge someone who has already contracted additional charges, including taxes, not agreed in the contract; whether that Act reaches a residential lease of ten years or less is unsettled, so the cautious course is to list every recurring or conditional charge, with its amount or how it is figured, in the lease, and to charge nothing that isn't listed. Guam's business-tax law also makes it unlawful to advertise or hold out that the business privilege tax is not part of the price, so don't present the tax as a separate government charge added to rent (`edu-rent-tax-gu`). Remember that at the start of the lease you may collect only the first month's rent and the deposit, and that, from October 1, 2026, a rental advertisement may not indicate any limitation based on a tenant's source of income.

title: Charging for Services Not Provided in Guam
bodyText: Guam has no landlord-specific rule against fees for services you don't provide, and no rule like some places' ban on charging for services needed to keep a unit habitable. Guam's Deceptive Trade Practices Act does make it unlawful to charge, or try to charge, a consumer for goods or services not provided or not to be provided, and knowingly to bill for amounts the consumer has already paid. Whether that Act reaches a residential lease is unsettled, so the cautious course is to charge only for services you actually provide, at the amount the lease states, and to stop a service charge when the service stops. The Rental Act points the same way: repairs needed to keep the premises fit and habitable are your duty, so don't charge a separate fee for them unless a good-faith written agreement shifts a task to the tenant (`tenant-repair-agreement-gu`); a charge for repairing damage the tenant caused must be the actual and reasonable cost, itemized (`tenant-caused-damage-gu`); and deposit deductions must be itemized with receipts. If you charge for a service, keep records showing it was provided.

title: Fees Count as Rent Under Guam's Rental Act
bodyText:
Guam's Rental Act defines rent as all payments to be made to you or for your benefit under the rental agreement, so for the Act's purposes every fee and charge the lease requires (pet rent, parking, utilities you bill, late charges, repair bills) is rent, whatever the lease calls it; no "additional rent" label is needed.

Three consequences follow. First, at the start of the lease you may collect only the first month's rent and the deposit, so a fee due at signing is a problem even though it is "rent" (`edu-move-in-money-gu`).

Second, where tenant damage materially affects health and safety and the tenant doesn't fix it within 5 working days after your written notice (or as promptly as an emergency requires), the Act lets you do the work and bill the itemized actual and reasonable cost as rent on the next rent date.

Third, the definition is the Act's own: the eviction chapter's five-day notice for unpaid rent doesn't adopt it, so the cautious course is to demand only periodic rent in a nonpayment notice, pursue unpaid fees separately (or from the deposit at move-out), and never base an eviction on an unpaid fee alone (`edu-nonpayment-notice-gu`).

For a tenant with a federal housing voucher, the program's own rules on what the tenant may be charged also apply (FEDERAL).

title: Passing Government Fees to Tenants in Guam
bodyText: Guam has no city or county governments, and no provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library either authorizes or forbids having a tenant reimburse a government fee charged to you. The fees you will meet are territorial: renting a dwelling is a licensed business (an annual service license of $10 if you rent no more than one family residential unit, or $25 or $5 per unit, whichever is greater, for multiple units), real property tax, and residential garbage collection, which the owner must subscribe to and pay for. Because Guam's Rental Act treats every payment due to you under the lease as rent, a reimbursement the lease requires is part of the rent: state it in the lease with its amount or formula, don't collect it at the start of the lease (only the first month's rent and the deposit may be collected then), and don't add it later without a change of terms the law allows. Present it as part of the rent, not as a separate government charge (`edu-rent-tax-gu`). For garbage, an owner of a residential building of four units or less may skip the subscription if the lease obligates the tenant to subscribe, but the owner stays responsible to the Solid Waste Authority.

title: Government Fines and Penalties in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library bars or regulates passing a government fine on to a tenant. Some Guam laws reach the tenant directly: the owner and the tenant of a lot with an illegal water or sewer hookup are personally, jointly and severally liable for the penalty and the estimated value of water used, and both must make sure there are no illegal hookups; an owner or lessee who disobeys a building-code notice or order may be fined up to $1,500. A lease may require the tenant to reimburse you for a fine or penalty that the tenant, the tenant's household or guests caused, at the amount actually imposed; that is reimbursement of an actual loss, not a fixed charge. Don't make the tenant pay a fine that results from your own failure to meet building and housing codes or to keep the premises fit and habitable, because the lease can't shift those duties except by a good-faith agreement, and an unagreed charge risks Guam's consumer-protection law. If the water utility is billing you as the customer, it may not disconnect your tenant without first offering the tenant service in the tenant's own name, and it may not collect your unpaid bill from the tenant.

title: No Statutory Late-Fee Cap in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations or the court rules searched for this library caps a residential late fee, sets a minimum grace period, or limits how often a late fee may be charged. The limit that does apply is Guam's contract rule on sums fixed in advance for a breach: a late fee is void unless, from the nature of the case, actual damage would be impracticable or extremely difficult to fix, in which case the parties may agree in the lease on an amount presumed to be the damage. See `edu-late-fee-gu` and the library's Guam late-charge clause `late-fee-gu`. Keep the fee to a reasonable estimate of what a late payment costs you, charge it once per late payment, don't charge interest on it, and leave it out of any nonpayment notice. For late housing-assistance payments, see `edu-subsidy-late-fee-gu`.

title: No Lease-Type Parity Rule in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires month-to-month tenants to get the same terms as fixed-term tenants or caps the rent difference between lease types. The Rental Act applies to every rental agreement for a dwelling unit, written or oral, whatever its term, so its protections are the same for both. The real differences come from the older general laws: a month-to-month tenancy can be ended, or its terms (including rent) changed, by written notice tied to the end of a rental month (`edu-term-change-notice-gu`, `edu-termination-notice-gu`), while a fixed term can't be changed mid-term unless the lease provides for it. An oral lease of a tenant's primary residence carries its own limits (a one-year initial period during which eviction is allowed only for nonpayment or damage, 90 days' notice after that, and rent increases of no more than 5% a year), which don't apply to a written lease signed by both parties. If you rent an accessory dwelling unit (or the main house while you live in the ADU), the rental must be under a written agreement signed by you and the tenant for at least six months, after which the same tenant may continue month to month.

title: Time Limits for Rent and Damage Claims in Guam
bodyText: Guam's general time limits for lawsuits come from its Code of Civil Procedure. A suit on a written lease (for unpaid rent or damages under the lease) must be brought within four years; a suit on an oral lease, or on a liability created by law other than a penalty, within three years; a suit for trespass on or injury to real property within three years; and a suit on a law imposing a penalty or forfeiture, when given to an individual, within one year unless that law sets another period. Specific rules shorten some periods: a tenant's suit to recover a security deposit must be started within one year after the rental agreement ends, and an unlawful-detainer notice for unpaid rent may be served only within one year after the rent became due. Guam's code says an acknowledgment or new promise extends a period only if it is in writing signed by the person to be charged; unlike some places, its text does not say that a part payment restarts the period, and no Guam case on part payments was searched. A lease can't shorten the tenant's deposit-suit period, because Rental Act rights can't be waived.

title: No Rent-Concession Rule in Guam
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library regulates rent concessions such as a free month, a move-in credit or reduced rent for the first months.

You may offer them; state each one in the lease (the library's tagged clause `rent-concession-wi` does this).

Three Guam rules affect how you write one. First, a clause making the tenant repay a concession if the tenant breaks the lease or leaves early fixes in advance what the tenant pays for a breach, which Guam's contract code makes void unless actual damage would be impracticable or extremely difficult to fix (`edu-liquidated-damages-gu`); the cautious course is to make a concession unconditional, or to recover only your actual loss.

Second, a concession doesn't change what you may collect at the start of the lease: only the first month's rent (as reduced by any concession for that month) and the deposit.

Third, if you describe a monthly rent with a concession built in, be clear which figure is the rent for the deposit cap (one month's rent) and for any later increase notice.

title: Rent Control in Guam
bodyText: Guam has no general rent control or rent stabilization, no rent registration, and no local governments that could adopt them; you may set the rent for a new tenancy and change it as the lease or the law on changing terms allows (`edu-term-change-notice-gu`). Three limits apply. First, an oral lease of a tenant's primary residence entered after January 1, 1988 may not be increased by more than 5% a year (written leases signed by both parties are exempt, which is one reason to put every lease in writing). Second, raising rent on the basis of a shortage caused or anticipated by a disaster is an unfair trade practice, with damages of five times the overcharge for rentals. Third, after a disaster that seriously damages 500 or more permanent homes, a typhoon with sustained winds of 100 mph or more, or an earthquake above 7.0 on Guam, the Governor may by executive order freeze residential rents at the level of the day before the disaster for up to 120 days; check for any current executive order after a typhoon. Public housing and federally assisted units follow their programs' own rent rules (FEDERAL), and Guam's source-of-income rule doesn't apply to housing projects subsidized by public funds or lands.

title: No General Bar on Demanding Rent for a Substandard Unit in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library forbids demanding or collecting rent while a unit is officially cited as substandard, as California's rule does. Rent stops or drops only in the situations the Rental Act names: if you don't deliver possession on the start date, rent abates until you do (and the tenant may end the lease on at least 5 working days' written notice); if you willfully or negligently fail to supply essential services the lease promises (running water, electricity, gas, hot water), the tenant may, after written notice, secure the services and deduct their actual and reasonable cost from the rent, or buy substitute housing and owe no rent for that period; if you don't begin, or make a good-faith effort to begin, repairing windstorm damage to the weatherhead within 10 working days after you become aware of it, the tenant may have a master and licensed electrician repair it and, after giving you an itemized invoice, deduct the reasonable cost from rent (spread over no more than three months if it exceeds one month's rent), unless an electrician or engineer has found the building unsafe for other reasons or the tenant has apparently abandoned it; after a fire or casualty that substantially impairs the unit, the tenant may vacate and end the lease, or vacate the unusable part and pay rent reduced in proportion. The tenant may not otherwise withhold rent for repairs not done. A serious, unremedied health-and-safety breach still lets the tenant end the lease (written notice; 14 working days to fix; termination no earlier than 30 working days after receipt) and recover damages. Working days exclude weekends and federal and Guam government holidays. Keep your rental business license current: Guam law calls renting without the license's permission illegal, though no Guam statute read for this library says that bars collecting rent.

title: Rent Increases During a Lease Term in Guam
bodyText:
During a fixed term, Guam law gives you no right to raise the rent unless the lease provides for it or the tenant agrees; a month-to-month tenancy is different, because its terms can be changed by written notice tied to the end of a rental month (`edu-term-change-notice-gu`).

So a scheduled or index-based increase must be written into the lease (`rent-escalation-la`), as must any pass-through of tax or insurance increases (`tax-insurance-escalation-la`); the library also offers an optional notice-based increase with a tenant exit right (`rent-increase-midterm-gu`).

Guam has no general retaliation statute of the kind that elsewhere makes a lease escalation clause a safe harbour, but two specific rules apply: you may not retaliate against a tenant because a household member is a victim of family violence, criminal sexual conduct or stalking, and you may not retaliate against someone for opposing housing discrimination.

Any increase is also subject to Guam's disaster rules: raising rent on the basis of a disaster shortage is an unfair trade practice, and a Governor's post-disaster rent freeze (up to 120 days) overrides a scheduled increase that falls inside it.

title: Notice of a Rent Increase in Guam
bodyText:
Guam's rent-increase notice rule is the general change-of-terms rule for month-to-month leases, which also governs tenancies under the Rental Act because the Act is silent on it: you may raise the rent by written notice given at least 30 days before the end of a rental month, effective at the end of that month if the tenant stays; a lease that creates the month-to-month tenancy may shorten the notice to 7 days (`term-change-notice-gu`; full rule in `edu-term-change-notice-gu`).

These are calendar days, computed by excluding the first day and including the last.

There is no separate notice period for raising the rent at the end of a fixed term; for a fixed term, the new rent is part of offering a new lease, and a tenant who stays and pays after the term ends is presumed to renew on the same terms for a month at a time. A rent increase during a fixed term needs a lease clause (`edu-rent-escalation-gu`).

Deliver the notice personally or by registered or certified mail. An oral lease of a primary residence can't be raised more than 5% a year, and Guam's disaster price-gouging and rent-freeze rules apply to any increase (`edu-rent-control-gu`).

title: Paying Rent in Installments in Guam
bodyText:
No Guam statute regulates paying rent in installments. Rent is payable at the time and place the parties agree, so a lease may split a month's rent into scheduled installments (`rent-installments-or`, tagged for Guam); if nothing is agreed, rent falls due at the end of each rental period.

Each installment is rent due on its own date, so a missed installment is unpaid rent: the Rental Act's nonpayment notice (5 working days to pay; termination no earlier than 30 working days after the tenant receives it) and the eviction chapter's 5-day notice both run from an installment that was due and unpaid (`edu-nonpayment-notice-gu`).

A late charge should apply only as the late-charge clause allows, and only once for the rental period.

Installments don't change the start-of-lease limit: at commencement you may collect only the first month's rent and the deposit, so schedule a first installment that doesn't exceed the first month's rent. Working days exclude weekends and federal and Guam government holidays.

title: When and Where Rent Is Paid in Guam
bodyText:
Under Guam's Rental Act, rent is payable without demand or notice at the time and place the parties agree, so the lease should state the amount, the due date and where and how to pay (`rent-payment`, tagged for Guam; `edu-payment-methods-gu`).

If the lease is silent, the older default makes rent payable at the end of each rental period, and if there is no rental agreement at all the tenant owes the fair market rental value.

Because rent is due without demand, you need not send a bill, but you must give the written notices the law requires before ending the lease for nonpayment (`edu-nonpayment-notice-gu`).

The tenant may lawfully pay less only where the Act allows: deducting the cost of securing essential services the landlord willfully or negligently failed to supply, or the cost of a weatherhead repair after a windstorm, in each case on the Act's conditions; otherwise the tenant may not withhold rent for repairs not done.

Apart from exemptions such as your own regular employees or a resident manager living on the premises, anyone who collects rent for you for compensation must be licensed under Guam's real estate licensing law, so use a licensed property manager.

title: Rent Receipts in Guam
bodyText: Guam has no landlord-specific receipt statute, but its contract code gives every debtor the right to require a written receipt from the creditor for anything delivered in performance of an obligation, so a tenant who asks for a receipt for rent, a deposit or any other payment is entitled to one. Guam's business-tax law separately makes it unlawful to conduct more than ten taxable business transactions a day in cash without giving a receipt or other record when the means to do so are available; renting is a licensed, taxable business, so a landlord taking many cash payments is covered. The simplest course is to give a dated written receipt for every cash payment and on request for any other payment, showing the amount, what it was for (rent for which period, deposit, pet deposit) and any balance due, and to keep a copy. Receipts also help you prove the start-of-lease limit (only the first month's rent and the deposit) and the deposit you must account for at move-out. Guam's evidence code also presumes that earlier rent was paid when the tenant produces a receipt for a later payment; the presumption can be overcome with other evidence, so keep your own payment ledger and write any unpaid earlier balance on the receipt you give. Guam has no rule making a missing receipt an eviction defense.

title: No Rent-Reporting Rule in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations or the court rules searched for this library creates a rent-reporting program, requires you to offer positive rent reporting, bars requiring a tenant to join one, or requires notice before you report late rent to a credit bureau. Federal credit-reporting law governs what you and any reporting service may furnish and the tenant's right to dispute it (FEDERAL). If you report, apply the same practice to every tenant; from October 1, 2026, Guam's source-of-income law forbids treating a tenant differently in the terms of a tenancy because rent comes from a housing-assistance program, and Guam's Safe Housing Act forbids disclosing information a tenant gave you about family violence, criminal sexual conduct or stalking without the tenant's written consent or a legal requirement, so keep any such information out of a report. A fee for a reporting service that the lease has the tenant pay to you or for your benefit is rent under the Rental Act, so at the start of the lease you can collect only the first month's charge, as part of the first month's rent, together with the security deposit, and no separate sign-up fee.

title: Taxes on Rent in Guam
bodyText: Guam has no sales tax on residential rent. Your rental income is subject to Guam's business privilege tax, a monthly tax on the gross income of a business, which includes rentals; the general rate is 4.5% from October 1, 2025, falling to 4% from October 1, 2026, and the first $40,000 a year of rental income from real property is exempt for a person whose gross annual rental income from real property was under $50,000 in the most recent tax year. The tax is yours, not the tenant's, and Guam makes it unlawful for a taxpayer to advertise or hold out in any way that the tax is not part of the price; the Compiler's note to that law reports a Guam Supreme Court decision that showing the tax as a separate government charge on top of the price violated it. So set the rent to cover the tax, and don't add a "BPT" line to the rent or describe it as a tax the tenant owes. Guam's hotel occupancy tax (11%, or 4% for a registered bed and breakfast) applies only to transient occupants of a hotel, lodging house, bed and breakfast or similar facility, meaning stays of less than 90 consecutive days; an ordinary residential lease is not subject to it.

title: Listing Required Fees in a Guam Lease
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a lease to list every fee, sets a notice period for adding a fee later, or requires a statement of each fee's purpose.

Several Guam rules still make listing them the safe course. Guam's consumer-protection law makes it unlawful to charge someone who has already contracted additional charges, including taxes, that weren't agreed in the contract, as a condition of performing it (its reach to residential leases is unsettled).

Every fee the lease requires the tenant to pay you is rent under the Rental Act, and at the start of the lease only the first month's rent (including the first month of any monthly fee) and the deposit may be taken, so a one-time fee can't be collected then.

A fixed fee for a breach (late, lease-break, holdover) is valid only within Guam's liquidated-damages rule.

And during a fixed term you can't add a fee without the tenant's agreement; in a month-to-month tenancy a new fee is a change of terms that needs written notice at least 30 days before the end of a rental month (or 7 days if the lease so provides).

The library's Guam clause `fees-and-charges-gu` lists every fee in one place.

title: No Shutdown Rent Protection for Government Workers in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library delays rent, waives late charges or pauses evictions for federal or Guam government employees or contractors affected by a government shutdown, even though many Guam tenants work for the federal government or the military. The ordinary rules apply: rent is due when the lease says, and ending a lease for nonpayment requires the Rental Act's written notice (5 working days to pay; termination no earlier than 30 working days after the tenant receives it) and the eviction chapter's 5-day notice. The one shutdown rule in Guam's code points the other way: from October 1, 2026, Guam's source-of-income law, which forbids treating a tenant differently because rent comes from a housing-assistance program, says that if the housing program's initial payment to you is not made on time under HUD's rules because of processing delays or a government shutdown, you may exercise any right or remedy the law otherwise gives you. Many landlords agree a short payment plan with a furloughed tenant; put any such agreement in writing. Working days exclude weekends and federal and Guam government holidays. FEDERAL: servicemembers have separate federal protections.

title: Guam Money Limits at a Glance
bodyText: Guam law sets these money limits for residential rentals, whatever the lease says. Move-in money: only the first month's rent and the security deposit (with any pet deposit) at the start of the lease. Security deposit: no more than one month's rent, plus a reasonable pet deposit of no more than $500 per pet. Deposit return: within 14 working days after the lease ends, with an itemized statement and receipts; wrongful and willful retention can cost three times the amount withheld. Late fees and other fixed charges for a breach: no dollar cap, but void unless actual damage would be impracticable or extremely difficult to fix (`edu-liquidated-damages-gu`). Application fee: no cap for landlords; a real estate licensee who charges a rental-information fee must refund all but $10 if no rental results and the prospective tenant asks within 10 days after the licensee's contracted services end (the whole fee if the rental information was not current or accurate). Interest: 6% a year on money owed after demand unless a written agreement sets another lawful rate (`edu-unpaid-amount-interest-gu`). Rent increases: no rent control, but an oral lease of a primary residence may rise no more than 5% a year, and disaster price-gouging and rent-freeze rules apply (`edu-rent-control-gu`). Safe Housing Act: a tenant who ends a lease as a victim owes one month's rent after vacating. Working days exclude weekends and federal and Guam government holidays.

title: No Guam Rule on Prorating Subsidized Rent for Habitability
bodyText: No Guam statute or regulation in the corpus sets a formula for reducing a subsidized tenant's share, or the housing authority's share, of rent when part of a unit is unfit. Guam's Rental Act has only general rent-relief rules that apply to every tenant: after a fire or casualty not caused by the tenant or the tenant's family, guests or invitees that substantially impairs enjoyment of the unit, a tenant who, where continued occupancy is lawful, vacates the unusable part owes rent reduced in proportion to the drop in fair rental value; if you willfully or negligently fail to supply essential services the lease promises (and the tenant, the tenant's family or others on the premises didn't cause the problem), the tenant may, after written notice to you, get substitute housing and owes no rent for that time; if you don't deliver possession, rent abates. The Act doesn't say how a reduction is split between the tenant's share and a housing-assistance payment; for a voucher tenancy, the federal program's own rules on withholding or stopping assistance payments for a unit that fails inspection govern the authority's share (FEDERAL), and GHURA administers those programs in Guam. A dwelling rented under Guam's one-time temporary business license must pass inspection, by a HUD-certified or GHURA-authorized inspector where the tenant receives federal housing assistance. Keep the unit fit and habitable; the duty can't be waived.

title: Late Charges When a Housing Subsidy Pays Part of the Rent in Guam
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library expressly bars charging a tenant a late fee for a late housing-assistance payment.

The cautious course is not to: a late charge is valid in Guam only as an agreed estimate of the damage from the tenant's own late payment, and the authority's lateness is not the tenant's breach; and from October 1, 2026, Guam's source-of-income law forbids treating a tenant differently in the terms of a tenancy because of the receipt of public housing assistance.

That law carves out one situation: if the program's initial payment to you is late under HUD's rules because of processing delays or a government shutdown, you may exercise any right or remedy the law otherwise allows; it says nothing about later late payments.

Apply your late-charge clause (`late-fee-gu`) only to the tenant's own share, and take up a late assistance payment with GHURA. Federal voucher rules (the HUD tenancy addendum) also limit what you may charge a voucher tenant (FEDERAL).

The source-of-income rule doesn't apply to housing projects subsidized by public funds or lands, or to Chamorro Land Trust leases.

title: Passing Property Tax or Insurance Increases to a Guam Tenant
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library governs passing real property tax or insurance increases through to a residential tenant, requires the clause to state the tenant's exact share, or requires you to refund an abatement.

It is a contract term: during a fixed term you may collect a share of an increase only if the lease says so (`tax-insurance-escalation-la`, tagged for Guam, states the share, the base year and the calculation, and requires a copy of the bill).

Several Guam rules shape the clause. Every such payment is rent under the Rental Act, and at the start of the lease you may collect only the first month's rent and the deposit, so bill a share of an increase when it falls due, not at move-in.

Guam's consumer-protection law makes it unlawful to charge a consumer additional charges, including taxes, not agreed in the contract as a condition of performance (its reach to residential leases is unsettled), so don't add a pass-through the lease doesn't state.

A pass-through of your business privilege tax is different: don't show it as a separate tax (`edu-rent-tax-gu`).

And raising rent on the basis of a shortage caused or anticipated by a disaster is an unfair trade practice, so keep a post-typhoon insurance pass-through to the premium actually charged, with the bill.

If your tax bill is later reduced, the fair course is to credit the tenant's share.

title: Interest on Unpaid Rent and Damages in Guam
bodyText:
Guam's legal rate of interest is 6% a year. It applies to money owed on an account after demand, and to judgments, without any lease clause; so once you have made a written demand for unpaid rent or damages, the debt can carry 6% a year.

A higher rate needs a written agreement, and it may not exceed the rates Guam's consumer-credit title allows; this library doesn't compute that ceiling for lease debts, so the optional clause (`interest-on-unpaid-amounts-gu`) leaves the rate to you with that limit. When no period is stated, an interest rate is an annual rate.

Interest is the law's compensation for the use or detention of money, not a fixed charge for a breach, so it is outside Guam's liquidated-damages rule; but don't charge interest on a late charge, which is itself compensation for late payment, and don't stack it so that the total is a penalty.

Interest the lease itself requires is rent under the Rental Act's definition; interest the law adds after demand is not a payment under the lease. Either way, leave it out of a nonpayment notice, which should state only the unpaid periodic rent as the amount due (the eviction notice must state 'the amount which is due' (21 GCA § 21103(b))).

title: Move-In Condition Records in Guam
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a move-in inventory, a joint inspection, photographs or a move-out inspection, or sets a notice or penalty tied to one.

A written condition record is still the most useful thing you can make at the start of a Guam tenancy, because the Rental Act measures the deposit against it: you may use the deposit to clean the unit back to as fit a condition as when the tenant took possession, less normal wear and tear, and to remedy damage from the tenant's failure to comply with the Act; normal wear and tear doesn't include items missing from the unit.

If you keep any part of the deposit, you must give written reasons with costs itemized and receipts (or estimates, if the repairs can't be done within 14 working days) within 14 working days after the lease ends, and in a dispute the court awards the disputed amount plus the cost of the suit to the side that wins (and if you kept it wrongfully and willfully, the court may award the tenant three times the amount wrongfully kept).

A signed, dated condition report with photographs is the best evidence of the starting condition (`move-in-condition-report-gu`). The tenant's acknowledgment of condition doesn't waive your duty to keep the premises fit and habitable (`existing-condition-pr`). Working days exclude weekends and federal and Guam government holidays.

title: No Pre-Set Deposit Charges in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library lets a lease pre-set what you will charge against the deposit for carpet cleaning, painting or other work, and its deposit law points the other way: if you keep any part of the deposit, the costs (such as cleaning or specific repairs) must be itemized and copies of receipts included, with written estimates allowed only if the work can't be done within 14 working days. So a schedule of charges in the lease can serve as a guide to what typical work costs, but every deduction must still match a cost you actually incurred (or a written estimate), for work the deposit may lawfully cover: cleaning back to the move-in condition less normal wear and tear, repairing damage from the tenant's failure to comply, unpaid rent, unreturned keys or items, and damages caused by a tenant who wrongfully quits the unit. A flat cleaning or repair charge stated as damages whatever the actual cost is a sum fixed in advance for a breach, void under Guam's contract code unless actual damage would be impracticable or extremely difficult to fix, and it is easy to fix here. Requiring professional cleaning regardless of condition goes beyond the deposit's statutory purpose (the library doesn't tag `carpet-cleaning-ar` for Guam). Working days exclude weekends and federal and Guam government holidays.

title: Unclaimed Deposit Refunds in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library expressly makes an uncashed or undeliverable deposit refund reportable to the government, or lets you keep a refund the tenant doesn't claim. Guam's escheat laws are aimed at decedents' estates, long-dormant bank deposits, money held by courts and the Treasurer, and sums business associations owe their shareholders or members; one 2017 section in the same group also sends to the Treasurer of Guam property held in a fiduciary capacity for another person that the owner hasn't claimed or asked about for more than three years after it became payable, and whether that reaches a landlord holding an unclaimed deposit refund is unsettled (no Guam case was searched). So the refund stays the tenant's money. Mail the itemized statement and any refund to the tenant's last known or forwarding address on or before the 14th working day after the lease ends and keep the Post Office proof of mailing, which satisfies your deadline even if the mail comes back. If it is returned or not cashed, keep the money identified as the tenant's and pay it when the tenant asks; the tenant may sue for a deposit within one year after the lease ends. Don't put a clause in the lease forfeiting an unclaimed refund to you: the Rental Act's rights can't be waived. (Proceeds from selling abandoned property follow a different rule; see `edu-abandoned-property-gu`.) Working days exclude weekends and federal and Guam government holidays.

title: No Deposit Installment Right in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library gives tenants a right to pay a security deposit in installments or sets an installment schedule. You may agree to accept the deposit in installments if you wish; nothing in Guam law forbids it. If you do, keep three Guam rules in mind. The total of all deposit installments (apart from a pet deposit of no more than $500 per pet) may not exceed one month's rent. At the start of the lease you may collect only the first month's rent and the deposit, so an installment plan can lower what is due at signing but can't add any other charge to it. And every installment is part of the security deposit you must account for within 14 working days after the lease ends, with an itemized statement and receipts for anything kept. Put the schedule in writing, and say that a missed deposit installment is a breach handled under the default terms of the lease rather than a reason to treat later rent as unpaid. Working days exclude weekends and federal and Guam government holidays.

title: Security Deposit and Last Month's Rent in Guam
bodyText:
In Guam the tenant may not use the security deposit as the last month's rent unless you agree with the tenant in writing; either way, you keep the right to have the tenant pay for damage the tenant caused.

Whether to agree is your choice. You may agree in the lease itself (`deposit-last-month-rent-gu`) or later in a separate signed writing. Before agreeing, remember that once the deposit has gone to rent there may be nothing left to cover cleaning or damage, and you would have to recover those costs from the tenant directly.

You also may not collect last month's rent in advance at the start of the lease: only the first month's rent and the deposit may be collected then (`edu-move-in-money-gu`).

A tenant who simply stops paying the last month's rent without your written agreement has not paid rent, and the usual nonpayment notices apply, though at the end of a lease the practical course is often to account for the unpaid rent from the deposit within 14 working days after the lease ends, with an itemized statement. Working days exclude weekends and federal and Guam government holidays.

title: Deposit Refund Does Not Depend on a Tenant Notice in Guam
bodyText: Guam's deposit law doesn't make the refund depend on the tenant giving notice of moving out, a forwarding address, a demand or the keys by a deadline. Your duty runs from the end of the rental agreement: within 14 working days after it ends, give the tenant the itemized written notice of anything kept (with receipts or, if repairs can't be done in time, estimates) and the balance. You meet the deadline by mailing on or before the 14th working day and getting acceptable proof of mailing from the Post Office, or by other evidence such as the tenant's acknowledgment. A lease can't add a condition that takes away the refund, because the Act's rights can't be waived. Asking for a forwarding address is still sensible (`security-deposit-return-gu` does), and the abandoned-property rule uses the tenant's forwarding or designated address. Two tenant acts do matter: unreturned keys or items furnished by you may be charged to the deposit, and if the tenant abandons the unit, the agreement ends when a new tenancy begins or, if you don't make reasonable efforts to re-rent or you accept the abandonment as a surrender, on the date you had notice of the abandonment, which starts the 14 working days. Working days exclude weekends and federal and Guam government holidays.

title: Deposits After a Safe Housing Act Termination in Guam
bodyText: Guam's Safe Housing Act lets a tenant who is a victim of family violence, criminal sexual conduct or stalking end the lease and vacate, out of fear of imminent danger to the tenant or the tenant's children because of that violence, after written notice with the evidence the Act lists (a police report or a professional's statement from the prior 30 working days, or a valid restraining or protective order). The tenant then owes one month's rent following vacating, due within 90 working days, plus anything already owed before the notice, and is otherwise released. The Act sets no special deposit timetable, so the ordinary rule applies: within 14 working days after the agreement ends for that tenant, give the itemized notice and any balance. The victim's liability for damage related to the violence is capped at the deposit if the alleged perpetrator is a tenant and the victim gives written notice and the documentation within 30 working days of the damage. The Act doesn't release co-tenants, and it doesn't say when the deposit must be accounted for if other tenants stay; no Guam case on that was searched, so the cautious course is to account to the departing victim for that tenant's share and hold the rest for the continuing tenancy. Don't disclose the victim's information without written consent or a legal requirement. These protections can't be waived or modified by the lease. Working days exclude weekends and federal and Guam government holidays.

title: No Expedited Deposit Procedure in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library sets an expedited or alternative deposit procedure: no quicker refund in exchange for waiving the itemized statement, no fee for faster processing, and no separate track for evictions or abandonment. One rule applies however the tenancy ends: within 14 working days after the rental agreement ends, give the tenant written reasons for anything kept, with costs itemized and receipts (or estimates if repairs can't be done within 14 working days), and the balance. You may always return the deposit sooner. Don't deduct a processing, administrative or accounting fee: the deposit may be used only for the purposes the Act lists (tenant damage from failure to comply with the Act, unpaid rent, unreturned keys or items, cleaning back to the move-in condition less normal wear and tear, and damages from wrongfully quitting). A lease term asking the tenant to give up the itemized statement or accept a flat deduction would waive Rental Act rights, which a lease can't do. A tenant who disputes your accounting may sue within one year; wrongful and willful retention can cost three times the amount withheld plus costs. Working days exclude weekends and federal and Guam government holidays.

title: Fees in Lieu of a Security Deposit in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library addresses deposit-alternative programs (a monthly or one-time fee, or a surety product, in place of a security deposit), and none requires you to let the tenant switch to a regular deposit or to give notice before reporting a damage claim to a collector. Guam's deposit rules limit how such a program could work. At the start of the lease you may collect only the first month's rent and the deposit, so a one-time, non-refundable deposit-alternative fee can't be taken then. A recurring fee charged after the start is rent under the Rental Act, must be stated in the lease, and, like other fees, is best left out of a nonpayment notice (`edu-fees-as-rent-gu`). And any money held against damage or unpaid rent, whatever it is called, is a security deposit, subject to the one-month cap and the 14-working-day accounting. If a third-party product is insurance, Guam's insurance laws govern who may sell it. Because of these limits, the library offers no fee-in-lieu clause for Guam; a landlord who wants one should take advice. Working days exclude weekends and federal and Guam government holidays.

title: Furnished Rentals in Guam
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a furniture inventory, and the Rental Act has no special rules for furnished units.

One older section of Guam's Civil Code reaches a furnished apartment house keeper (and furnished bungalow court and mobile home keepers): liability for loss of or injury to a tenant's or guest's personal property is that of a depositary for hire, capped at small listed sums unless the keeper agrees in writing to more; whether an ordinary furnished house or unit counts was not settled.

A few general rules also apply. Furnishings you promise in the lease become part of the rental agreement, so the tenant has the Rental Act's remedies if you fail to provide or maintain them as agreed (`furnishings-included-la`, tagged for Guam, lists them). The security deposit may cover a tenant's failure to return keys or other items you furnished, and normal wear and tear never includes items missing from the unit, so a signed list of furnishings and their condition at move-in is the best evidence at move-out (`move-in-condition-report-gu`). Wear from ordinary use is not chargeable.

Furnished rentals for stays of less than 90 consecutive days in a hotel, lodging house, bed and breakfast or similar facility are subject to Guam's hotel occupancy tax (11%, or 4% for a registered bed and breakfast), and short-term vacation rentals need their own certificate; an ordinary residential lease is not affected.

title: Holding Deposits Before a Guam Lease Is Signed
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library addresses holding deposits, reservation fees or earnest money taken before a residential lease is signed. Several Guam rules shape one. The start-of-lease limit lets you collect only the first month's rent and the security deposit (with any pet deposit) at commencement; money taken earlier is outside its words, but the cautious course is to credit a holding deposit in full toward the first month's rent or the deposit when the lease starts, so that you never hold more than those amounts once it begins. If the applicant backs out, keeping the whole holding deposit as forfeit fixes in advance what a breach costs, which Guam's contract code makes void unless actual damage would be impracticable or extremely difficult to fix; keep only a loss you can show (such as rent lost while the unit was held), and say so in writing when you take the money. If you back out or the unit isn't available, return it promptly: Guam's consumer-protection law forbids retaining deposits without delivering what was promised after a written demand for a refund, and failing to apply a consumer's deposit against the price (whether that law reaches a residential lease is unsettled, so follow it as the cautious course). A real estate broker who takes the money must hold it in a trust account. Treat every applicant the same way; from October 1, 2026, that includes applicants who pay with housing assistance.

title: No Inspection-Notice Penalty in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a move-in or move-out inspection, so none sets a penalty for skipping an inspection or an inspection notice. The consequences that matter come from the deposit rules. If you keep any part of the deposit, you must give written reasons, with costs itemized and receipts (or estimates, if the repairs can't be done within 14 working days), within 14 working days after the lease ends. If a court finds you kept money wrongfully, it must award the tenant that amount plus costs; if wrongfully and willfully, it may award three times that amount plus costs; and if you were entitled to keep it, it awards you the disputed amount plus costs. The practical penalty for not documenting the unit's condition is therefore evidentiary: without a move-in record and photographs you may be unable to prove that the condition at move-out is worse than at move-in, less normal wear and tear (`edu-condition-inspection-gu`). If you want to inspect before move-out, the Rental Act's entry rules apply: at least 24 hours' notice and entry at reasonable times (`edu-landlord-entry-gu`). Working days exclude weekends and federal and Guam government holidays.

title: No Nonrefundable Deposits in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library creates a category of nonrefundable deposit or a notice rule for one. A security deposit is money the tenant gives you to be held for the purposes the Rental Act lists (unpaid rent, damage from the tenant's failure to comply, unreturned keys or items, cleaning back to the move-in condition less normal wear and tear, and damage from wrongfully quitting), and whatever isn't properly kept for those purposes must be returned within 14 working days after the lease ends, with an itemized statement. So don't call any part of a deposit or pet deposit nonrefundable. A nonrefundable fee is a different thing, and Guam limits it too: at the start of the lease you may collect only the first month's rent and the deposit (with any pet deposit), so a nonrefundable move-in, cleaning, administrative, key or pet fee can't be collected then (`edu-move-in-money-gu`; the library doesn't tag `nonrefundable-fees-wv` for Guam). A fee for a service actually provided later in the tenancy, stated in the lease, is rent and is not a deposit. A pre-lease application fee is outside the start-of-lease limit (`edu-application-fees-gu`). Working days exclude weekends and federal and Guam government holidays.

title: No Separate Notice Rule for Nonrefundable Deposits in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a separate written notice when part of a deposit or fee is nonrefundable. That is because no part of a Guam security deposit can be made nonrefundable: it is held for the tenant, may be used only for the purposes the Rental Act lists, and the rest must be returned within 14 working days after the lease ends with an itemized statement; and a nonrefundable fee can't be collected at the start of the lease, when only the first month's rent and the deposit may be taken. See `edu-no-nonrefundable-deposit-gu`. If you charge a fee later in the tenancy for a service you actually provide, state it in the lease (`fees-and-charges-gu`). Working days exclude weekends and federal and Guam government holidays.

title: Holding a Security Deposit in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a landlord to keep tenants' security deposits in a separate, escrow or interest-bearing account, to tell the tenant where the deposit is held, or to post a bond. The deposit is still the tenant's money held for the purposes the Rental Act lists, and you must account for it within 14 working days after the lease ends, so keep it identifiable and available; if you sell the property, you stay liable for the deposit unless the buyer is credited with it and all parties are notified (`edu-security-deposit-on-sale-gu`). If a real estate broker or property manager collects deposits for you, Guam's licensing law requires the broker to keep a separate trust account in Guam for all trust funds received on behalf of a principal or any other person, to tell the Real Estate Commissioner where it is, and not to commingle those funds, with a $100 penalty for each violation. Guam has no rule on who keeps interest earned on a deposit (`edu-no-deposit-interest-gu`). Working days exclude weekends and federal and Guam government holidays.

title: No Interest Required on Security Deposits in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a landlord to pay interest on a residential security deposit, to hold it in an interest-bearing account, or to report deposit interest, and it sets no rate. If the deposit earns interest in your account, no Guam statute says who keeps it; the lease may say. A Guam Housing Corporation rule lists interest earned from tenant security deposits among possible sources for the Housing Trust Fund, but only as the Legislature approves, and no Guam statute in the corpus directs landlords to pay such interest to the Fund. Guam's legal rate of interest (6% a year) applies to money owed after a demand, so a deposit balance you fail to return when due could carry interest once the tenant demands it, in addition to the deposit remedies (three times the amount for wrongful and willful retention). If you hold deposits through a broker, the broker's trust-account rules apply (`edu-security-deposit-holding-gu`).

title: Deposit Rights Can't Be Waived in Guam
bodyText: A Guam lease may not provide that the tenant waives or gives up any right or remedy under the Rental Act, and a provision the Act prohibits is unenforceable. That covers every deposit rule: the one-month cap and the $500-per-pet limit, the start-of-lease limit, the 14-working-day itemized accounting with receipts, the one-year period to sue, the court's power to award the deposit (or three times the amount wrongfully and willfully kept) plus costs, and the rule that the deposit may not be used as last month's rent without your written agreement. So don't include terms such as a nonrefundable deposit, a flat deduction regardless of actual cost, forfeiture of the deposit for leaving early, a waiver of the itemized statement, or a shorter time to claim it. If the lease has such a term, it is unenforceable, but the rest of the lease stands (`severability`).
