The Safe Housing Act's deposit protections for victims of family violence, criminal sexual conduct or stalking, and the source-of-income rules in effect from October 1, 2026, are separately non-waivable. Working days exclude weekends and federal and Guam government holidays.

title: Security Deposits When a Guam Rental Is Sold
bodyText: When you sell a rented dwelling, Guam's Rental Act relieves you of liability under the lease and the Act only after you give the tenant written notice of a good-faith sale to a bona fide purchaser. Even then, you stay liable for the recoverable security deposit unless the buyer is credited with the deposit and all parties (you, the buyer and the tenant) are notified; from then on the buyer is liable for the deposit and any refund. So at closing, credit the buyer with each tenant's deposit (and any pet deposit), and send each tenant a written notice, delivered personally or by registered or certified mail, naming the buyer and stating the amount transferred; keep proof of delivery. A buyer should insist on the credit and a tenant estoppel letter confirming the deposit. A property manager is relieved of liability after written notice to the tenant that its management has ended, unless otherwise agreed; that doesn't move the deposit. If you are buying, remember that without the credit and notice the seller remains liable, but you will hold the tenancy and should account for the deposit at move-out to avoid a dispute.

title: Penalties for Mishandling a Security Deposit in Guam
bodyText:
Guam has no automatic deposit forfeiture: no provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library says you lose the right to keep any part of the deposit because the written notice or refund was late or incomplete.

The consequences come through a lawsuit, which either you or the tenant may bring.
- If the court finds you wrongfully and willfully kept all or part of the deposit, it may award the tenant three times the amount wrongfully and willfully kept, plus the cost of the suit.
- If you kept it wrongfully but not willfully, the court must award the tenant the amount wrongfully kept plus costs.
- If you were entitled to keep it, the court must award you the disputed amount plus costs.

The tenant must sue within one year after the rental agreement ends. The Small Claims Division hears landlord-tenant disputes, for claims of $10,000 or less.

Missing the 14-working-day deadline (weekends and federal and Guam government holidays excluded), or keeping money without itemized costs and copies of receipts, makes a finding of wrongful, and possibly willful, retention more likely.

If you sell the property, you stay liable for the deposit unless the buyer is credited with it and everyone is notified. Any attorney's-fee clause in your lease works both ways in Guam. Send the notice and any refund on time, keep the Post Office proof of mailing, and keep the receipts.

title: No Deposit-Standards Posting Rule in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations or the court rules searched for this library requires you to post or hand out the standards you use to set deposit amounts, even if different tenants pay different deposits, and Guam has no rule on holding the deposit in a separate or interest-bearing account. Three limits still apply. The security deposit may not be more than one month's rent, plus a separate reasonable pet deposit of no more than $500 per pet. Guam's housing-discrimination law makes it unlawful to discriminate in the terms or conditions of a rental offered on the open market (through a broker or any advertising, signs included), which reaches different deposits based on race, color, religion, sex or national origin (with narrow exemptions, such as an owner of no more than three single-family houses renting without a broker, or an owner-occupied building of up to four units). And since October 1, 2026, you may not set different rental terms because of a tenant's lawful source of income, such as housing assistance. Federal fair-housing law also applies. Base any difference in deposits on written, neutral criteria and apply them the same way to every applicant.

title: What a Security Deposit May Be Used For in Guam
bodyText:
Guam defines a security deposit by what it is held for:
- to remedy the tenant's defaults for accidental or intentional damage from failing to meet the tenant's duties under Guam's Rental Act, for unpaid rent, or for keys or other items you furnished and the tenant didn't return;
- to clean the unit at the end so it is as fit as when the tenant moved in, less normal wear and tear;
- and to cover your damages if the tenant wrongfully quits.

Rent in Guam means all payments due to you under the lease, so unpaid lease charges count as unpaid rent. Normal wear and tear is deterioration from ordinary, reasonable use, but missing items are not wear and tear. The library's Guam deposit clause (`security-deposit-use-gu`) lists only those three purposes.

Don't pre-set flat cleaning, carpet or repair charges to take from the deposit: Guam requires itemized costs with copies of receipts (or estimates if the work can't be done within 14 working days, weekends and federal and Guam government holidays excluded), and a sum fixed in advance as damages for a breach is void unless actual damage would be impracticable or extremely difficult to fix.

The tenant may not use the deposit as last month's rent unless you agree in writing, and you can still recover damage the deposit doesn't cover. A pet deposit is separate (up to $500 per pet).

title: Utility Deposits in Guam
bodyText: Guam has no separate category of utility deposit held by a landlord. Money you hold to secure utility charges the tenant owes you under the lease is part of the security deposit, because Guam counts every payment due to you under the lease as rent: it counts toward the one-month cap, can't be collected on top of the first month's rent and deposit at the start of the lease, and is returned or itemized within 14 working days (weekends and federal and Guam government holidays excluded) under the deposit-return rules (`security-deposit-return-gu`). Deposits a utility takes from the tenant are between the tenant and the utility. Guam's public-utility rules let a utility require a deposit of up to two estimated monthly bills in set cases (for example, no established credit), and require refund with accrued interest within 30 days after service ends or credit is established, less unpaid bills. Guam Power Authority's rules cap a residential deposit at one and one-half times the estimated monthly bill and pay 5% interest; Guam Waterworks Authority's rules refund the balance of its service deposit, after unpaid bills, without interest. These rules were read as compiled; check the utility's current rules and rate schedule.

title: Alterations and Fixtures in Guam
bodyText:
No Guam statute stops you from requiring your written consent before a tenant alters, improves or installs anything; Guam uses the shared Alterations clause (`no-alterations`) and, if you want one, the improvements-ownership clause (`improvements-ownership-la`).

Know the default rules the lease is written against. Something a person attaches to your land without an agreement letting them remove it belongs to you, unless you choose to require its removal. But a tenant may remove, during the term, anything attached for trade, manufacture, ornament or domestic use if it can be removed without injuring the premises and hasn't become an integral part of them, so say in the lease what happens to installations. A tenant must not deliberately or negligently damage or remove any part of the premises, and may not do repairs without your express written consent.

The tenant may not unreasonably refuse you entry to make agreed alterations or improvements, on at least 24 hours' notice. Larger work must meet Guam's building law; minor non-structural work by an owner or lessee themselves (painting, drywall repair, interior walls) may be done without applying to the building official.

Guam's disability-access law doesn't require you to modify your property, but federal fair-housing law requires you to allow reasonable modifications for a tenant with a disability, at the tenant's expense, and you may condition some on restoration. For contractor liens from tenant work, see `edu-construction-liens-gu`.

title: Bed Bugs and Pests in Guam
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations or the court rules searched for this library deals with bed bugs, or sets inspection or treatment deadlines, a cost rule or a tenant's duty to cooperate with treatment.

The general rules apply. You must keep the premises fit and habitable and comply with building and housing codes on health and safety. The tenant must keep the unit as clean and safe as the premises permit, dispose of garbage cleanly and safely, and not damage the premises.

Guam's rodent-control law requires every owner, lessee or occupant of an occupied building to take adequate measures in good faith to eradicate rodents and to keep the property free of food, garbage and rubbish that could harbor them. The tenant may not unreasonably refuse entry to inspect or make repairs, and you must give at least 24 hours' notice except in an emergency or where impracticable.

Use a licensed pest control operator for structural treatment. Guam uses the library's optional pest clause (`pest-cooperation-pr`), which adds prompt reporting, preparation instructions and fault-based cost terms, and sends entry through the lease's entry section (`landlords-access-mi`, with Guam's 24 hours' notice).

title: Carpet Cleaning at Move-Out in Guam
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library addresses professional carpet cleaning at move-out: nothing requires it and nothing forbids a lease term about it.

What Guam does allow is using the security deposit to clean the unit, or have it cleaned, when the lease ends so it is as fit as when the tenant moved in, less normal wear and tear. Any cleaning deduction must be itemized in your written notice with copies of receipts, within 14 working days after the lease ends (weekends and federal and Guam government holidays excluded).

So don't charge a flat carpet-cleaning fee whatever the carpets' condition or cost, and don't collect a cleaning fee at the start of the lease: at commencement you may collect only the first month's rent and the security deposit.

If you want a carpet term, use the optional `carpet-cleaning-gu` clause, and only if the carpets were professionally cleaned right before the tenancy began. Record the carpets' condition at move-in.

title: Cold-Weather Vacating Notice: Not Applicable in Guam
bodyText: Guam has a tropical climate with no freezing season, and no Guam law requires a tenant to warn you before leaving a unit vacant in cold weather, so this topic does not apply. If you want to know when a tenant will be away, Guam lets the lease require notice of an anticipated absence of more than seven working days (weekends and federal and Guam government holidays excluded); see `extended-absence-notice-gu`. The seasonal risk in Guam is typhoons, not freezing: see `edu-disaster-duties-gu` and `casualty-termination-gu`.

title: Contractor Liens for a Tenant's Work in Guam
bodyText:
Guam's mechanics' lien law gives contractors, suppliers and workers a lien on real property for the value of labor or materials for a work of improvement, and treats every contractor in charge of the work as the owner's agent.

But your interest as owner is protected when your tenant orders the work: no owner's interest is subject to a lien based on work contracted for by a person holding an estate under that owner, and that person isn't your agent, where the lease was negotiated at arm's length on commercially reasonable terms (or runs at least 30 years). A lien then attaches only to the interest of the person for whose benefit the work was done.

An ordinary market-rate residential lease should meet the arm's-length test, but whether a particular lease does turns on its facts; a below-market lease to a relative or employee may not.

Most lien claimants must also give the owner a written preliminary notice within 20 days of first furnishing work or materials. If you get one for work your tenant ordered, act on it.

Guam uses the optional shared clause `no-liens-ar`, which makes the tenant pay for work the tenant orders, keep liens off the property and tell contractors the tenant is responsible.

title: Disturbing Neighbors in Guam
bodyText:
Guam law itself makes the tenant conduct himself, and require his guests and invitees to conduct themselves, so as not to disturb neighbors or other tenants, so the shared Disturbance clause (`no-disturbance`) restates a duty the tenant already has.

Separately, making unreasonable noise with intent to cause public inconvenience, annoyance or alarm, or recklessly risking it, is disorderly conduct under Guam's criminal code, and apartment houses and neighborhoods count as public places for that offense.

To end a lease over a disturbance, give written notice specifying the breach; the lease can end no earlier than five working days after the tenant receives it (weekends and federal and Guam government holidays excluded), and not at all if the tenant remedies a remediable breach in time. The eviction chapter separately requires a three-day written notice to perform or quit before an unlawful-detainer case, so a single notice should satisfy both (`default-by-tenant-gu`).

Don't evict a tenant who is a victim of family violence, criminal sexual conduct or stalking because of incidents of that violence; you may still proceed against the tenant who committed it.

title: Recording Move-In Condition in Guam
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a move-in checklist, condition report or inventory, or lets a tenant's signature on one waive your duties.

But the move-in condition matters: the security deposit may be used at the end to clean the unit so it is as fit as when the tenant took possession, less normal wear and tear, and missing items are not wear and tear. Without a record of that starting condition, it is hard to prove what the tenant must restore.

Guam uses the library's Existing Condition clause in the version that records the condition in a signed move-in report plus any defects the tenant reports in writing soon after moving in (`existing-condition-pr`); the shorter shared version, which has the tenant acknowledge the property is "in good order and repair", isn't used.

A condition acknowledgment can't waive your duty to keep the premises fit and habitable or any other right the tenant has under Guam's Rental Act. Walk the unit with the tenant, take dated photos, and give the tenant a copy of the signed report.

title: Family Child Care in a Guam Rental
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library gives a tenant the right to run a family child care home in a rental, or limits a lease term restricting it, so the lease's residential-use and business-use terms control (`residential-use-only`, `edu-home-business-gu`). If you allow it, the tenant must be licensed: Guam treats any person or place that regularly cares for one or more children not related to the caregiver, for pay or not, as a child care facility, including family day care homes, and no one may operate one without a Department of Public Health and Social Services license (with exceptions such as care by an occasional relative or parents trading care). Before licensing, the applicant must certify compliance with health, safety, fire, building and sanitation rules. A home used as a child care facility also loses the private-residence exemption from Guam's smoking law. If you agree to child care, put the permission, licence, insurance and any conditions in writing.

title: Home Businesses in a Guam Rental
bodyText:
Guam's Family Home Occupation Act, part of the zoning law, makes a family home occupation an accessory use of a residential dwelling in any zone without a use variance, if it causes no consternation to the neighbors, employs only family members living there, shows no outside sign of the business, adds no more traffic, noise, fumes or waste than normal residential use, and involves nothing illegal.

That is a zoning permission; it does not give a tenant a right to run a business against the lease. No Guam statute stops a lease from requiring your written consent for a home business, and a property used for a purpose other than the one it was let for exposes the tenant to damages or rescission.

In a condominium or other property regime, the regime's documents and rules may limit or ban home occupations, and a condominium tenant is bound by the declaration and bylaws.

A tenant who does business at home still needs a Guam business licence; a home industry licence covers small home manufacturing (handicrafts, food and similar items, up to $100,000 a year) using only family members.

If you allow a home business, say so in writing and list any conditions. Child care in the home has its own licensing (`edu-no-family-child-care-rule-gu`).

title: Joint Liability of Co-Tenants in Guam
bodyText:
Guam presumes an obligation imposed on several people is joint, not several, except in special cases, and one of those covers most leases: where everyone who joins in a promise receives some benefit from it, or a promise worded in the singular ("Tenant will pay") is signed by several people, the promise is presumed joint and several, so each co-tenant can be liable for the whole.

To avoid any argument, the lease should still say so, as the shared Joint and Several Liability clause does (`joint-liability`); apart from the Safe Housing Act's limits below, no Guam provision searched for this library limits that term.

Performance by one joint debtor extinguishes the liability of all, and a co-tenant who pays more than his share may require a proportionate contribution from the others.

No Guam statute says that accepting one co-tenant's share of the rent waives joint liability for the rest; to avoid an argument, state in the lease (as the shared clause does) that rent is due in full however the tenants divide it, and don't give receipts that describe a payment as one tenant's share in full.

If one co-tenant ends the lease as a victim of family violence, criminal sexual conduct or stalking under Guam's Safe Housing Act, that tenant owes one month's rent after vacating, but the other tenants stay bound by the lease; and where the person who committed the violence is a tenant, a victim who gives written notice of the damage, with the Act's documentation, within 30 working days after the damage occurs isn't liable for damage related to the violence beyond the security deposit.

title: Yard Care and Irrigation in Guam
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library assigns lawn, yard or irrigation care to landlord or tenant, so the lease decides.

Guam uses the shared Landscaping and Irrigation clause (`landscaping-irrigation`). Where yard work overlaps your duty to keep the premises fit and habitable, you and the tenant may agree that the tenant does it, but only in good faith; Guam has no separate-writing or single-family rule (`tenant-repair-agreement-gu`).

Guam's rodent-control law requires the owner, lessee or occupant of an occupied building to keep weeds and grass around it, including the strip between the property line and the road, maintained so they don't harbor or breed rodents, so make clear in the lease who does this.

When the Governor declares a state of emergency for a disaster threatening the public water supply, using Guam Waterworks Authority water to irrigate lawns, plants or shrubs is an unauthorized use punishable by a fine of $1,000 to $25,000; the tenant's watering duty should give way to such an order. Irrigation systems on GWA water need backflow prevention under GWA's rules.

title: No Utility Lien for a Tenant's Unpaid Bill in Guam
bodyText: Guam has no cities or counties; water, sewer and power are supplied island-wide by the Guam Waterworks Authority and the Guam Power Authority. No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations or the court rules searched for this library makes a tenant's unpaid water, sewer, power or garbage bill a lien on your property, or makes you, as owner, liable for a bill in the tenant's own name. The utility liens that do exist are different: unpaid installments under a Guam Waterworks sewer-connection contract with a homeowner are a lien on that property, and the cost of sewage-facility work the government does after an owner ignores an order is entered on the real property tax roll as a lien. Garbage is the exception to keep in mind: since 2025 every owner of a residential building must subscribe to and pay for garbage collection, and a tenant paying on your behalf doesn't change that, unless a building of four units or less qualifies for an exemption because the lease obligates the tenant to subscribe (see `garbage-subscription-gu` and `edu-utilities-responsibility-gu`). The reverse is protected too: when the water account is yours, GWA may not collect your arrears from the tenant. Keep utility accounts in the tenant's name where the tenant pays, and ask for proof of payment (`utility-payment-evidence`).

title: Occupancy Limits in Guam
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library sets a maximum number of occupants for a private residential rental or gives neighbors a right to enforce one.

Guam's old Housing Code was repealed in 2010; construction is governed by the adopted International Building and Residential Codes (2009 editions, as amended), and the International Property Maintenance Code will apply only to hotel-zoned properties (the law takes effect June 3, 2027, and the Department of Public Works must still adopt the code).

So the lease sets who may live there; Guam uses the shared Permitted Occupants clause (`permitted-occupants`).

Keep any limit reasonable and apply it evenly: Guam's housing-discrimination law forbids different terms based on race, color, religion, sex or national origin, and federal fair-housing law protects families with children, so a limit stricter than needed can be challenged.

A person who rents part of a room as a dwelling is entitled to the whole room despite any agreement to the contrary, and letting one room to more than one family relieves every tenant in the building of rent while it continues (`edu-double-letting-gu`).

No Guam statute lets a household member take over a lease when the tenant dies; a fixed-term lease isn't ended by a party's death, but a hiring terminable at will ends on notice of the death.

title: Tenant's Statutory Prohibitions in Guam
bodyText:
Guam's Rental Act binds the tenant directly, whether or not the lease repeats it.

The tenant must keep the unit and the premises he uses as clean and safe as the premises permit, dispose of garbage cleanly and safely, not deliberately or negligently destroy, deface, damage or remove any part of the premises or let anyone else do so, use power, water and common areas reasonably, and not disturb neighbors or other tenants, nor let guests do so.

The tenant may not unreasonably refuse consent to your entry to inspect, repair, supply agreed services or show the unit. If the tenant refuses lawful access, you may seek a court order or end the lease and recover actual damages, costs, lost rent and reasonable attorney's fees.

A tenant for years who commits waste may be liable for treble damages.

Guam uses the shared Prohibited Acts clause (`prohibited-acts-renter-wy`). Enforce a breach with the written notices described in `edu-cure-and-eviction-grounds-gu`; don't treat a victim's family-violence incident as the tenant's breach.

title: Residential Use Only in Guam
bodyText:
Guam law backs a residential-use term: when property is let for a particular purpose, the tenant must not use it for any other purpose, and if he does, he is liable for all damages resulting from that use, or you may treat the lease as rescinded.

You may also end the hiring before the term ends if the tenant uses the property, or lets it be used, contrary to the lease. In practice, give the written breach notices described in `edu-cure-and-eviction-grounds-gu` before going to court.

Guam uses the shared Residential Use clause (`residential-use-only`).

Two Guam rules make it worth enforcing: renting all or part of a dwelling to transient guests for stays of 30 consecutive days or less is a short-term vacation rental that needs a certificate from the Department of Revenue and Taxation, and an owner whose property is advertised as a lodging facility without proper licences faces a $5,000 fine; if a tenant or other operator runs it, the operator is fined first and you get a notice of illegal operation, and if the operator is caught again within a year you face $5,000 for every day it kept operating.

Family home occupations are a zoning matter (`edu-home-business-gu`).

title: Smoking and Vaping Rules in Guam Rentals
bodyText:
Guam's smoke-free law, the Natasha Protection Act, bans smoking (including electronic smoking devices) in enclosed public places, but private residences are not regulated unless used as a child care or health care facility, so smoking inside a rental is left to the lease.

A person who controls an establishment or area where smoking is not, or only partly, regulated may prohibit it throughout.

Guam's cannabis law also lets anyone who occupies, owns or controls private property prohibit or regulate the possession, use, consumption or growing of cannabis there, and gives medical-cannabis patients no right to cultivate if the landlord prohibits it.

No Guam law protects a tenant's cannabis use in a rental, so the shared Smoking Policy clause (`smoking-policy`), which bans tobacco, marijuana and vaping everywhere on the property, needs no narrowing.

Cannabis smoke or odor that drifts onto another person's real property is a nuisance under Guam law, and consuming cannabis openly in public is unlawful; Guam's cannabis rules count common areas of apartment buildings as public places.

Put a smoking ban in the lease at signing. A ban added during the tenancy as a rule binds the tenant without consent only if it meets Guam's four rule criteria, including 30 working days' prior notice (`rules-gu`).

title: Subletting and Assignment in Guam
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires you to consent to a sublease or assignment or limits the reasons for refusing, so a lease may require your prior written consent in your sole discretion, as the shared Sublet and Assignment clause does (`no-sublet-assign`).

Guam's eviction chapter gives that clause teeth: a tenant or subtenant who assigns or sublets contrary to the lease thereby terminates it, and after five days' notice to quit served on the persons in possession, you are entitled to restitution of possession.

Breach of a covenant not to assign or sublet is also a ground for the three-day notice to perform or quit, and Guam's Rental Act has its own written breach notice; a single notice should satisfy both (`default-by-tenant-gu`).

If you consent to an assignment, the assignee becomes answerable to you for breaches while he holds the lease, and the lease should say the original tenant stays liable.

Short-term subletting matters in Guam: renting a dwelling to transient guests for 30 consecutive days or less needs a short-term vacation rental certificate, and if a tenant runs one, you get a notice of illegal operation and, if the tenant is caught again within a year, can be fined $5,000 for every day it kept operating.

Don't refuse a proposed subtenant because of race, color, religion, ancestry, national origin, sex, place of birth or, since October 1, 2026, lawful source of income.

title: Forwarding Notices of Proceedings in Guam
bodyText:
Guam law requires every tenant who receives notice of a proceeding to recover the property, or its possession, to tell you immediately and to deliver the notice to you if it is in writing. A tenant who doesn't is responsible to you for all damages you suffer because of that omission.

The duty applies whether or not the lease repeats it, and Guam uses the shared clause that restates it (`tenant-forward-proceedings-ca`).

A related rule protects your title: a tenant's attornment to a stranger, that is, agreeing to hold the property under someone else, is void unless you consent or a court judgment requires it.

Both rules are in Guam's older hiring-of-real-property chapter, which applies to residential leases except where the Rental Act conflicts; nothing in the Act conflicts with them.

title: Tenant's Insurance and Insurance Claims in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library says whether you may require a tenant to carry renter's insurance, to make a claim on the tenant's own policy, or to name you on it, and none governs subrogation between you and the tenant. The lease controls, within limits. A contract term that exempts anyone from responsibility for his own fraud, willful injury to another's person or property, or violation of law, willful or negligent, is against Guam's public policy, and a lease may not waive the tenant's rights under the Rental Act, including your duty to keep the premises fit and habitable. So don't use a tenant's policy as the first source for repairs that are yours to make, or for damage you or your agents caused. You may recover from the tenant damage the tenant, the tenant's family or guests deliberately or negligently cause (`tenant-caused-damage-gu`); whether the tenant claims that on its own policy is between the tenant and the insurer. Guam uses the library's renter's-insurance clause without a liability disclaimer (`tenants-property-insurance-ks-oh-ca`).

title: Tenant's Upkeep Duties in Guam
bodyText:
Guam's Rental Act makes the tenant keep the unit and the premises he uses as clean and safe as the premises permit, dispose of garbage cleanly and safely, not damage the premises, use utilities and common areas reasonably, and report, as soon as practicable, defects he has reason to believe you don't know about and are yours to repair.

Guam's general hiring law adds that a tenant must use ordinary care to preserve the property and repair damage caused by his own want of ordinary care.

Guam uses the shared Tenant Maintenance clause (`tenant-maintenance`).

Repairs and upkeep that are your duty may be shifted to the tenant only by a good-faith agreement (`tenant-repair-agreement-gu`), and a tenant may not repair and deduct without your written consent, except for essential services you willfully or negligently fail to supply, after written notice and not where the tenant's side caused the problem (21 GCA § 48304), and windstorm damage to the weatherhead that you don't begin, or make a good-faith effort to begin, repairing within 10 working days after you become aware of it, with repairs by a master and licensed electrician, an itemized invoice and deductions spread over no more than three months, subject to the exclusions in 21 GCA § 48307(c) (21 GCA § 48307).

Septic and sewage systems: you as owner are responsible for the structural integrity, repair and replacement of toilet and sewage facilities, while the lessee or occupant keeps them clean and sanitary.

Guam EPA rules make maintenance of septic tanks and leaching fields the responsibility of the owner, lessee, occupant or person in possession, and owners must pump the tank when necessary, so say in the lease who arranges pumping.

If the tenant's breach of these duties materially affects health and safety and can be remedied by repair or replacement of a damaged item, and the tenant doesn't remedy it as promptly as conditions require in an emergency or within five working days after your written notice specifying the breach and asking for the remedy, you may enter and have the work done in a workmanlike manner after that notice (weekends and federal and Guam government holidays excluded) and bill the cost as rent (`tenant-caused-damage-gu`).

title: Tenant's Statutory Duties in Guam
bodyText:
Guam law sets these tenant duties whatever the lease says.

Under the Rental Act the tenant must keep the unit and the premises he uses as clean and safe as the premises permit; dispose of garbage, rubbish and other waste cleanly and safely; not deliberately or negligently damage or remove any part of the premises or let anyone else do so; use power, water and common areas reasonably; not disturb neighbors or other tenants, nor let guests do so; report, as soon as practicable, defects he has reason to believe you don't know about and are yours to repair; and not unreasonably refuse you entry for the Act's purposes.

Rent is payable at the agreed time and place without demand.

Guam's older laws add: use ordinary care to preserve the property and repair damage from his own want of care; use it only for the purpose it was let; tell you immediately about any proceeding to recover the property and hand over written notices; keep toilet and sewage facilities clean and sanitary; and, as an occupant, take good-faith measures against rodents.

Details and enforcement are in `edu-prohibited-acts-renter-gu`, `edu-tenant-maintenance-gu`, `edu-disturbance-gu`, `edu-residential-use-only-gu` and `edu-tenant-forward-proceedings-gu`.

title: Who Pays Utilities in Guam
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library bars a lease that makes the tenant arrange and pay utilities directly, so Guam uses the shared Utilities clause (`utilities-responsibility`) with `utility-service-continuity` and `utility-payment-evidence`.

Guam Waterworks Authority asks every applicant to document that he is the owner or tenant of the premises, and the customer who signs up pays for service until he gives notice to stop.

If you keep the water account in your name and fall behind, GWA, where it knows or has reason to know of the tenancy, must, where feasible and after notice, offer the tenant service in the tenant's own name before disconnecting, and may not collect your arrears from the tenant or make the tenant pay them to get service.

GWA's listed grounds for refusing service don't include a former occupant's unpaid bill, but Guam's general utility rules let a utility require a deposit to continue service at premises where a delinquent prior customer still lives, and GWA may refuse service to an applicant who himself owes GWA.

Garbage is different: since August 2025 every owner of a residential building must subscribe to and pay for garbage collection, even if the tenant pays the hauler. An owner of a building of four units or less may petition the Guam Solid Waste Authority, yearly, for an exemption if the lease obligates the tenant to subscribe; the optional `garbage-subscription-gu` clause supplies that lease term.

If you agree to supply running water, electricity, gas or hot water, a willful or negligent failure to supply it lets the tenant, after written notice specifying the breach, use the essential-services remedies (unless the tenant's side caused the condition), and you must never willfully cut off running water, electricity, gas or hot water.

title: Submetered Utilities and Service Interruptions in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library sets a special regime for electricity or water that a landlord submeters and bills to tenants: none sets how you must bill, notify or restore submetered service. Three rules still apply. First, if you supply a utility under the lease and willfully cut it off, or willfully cause an interruption of running water, electricity, gas or hot water, the tenant may recover possession or end the lease and recover actual damages; if you fail to supply it willfully or negligently, the tenant may, after written notice, secure the service and deduct the reasonable cost or obtain substitute housing with rent excused. Second, Guam Waterworks Authority's rules say retail resale of water received by a customer is not permitted unless GWA approves in writing, so check with GWA before charging tenants for submetered water beyond passing through your actual cost. Third, when a utility plans to disconnect service through a master meter, Guam's utility rules make it try to inform the occupants and, if an occupant asks, give at least five days to arrange continued service, so keep the master account current; for water, where GWA knows or has reason to know of the tenancy, it must also, where feasible and after notice, offer the tenant service in the tenant's own name before disconnecting a landlord's account. State in the lease which utilities you supply and how any charge is calculated; a utility charge you collect is rent under Guam's Rental Act.

title: Proof of Utility Payment in Guam
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library limits asking a tenant for reasonable proof that utilities the lease makes the tenant's responsibility have been paid, so Guam uses the shared clause (`utility-payment-evidence`).

It is worth using in Guam because a tenant's unpaid utility bills can complicate service at your property: Guam Waterworks Authority may refuse service to an applicant who owes it money, a utility may require a deposit to keep serving premises where a delinquent prior customer still lives, and garbage collection is the owner's obligation unless an exemption applies (`edu-utilities-responsibility-gu`).

Ask for the bill and receipt, or the utility's account statement, not the tenant's account password. Keep requests reasonable and make them of every tenant alike.

title: Keeping Utilities On in Guam
bodyText:
Guam law already makes the tenant use in a reasonable manner all power, water and other common areas you provide, and no Guam statute limits a lease term requiring the tenant to keep water, electricity, sewer and trash service on during the term, so Guam uses the shared clause (`utility-service-continuity`).

Keeping service on matters in Guam: water left off can let sewage and septic systems fail, which Guam's health laws make the owner fix on short notice, and an occupied residential building must have garbage collection.

After a typhoon, power may stay off until a damaged weatherhead is repaired; Guam's Rental Act gives you 10 working days (weekends and federal and Guam government holidays excluded) after you become aware of damage from winds over 34 knots (40 mph) to start, or make a good-faith effort to start, the repair before the tenant may have a master and licensed electrician repair it and, after giving you an itemized invoice, deduct the reasonable cost from rent (over up to three months if it exceeds one month's rent), except in the cases the statute excludes (`edu-landlord-maintenance-gu`).

For your own duties when you supply a utility, see `edu-utility-interruption-submeter-gu`.

title: Smoke and Carbon Monoxide Alarms in Guam
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a residential landlord to install or maintain smoke or carbon monoxide alarms in a long-term rental, or gives the tenant a duty to maintain them.

The explicit alarm rules reach other uses: bed and breakfast homes must have single-station smoke detectors in every guest bedroom, and care homes must have automatic smoke detectors, fire alarm systems and sprinklers.

Guam has adopted the International Fire Code and the International Building and Residential Codes (2009 editions, as amended), which contain smoke-alarm requirements for buildings, and Guam's Rental Act makes you comply with applicable building and housing codes on health and safety; check with the Guam Fire Department and the Department of Public Works what applies to your building.

Fire code violations carry civil penalties that rise with repeat offenses.

The cautious course: install working smoke alarms in each sleeping area and on each level, a carbon monoxide alarm where there is fuel-burning equipment or an attached garage, test them at move-in, and use the optional detector-care clause (`detector-care-la`) so the tenant reports problems and doesn't disable them.

title: Substitute Housing When Essential Services Fail in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires you to provide or pay for alternate housing while you make repairs, even after a typhoon or fire. The one substitute-housing rule is tenant-triggered: if, contrary to the lease, you willfully or negligently fail to supply essential services (running water, electricity, gas or hot water), the tenant may give you written notice and procure substitute housing while the failure lasts. The tenant is then excused from paying rent for that period, but you are not responsible for the cost of the substitute housing unless both of you agreed to it in writing. The right doesn't apply if the tenant, a member of the tenant's family or others on the premises caused the condition. After a fire or casualty that substantially impairs the unit, the tenant may instead immediately vacate and end the lease by written notice within 14 working days afterwards (weekends and federal and Guam government holidays excluded), or, if continued occupancy is lawful, vacate the unusable part and pay proportionally reduced rent; neither applies to damage the tenant, the tenant's family, guests or invitees caused. A lease may add a written agreement that you will pay for substitute housing; the library doesn't offer one, because it serves the tenant, but it is lawful if you choose it. Government relocation-assistance laws apply only to government acquisitions and GHURA projects.

title: Appliances You Leave but Don't Supply in Guam
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library presumes that every appliance left in a unit is yours to maintain, and none lists appliances you can't exclude.

What you must do is set by Guam's Rental Act and the lease: keep the premises fit and habitable, comply with building and housing codes on health and safety, and supply the essential services the lease promises (running water, electricity, gas, hot water). The tenant's remedies reach your breach of the lease as well as of the Act, so an appliance you list as supplied (`appliances-included`) is one you must keep working.

If you leave an item you won't maintain, such as an old freezer or a tenant-owned washer, list it with the optional `appliances-excluded-gu` clause. Don't exclude equipment that supplies running water, electricity, gas or hot water or that keeps the unit habitable, and never disclaim losses from your own negligence, willful act or violation of law, which Guam treats as against public policy. Record supplied and excluded items at move-in.

title: Appliances You Supply in Guam
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library lists appliances a landlord must supply.

But anything you promise in the lease becomes part of what you must keep up: the tenant's remedies under Guam's Rental Act reach your noncompliance with the lease as well as with the Act's repair and code duties, and if you promise running water, electricity, gas or hot water and willfully or negligently fail to supply it, the tenant may give written notice and secure the service and deduct its reasonable cost, or obtain substitute housing with rent excused.

So list in the lease exactly what you supply and will maintain, using the shared clause (`appliances-included`) and `{{appliance_list}}`, and list separately anything you leave but won't maintain (`appliances-excluded-gu`).

Apart from that essential-services remedy (and weatherhead repairs under 21 GCA § 48307), a tenant may not repair a supplied appliance and deduct the cost without your written consent, and may not withhold rent for a repair you haven't done. If the tenant breaks an appliance through deliberate or negligent conduct, the tenant pays (`tenant-caused-damage-gu`). If you rent under Guam's one-time temporary licence for dwelling units, the home inspection covers electrical, plumbing and HVAC.

title: Common-Area Lighting in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires lighting in the common areas of a rental building, or says whether a tenant may be made to pay for common-area lights wired to the tenant's own electric service. The only lighting rule found is for care homes. General duties still apply: the premises you must keep fit and habitable include the grounds, areas and facilities promised for the tenant's use, and you must comply with applicable building and housing codes on health and safety, including the adopted building and fire codes (texts not in this library's corpus). If any common-area light runs through a tenant's meter, say so in the lease at signing and credit or reimburse the cost, or rewire it to your account; a charge the tenant pays to you or for your benefit under the lease counts as rent in Guam.

title: Rent After an Unsafe-Building Order in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library expressly bars a landlord from collecting rent after a building is declared unsafe or ordered vacated. But Guam's building law declares every unsafe building illegal, including one that is unsanitary or unfit for human habitation: the building official must order it vacated and not reoccupied until a new certificate of occupancy issues, post it, and may order it repaired or demolished, with the cost a lien on the land. It is unlawful to use or occupy a building contrary to that law, and the owner, occupant and lessee all receive the notice. A unit no one may lawfully occupy can't be kept fit and habitable as Guam's Rental Act requires, and the tenant then has the Act's remedies: written notice and termination if you don't remedy the breach, actual damages, and, for fire or casualty damage that substantially impairs enjoyment of the unit (and that the tenant's side didn't cause), the right to vacate immediately and end the lease by written notice within 14 working days, or pay proportionally reduced rent for any part still lawfully occupied. No Guam case deciding whether rent is owed for the period of a vacate order was searched; the cautious course is to stop charging rent from the date a vacate order takes effect until occupancy is lawful again, and to refund any rent paid for that time.

title: Who Makes Repairs in a Guam Rental
bodyText:
Guam gives you more control over who repairs your rental than most places: a tenant may not do repairs, or hire anyone to do them, without your express written consent, may not deduct repair costs from rent unless you approve in writing, and may not withhold rent for repairs you haven't done. Guam's older repair-and-deduct rule gives way to this.

So a lease may name your repair contact and say that any consent you give will name the approved repairer, as the optional `designated-repairer-gu` clause does.

Two tenant self-help rights survive and can't be narrowed by the lease. If you willfully or negligently fail to supply running water, electricity, gas or hot water as the lease requires, the tenant may, after written notice, secure those services and deduct the reasonable cost.

And if you don't start repairing a weatherhead damaged by winds over 34 knots within 10 working days after you become aware of it (weekends and federal and Guam government holidays excluded), the tenant may have a master and licensed electrician repair it and deduct the cost after giving you an itemized invoice.

title: Disability Access and Accommodation in Guam Rentals
bodyText:
Guam's own disability rule for rentals is older and narrower than federal law.

Blind, visually impaired and other physically disabled persons are entitled to full and equal access to all housing accommodations offered for rent in Guam, subject to conditions applying alike to everyone (the rule doesn't cover a single-family home whose occupants rent out no more than one room).

A totally or partially blind person may be accompanied by a trained guide dog without paying an extra charge for it, but is liable for any damage the dog does; Guam's chapter also says a landlord who refuses all tenants with dogs need not accept a blind, visually impaired or other physically disabled tenant with a dog, even a guide dog; that sentence pulls against the guide-dog right, and for housing the federal law covers, the federal accommodation duty below governs in practice.

Interfering with these rights is a misdemeanor. Guam's rule says you don't have to modify your property or give a higher degree of care, and Guam's housing-discrimination law doesn't list disability.

Federal fair-housing law goes further and applies in Guam: you must make reasonable accommodations in rules and services (for example, allowing an assistance animal despite a no-pets rule, without a pet deposit) and allow reasonable modifications at the tenant's expense, and you may condition some modifications on restoration.

Guam's service-animal law points to that federal rule and makes it a misdemeanor to misrepresent an animal as a service animal. No Guam law requires the lease to state your restoration right. Guam uses the shared `assistance-animal-accommodation` clause.

title: Renting Part of a Room (Double Letting) in Guam
bodyText: Guam forbids letting part of a room as a dwelling. A person who rents part of a room to live in is entitled to the whole room, whatever the agreement says. If you let a room as a dwelling for more than one family, the person to whom you first let any part of it is entitled to possession of the whole room for the agreed term, and every tenant in the building who rents from you is relieved of all obligation to pay you rent while the double letting continues. The rule comes from Guam's older hiring-of-real-property chapter and can't be varied by agreement. Nothing in Guam's Rental Act conflicts with it. So don't rent beds or shares of a single room to separate households. Renting separate rooms in one dwelling, each to one household, is a different arrangement, but it may make the house a lodging or boarding use under zoning and licensing rules, and stays of 30 days or less are short-term rentals that need a certificate.

title: Screening Staff Who Enter Units in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires you to run background checks on employees or managers who have access to tenants' units, or sets standards for doing so. A related licensing rule matters: a person who, for another and for compensation, rents or leases real estate, offers to, or negotiates leases is a real estate broker under Guam law and must be licensed, but a resident manager for the owner (or an employee acting as resident manager for a managing broker) who lives on the premises and leases in connection with that employment is exempt. Your entry rules bind anyone you send in: your staff and contractors may enter only on at least 24 hours' notice during reasonable hours (except in an emergency or where impracticable), and an entry that is unlawful or harassing gives the tenant remedies against you. Screening staff who hold keys is a prudent practice; if you use consumer reports to screen employees, federal consumer-reporting rules apply.

title: How Serious a Repair Problem Must Be in Guam
bodyText: Guam's Rental Act ties each tenant remedy to a threshold, but no provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library lists which conditions count. Your code duty covers building and housing codes relative to health and safety, and your repair duty covers repairs reasonably necessary to keep the premises fit and habitable. The tenant's termination remedy needs either your noncompliance with the lease or noncompliance with those duties affecting health and safety: the tenant gives written notice specifying the breach and a termination date at least 30 working days after you receive it, and the lease doesn't end if you remedy the breach within 14 working days (weekends and federal and Guam government holidays excluded). The tenant may also recover actual damages, and attorney's fees if your noncompliance is willful. Self-help is limited to essential services (running water, electricity, gas, hot water) you willfully or negligently fail to supply, and to weatherheads damaged by winds over 34 knots (40 mph). After a fire or casualty, the tenant's rights turn on whether enjoyment of the unit is substantially impaired. The tenant can't terminate, or use the essential-services remedy, for a condition the tenant, the tenant's family or others on the premises caused, and the casualty rights don't apply to damage caused by the tenant, their family, guests or invitees. Minor or cosmetic defects that don't affect health and safety still matter if the lease promises them, because the lease itself is a remedy trigger.

title: Can a Guam Lease Shift Repair Duties?
bodyText: Guam's Rental Act says a lease may not make the tenant waive or give up any right or remedy under the Act, and a prohibited lease provision is unenforceable. But the Act itself lets you and the tenant agree that the tenant will perform your code-compliance and repair duties (and the defect-reporting duty), only if the agreement is entered in good faith, meaning honestly and objectively with no deliberate intent to defraud. Guam has no separate-writing, single-family or consideration requirement for that agreement, but a specific written term is the safest evidence of good faith (`tenant-repair-agreement-gu`). What you can't do is strip the tenant's remedies: the termination and damages remedies, the essential-services remedy and the weatherhead remedy stay. Guam's older rule that a lessor must make a dwelling habitable "in the absence of an agreement to the contrary" gives way to the Act. Guam has no rule letting a lease waive a water supply where there is no well or public water; if a property relies on catchment or a private well, describe the supply in the lease and keep it working.

title: No Presumption of Repair Breach in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library presumes that you breached a repair or habitability duty, or that you took too long to repair, from a code violation, an agency notice or the passage of time. The tenant must prove the breach. Guam's Rental Act uses fixed periods instead: after the tenant's written notice of a breach affecting health and safety, you have 14 working days to remedy it before the lease can end on a date at least 30 working days after you received the notice; you have 10 working days after becoming aware of wind damage to a weatherhead to start the repair (weekends and federal and Guam government holidays excluded). The tenancy presumptions Guam law does contain are not about repairs: the evidence code presumes earlier rent paid when a receipt for later rent is produced (rebuttable) and bars a tenant from denying your title at the start of the tenancy, and the hiring chapter presumes the term: a dwelling rented for an unspecified term is presumed to be for the rent period (monthly if nothing was agreed), and accepting rent after the term ends presumes renewal on the same terms, for no more than a month when rent is monthly. Keep dated records of repair requests and what you did, because the records, not a presumption, will decide a dispute.

title: No Required Habitability Statement in a Guam Lease
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a residential lease to state that you will deliver the unit fit for habitation or keep it habitable. Your duties apply whatever the lease says: comply with building and housing codes on health and safety, make the repairs reasonably necessary to keep the premises fit and habitable, and deliver possession on the lease's start date, or rent abates and the tenant may end the lease on at least five working days' written notice (weekends and federal and Guam government holidays excluded), with all deposits returned. A lease may restate these duties, and the library's maintenance clauses do; it may not narrow them, because a lease can't waive the tenant's rights or remedies under Guam's Rental Act. The lease statutes Guam does have that prescribe contents are for government programs, such as Guam Housing Corporation lease-to-own contracts and GHURA and Chamorro Land Trust leases, not private rentals; the Horizontal Property Act also lists particulars for deeds or leases of apartments in a condominium regime (21 GCA § 45112), none about habitability.

title: Public Health Rules for Guam Rentals
bodyText: Guam has no health districts, and no provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires you to give a tenant the Department of Public Health and Social Services' rental regulations on request or to refer tenants to a health office. DPHSS's Division of Environmental Health does license and inspect certain kinds of housing, and if your rental is one of them its rules apply directly. Temporary workforce housing (living quarters where at least 51% of residents are temporary workers on Guam for a specific project, such as H-2B worker dormitories) needs a DPHSS sanitary and workers' dormitory permit and is inspected under the Temporary Workforce Housing Regulations. Hotels, motels and dormitories that offer sleeping accommodations to guests for a fee need sanitary permits, and care homes have their own rules. An ordinary long-term rental of a house or apartment needs no health permit, but Guam's public-health laws still reach it: rodent control, toilet and sewage maintenance, septic pumping and mosquito-breeding rules apply to owners and occupants. Code complaints about building condition go to the Department of Public Works' building official.

title: Heating and Cooling in Guam Rentals
bodyText: Guam's tropical climate has no heating season, and no provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a landlord to supply heat or sets a minimum indoor temperature, so heating rules don't apply. No Guam provision found imposes an air-conditioning or cooling duty: the Rental Act defines essential services as 'basic needs such as running water, electricity, gas, or hot water' (21 GCA § 48102(h)), a list that names no cooling, though its "such as" leaves the point open and no Guam case was searched. If the lease says you supply air conditioning or another cooling system, it becomes part of your obligations: the tenant's termination and damages remedies reach your noncompliance with the lease, so maintain what you promise or list the unit as not supplied (`appliances-excluded-gu`). Hot water is an essential service, so a water heater you supply must be kept working; if you willfully or negligently fail to supply it as the lease requires, the tenant may, after written notice, secure it and deduct the reasonable cost or obtain substitute housing with rent excused. Units rented under Guam's one-time temporary licence are inspected for HVAC among other systems.

title: Tenant's Remedies When a Guam Landlord Breaches
bodyText: When you breach the lease or your repair and code duties, a Guam tenant's remedies are set by the Rental Act, and the lease can't waive them. (1) Termination: written notice specifying the breach, ending the lease on a date at least 30 working days after you receive it unless you remedy the breach within 14 working days (or show why the date can't be met). (2) Damages and an injunction, plus reasonable attorney's fees if your noncompliance is willful, and return of the recoverable deposit if the lease ends. (3) Essential services you willfully or negligently fail to supply: after written notice, the tenant may secure them and deduct the reasonable cost, or obtain substitute housing with rent excused. (4) Failure to deliver possession: rent abates, and the tenant may end the lease on five working days' written notice; double damages and fees if willful and not in good faith. (5) Fire or casualty that substantially impairs enjoyment of the unit: vacate immediately and end the lease by written notice within 14 working days, or, if continued occupancy is lawful, vacate the unusable part at proportionally reduced rent. (6) Unlawful ouster or willful interruption of essential services: recover possession or end the lease, plus actual damages. (7) Unlawful or harassing entry: injunction or termination, damages, costs and fees. (8) Weatherhead damaged by winds over 34 knots (40 mph) and not started within 10 working days after you become aware of it: repair by a master and licensed electrician and, after an itemized invoice, deduction from rent over up to three months. What a tenant may not do is repair other items and deduct, or withhold rent for repairs not done, without your written consent. Working days exclude weekends and federal and Guam government holidays. The termination, essential-services and casualty remedies don't apply to conditions the tenant's side caused (each section words the exception differently).

title: Landlord's Repair and Maintenance Duties in Guam
bodyText:
Guam's Rental Act makes you comply with all applicable building and housing codes relative to health and safety and make all repairs reasonably necessary to keep the premises, including the grounds, areas and facilities promised for the tenant's use, fit and habitable.

The tenant must report, as soon as practicable, defects he has reason to believe you don't know about and are yours to repair.

Guam's building law adds that every building must be kept in a safe and sanitary condition, with required safety devices in good working order, and makes the owner or his agent responsible for that maintenance; as owner you also answer for the structure and repair of toilet and sewage facilities.

Guam has no separate housing code (it was repealed in 2010), no statutory list of dangerous conditions and no general repair deadline (but the tenant's termination notice gives you 14 working days to remedy, and building-law orders set their own deadlines); the one fixed start date is the weatherhead rule: after winds over 34 knots (40 mph) damage a weatherhead, start repairs within 10 working days after you become aware of it (weekends and federal and Guam government holidays excluded) or the tenant may have a master and licensed electrician do it and deduct the cost.

A good-faith agreement can shift specific tasks to the tenant (`tenant-repair-agreement-gu`); the lease can't waive the tenant's remedies (`edu-landlord-breach-remedy-gu`). Guam uses the shared maintenance clauses `landlord-maintenance` and `landlord-maintenance-nd`.

After typhoons, inspect roofs, windows, shutters and weatherheads promptly.

title: Habitability: What Guam Has and Lacks
bodyText: How Guam compares on habitability features found elsewhere. Present: a fitness and code duty that a lease can't waive, though a good-faith agreement may shift specific duties to the tenant; written-notice termination (14 working days to remedy, termination no sooner than 30 working days after receipt); an essential-services self-help and substitute-housing remedy; a weatherhead repair-and-deduct rule after winds over 34 knots (10 working days); rent abatement if possession isn't delivered; casualty termination or rent reduction where enjoyment is substantially impaired; unsafe-building vacate orders under the building law. Absent (no provision found in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library): (1) a separate housing code (repealed 2010) or statutory list of dangerous conditions; (2) a general repair-and-deduct remedy (barred without your written consent) and any right to withhold rent for repairs; (3) a heat standard or cooling duty; (4) a residential smoke or carbon monoxide alarm statute; (5) any presumption of breach or unreasonable delay; (6) a duty to provide or pay for alternate housing; (7) an express rent bar for condemned units; (8) rent escrow; (9) a required habitability statement in the lease; (10) a small-landlord exemption; (11) a bed-bug or mold rule; (12) a general anti-retaliation statute, for example for repair complaints (Article 5 bars retaliation against a tenant solely because the tenant or a household member is a victim of family violence, criminal sexual conduct or stalking or ended a lease under Article 5, and Guam's housing-discrimination law bars retaliation against anyone who opposed a discriminatory housing practice or took part in a complaint or proceeding under it). Working days exclude weekends and federal and Guam government holidays. Details are in the linked Guam rows.

title: Shifting Maintenance Duties to the Tenant in Guam
bodyText:
Guam's Rental Act lets you and the tenant agree that the tenant will take on your own maintenance duties: complying with building and housing codes relative to health and safety, making repairs needed to keep the premises fit and habitable, and reporting defects.

The only condition the Act sets is that the agreement is entered in good faith, meaning honestly, objectively and with no deliberate intent to defraud.

Guam has no list of particular conditions that may be shifted, no separate-writing rule and no limit by building size.

One Guam rule does work the way some states' lists do: garbage. Every owner of a residential building must subscribe to garbage collection, but the owner of a building of four units or less may petition the Guam Solid Waste Authority, yearly, to skip the subscription if the lease obligates the tenant to subscribe.

Use `tenant-repair-agreement-gu` for specific repair or upkeep tasks, with something given in return, and `garbage-subscription-gu` for garbage. Don't use a blanket clause handing all repairs to the tenant: it is unlikely to pass as good faith, and lease terms that waive the tenant's rights under the Act are unenforceable.

title: Facilities You Must Provide in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library lists facilities a landlord must supply inside a rental home, such as screens, a mailbox, a stove or particular lighting. Guam's Housing Code article was repealed in 2010. What does apply: no building may be occupied as a dwelling without toilet and sewage facilities of the type Guam's sewage law requires, and you as owner are responsible for their structural integrity, repair and replacement of broken or worn-out parts, while the tenant keeps them clean and sanitary. Guam has adopted the International Building Code and International Residential Code (2009 editions, as amended) as construction standards; their text is not part of Guam's compiled code, so check with the Department of Public Works for what applied when your building was built or altered. From June 3, 2027, the International Property Maintenance Code will apply, as the Department adopts it, only to buildings on Hotel-zoned (H) properties. Guam's Building Law also makes the owner or the owner's designated agent responsible for maintaining every building in a safe and sanitary condition, with required devices and safeguards in good working order. Beyond that, your duties are to meet the building and housing codes relative to health and safety and keep the premises fit and habitable. Anything the lease promises (a pool, laundry, parking, appliances) becomes part of the premises and part of the tenant's remedies, so list only what you will actually maintain.

title: Promises to Repair in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library sets a rule, like Wisconsin's, that a landlord's promise to clean, repair or improve a unit must be in writing, carry a completion date or be made before the lease is signed. Whether a promise binds you is left to general contract law. Three Guam rules make writing it down the sensible course. First, Guam's Rental Act treats the rental agreement, written or not, as the source of the tenant's remedies: if you don't do what the agreement promises, the tenant may give written notice and end the lease if the breach isn't remedied within 14 working days (weekends and federal and Guam government holidays excluded), and recover damages. Second, a lease for longer than one year is invalid unless it, or a note or memorandum of it, is in writing and signed by the party to be charged. Third, the tenant may not unreasonably refuse you entry to make necessary or agreed repairs, so a written list of agreed work, with target dates, supports your entry to do it. List any promised work in the lease or a signed addendum, and don't make promises orally that you don't intend to keep.

title: Quiet Possession in Guam
bodyText: Guam puts a covenant of quiet possession into every hiring by statute: an agreement to let binds you to secure the tenant's quiet possession of the property during the term against all persons lawfully claiming it. Its words are a promise against superior claims (a lender, a co-owner, a prior tenant or buyer); whether it also reaches your own or a third party's disturbance is for case law, which this library did not search. If you don't, within a reasonable time after request, place and secure the tenant in quiet possession, the tenant may end the lease before the term ends. Guam's Rental Act adds the protections tenants usually mean by quiet enjoyment: you may not abuse your right of entry or use it to harass; an unlawful entry or repeated harassing demands for entry let the tenant get an injunction or end the lease and recover damages, costs and attorney's fees; and if you unlawfully remove or exclude the tenant, or willfully cut essential services, the tenant may recover possession or end the lease and recover actual damages. These rights can't be waived in the lease. Make sure a lender or co-owner can't disturb the tenancy before you lease, and give notice of a sale as Guam law requires.

title: Rent Collection and Your Repair Duties in Guam
bodyText: Some states say expressly that whoever receives the rent keeps the repair duty, whatever a lease, assignment, deed or mortgage says. No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library states such a rule, but its Rental Act reaches the same people in other ways. A "landlord" under the Act is the owner, lessor or manager of the property, so each of them carries the Act's duties, including code compliance and repairs. You are relieved of liability after a sale only by giving the tenant written notice of a good-faith sale to a bona fide purchaser, and you stay liable for the security deposit unless the buyer is credited with it and everyone is notified. A manager is relieved only after written notice to the tenant that the management has ended, unless otherwise agreed. And no lease term may make the tenant waive the Act's rights or remedies. Assume that assigning rents to a lender, or having a manager collect them, leaves every repair duty in place.

title: Government Inspections of Rentals in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library sets up a rental registration or periodic rental inspection program. Inspections reach rentals in three ways. First, the Department of Public Works' building official, showing proper credentials, may enter any building or premises at any reasonable time as needed to perform the Building Law's duties, and may order an unsafe building vacated and repaired or demolished. Second, renting real property needs a Guam business licence; the one-time temporary licence for a dwelling unit (available since August 2025) requires a Certification of Suitability for Occupancy from a Certified Home Inspector (or, for federally assisted tenants, a HUD-certified or GHURA-authorized inspector) covering electrical, plumbing, air conditioning, environmental, security and egress items, and is revoked if a violation isn't corrected within 14 calendar days after a notice of violation. Third, voucher units are inspected under federal program rules. No Guam law says a lease can authorize a government inspector to enter without the tenant's consent. Your own inspection entry is limited to the Rental Act's rule: the tenant may not unreasonably refuse, and you give at least 24 hours' notice and enter at reasonable hours. To have an inspector inspect, arrange the visit with the tenant on that notice and attend.

title: No Small-Landlord Repair Remedy Exemption in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library sets up a rent-escrow procedure for repairs or a notice that lets a landlord with few units, or an owner-occupant, opt out of the tenant's repair remedies. The tenant's remedies under Guam's Rental Act (written notice and termination if a health-and-safety breach isn't remedied within 14 working days, damages, the essential-services and typhoon-weatherhead remedies) apply to every residential landlord whatever the number of units, and a lease can't waive them. A tenant may not withhold rent for repairs not done, and may not repair and deduct without your written consent except for essential services and a wind-damaged weatherhead. The only small-building exemptions found in Guam law are unrelated to repairs: the garbage-subscription exemption for buildings of four units or less (`garbage-subscription-gu`) and the fair-housing exemptions for small owners. Don't put an "exemption" or escrow-waiver notice in a Guam lease.

title: How Tenants Give Repair Notice in Guam
bodyText: Guam's Rental Act makes the tenant report any defect the tenant believes you don't know about and believes you must repair, as soon as practicable; it doesn't say how. Formal remedies are different: to end the lease for your health-and-safety or lease breach, or to use the essential-services remedy, the tenant must give you written notice specifying the breach. A lease may ask for repair requests in writing, and the tagged maintenance clause does, but treat that as a request for good records, not a condition of your duty. Your duties to meet health-and-safety codes and keep the premises fit and habitable don't depend on a written request, and the tenant's damage claims for your noncompliance don't either. For typhoon damage to the weatherhead, your 10-working-day repair clock (weekends and federal and Guam government holidays excluded) starts at the earliest of when you or your agent becomes aware, when the tenant tells you in writing or orally, or when Guam Power Authority notifies you or the tenant after a post-storm inspection; a lease term making written notice the only trigger would waive an Act right and is unenforceable. A notice to you is received when delivered at your place of business or where the lease was signed, so state that address in the lease.

title: No Security-Device or Re-Keying Statute in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a residential landlord to install deadbolts, peepholes or door viewers, window latches or security bars, or to re-key the locks between tenants, at any building size or construction date. Doors and windows that close and lock are still part of keeping the premises fit and habitable and meeting the building codes relative to health and safety, and the inspection for Guam's one-time temporary rental business licence covers "security and egress". A vacant building not secured against entry is treated as unsafe under Guam's Building Law, so secure a unit between tenancies. The one lock duty Guam does impose is in the Guam Safe Housing Act: when a tenant protected by a court order gives you a copy and the restrained person is a tenant of the same unit, you must change the locks within 24 hours at your own cost (`edu-dv-lockchange-gu`). Re-keying at turnover is good practice; the `keys-gu` clause lets you charge a tenant the actual cost of re-keying when keys aren't returned or are lost, but never for the Safe Housing Act lock change.

title: No Senior-Housing Staff Work Card in Guam
