bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library sets a work-card or mandatory background-check rule for staff of senior (55-plus or 62-plus) apartment buildings or of any other ordinary rental housing. The background checks Guam law does require are tied to professional and program licences (physicians, nurses, teachers, peace officers, foster parents, child care homes, firearm and cannabis cards) and not to real estate licensing as such: that licensing reaches agents who manage rentals for others and has no background-check rule in the Guam law searched, though a licence may be denied, suspended or revoked for a felony or a crime involving moral turpitude. If your property provides care to residents, it may be a licensed care facility with its own rules; that is outside a residential lease. Screening staff who hold keys or enter units is good practice, and federal program rules may apply to assisted senior properties.

title: Services and Utilities You Provide in Guam
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library lists services a landlord must furnish; the lease decides which utilities and services you provide, and Guam uses the tagged clause `services-utilities-provided-ks-oh` (you provide only what the lease lists and what the law requires).

Once the lease has you supply a service, it is part of the rental agreement and the tenant's remedies reach it.

For essential services (running water, electricity, gas, hot water) that you willfully or negligently fail to supply under the lease, the tenant may give written notice and then either arrange the service and deduct its actual and reasonable cost from the rent, or move to substitute housing with rent excused for the period (you don't pay for the substitute housing unless you agreed in writing).

If you willfully interrupt an essential service, the tenant may recover possession or end the lease and recover actual damages. These remedies don't apply where the tenant, the tenant's family or others on the premises caused the condition.

Other promised services (laundry, a pool, internet) are enforced through the tenant's general remedy for breach of the lease.

Two things stay yours: the structure and repair of toilet and sewage facilities, and garbage collection subscription for the building, unless GSWA grants you one of the statute's exemptions, for example where the building has four units or fewer (or is another qualifying building) and the lease obligates the tenant to subscribe, or where you or the tenant register with GSWA as a self-hauler (`garbage-subscription-gu`).

title: No Stove or Refrigerator Requirement in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires you to supply a stove, range or refrigerator in a rental home, or says who maintains one. Guam's Housing Code article was repealed in 2010, and nothing in the Rental Act lists appliances. If the lease includes a stove or refrigerator, it is part of what you promise: the tenant's remedies for breach of the lease reach it, so list every appliance you supply and will maintain (`appliances-included`), and say plainly which items you leave in the unit but won't maintain. One related rule: under Guam's apartment-keeper's lien, a tenant's own refrigerator, stove and other kitchen furniture are exempt from any lien for unpaid rent.

title: Repair Orders for Unsafe Buildings; No Receivership in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library sets up a code-enforcement receivership for rental housing: none lets tenants or the government ask a court to appoint a receiver to collect rents and fix a substandard building. Guam's general receivership law lets a court appoint a receiver only in listed situations, including a mortgage foreclosure where the property is in danger or the security is insufficient, after judgment, in an unlawful-detainer action, and in other cases traditionally allowed in equity; a receiver may then collect the rents under the court's control. Repair orders come instead from two agencies. The Building Law makes the owner (or a designated agent) responsible for maintaining every building in a safe and sanitary condition; the building official may find a building unsafe (including unsanitary or unfit for human habitation), order it vacated and repaired or demolished within a stated time of no more than 30 days, and, if the owner doesn't comply, have the work done with the cost a lien on the land. The health law makes the owner fix a failing toilet, septic or sewage system within 48 hours after written notice, or the work is done at the owner's expense, also a lien. An order to vacate your rental may also give the tenant the Rental Act's remedies.

title: Cable Television Access for Tenants in Guam
bodyText: Guam's Consumer Protection and Right to Choose Cable Television Service Act limits what you may do about cable television in a residential building. You may not forbid or prevent a tenant from receiving cable service from a cable operator; may not demand or accept payment from the operator or the tenant as a condition of allowing installation or service (unless you are yourself the provider); and may not charge different rent to tenants who do or don't subscribe. You may require the cable operator and the tenant to bear the full cost of installation, operation and removal, require reasonable indemnity or security for damage, and claim just compensation from the operator for the installation through the Act's notice procedure (written notice within 20 days after the operator notifies you; otherwise compensation is presumed to be $1). In buildings of 12 or more units you may require installation plans, and approval may not be unreasonably withheld. Cable wiring installed inside a dwelling becomes a fixture owned by the building owner. Guam has no comparable rule for internet-only service or satellite dishes; federal rules on antennas and dishes may apply. Don't put a lease term barring cable service or charging cable subscribers more.

title: Utilities You Pay Under a Guam Lease
bodyText:
No Guam law stops you from including some or all utilities in the rent; Guam uses the tagged `utilities-paid-by-landlord` clause to list them.

A utility you agree to pay becomes one you must supply under the lease. If it is running water, electricity, gas or hot water and you willfully or negligently fail to supply it (for example, by letting your account be disconnected), the tenant may, after written notice, restore the service and deduct the actual and reasonable cost from the rent, or move to substitute housing with rent excused for that period; a willful interruption also lets the tenant recover possession or end the lease and recover damages (`edu-services-utilities-provided-gu`).

Keep the accounts current: where it knows or has reason to know of the tenancy, Guam Waterworks Authority must, where feasible and after notice, offer your tenant water service in the tenant's own name before disconnecting your account, and can't make the tenant pay your arrears (`edu-utility-landlord-account-gu`).

If you charge the tenant separately for a utility instead of including it in the rent, the charge is rent under Guam's Rental Act, and Guam's water rules bar retail resale of water without GWA's written approval (`edu-utility-allowance-gu`).

title: Utility Allowances and Overage Charges in Guam
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library governs a private landlord's utility allowance, where you pay a utility up to a monthly amount and the tenant reimburses the overage; the utility allowances in Guam's public-assistance rules concern welfare budgeting, not leases.

Guam uses the tagged clause `utility-allowance-cap-co`. Three cautions.
- First, the overage is "rent" under the Rental Act's definition (every payment due to you under the lease), but the clause agrees not to treat it as Rent for nonpayment remedies, which only narrows your own remedies.
- Second, for water and sewer: Guam Waterworks Authority's rules say retail resale of water received by a customer is not permitted without GWA's written approval, and unauthorized resale lets GWA disconnect without notice. Passing on only the actual overage shown on GWA's bill for the unit's own meter, with no markup and a copy of the bill, is the cautious course; whether that counts as resale isn't settled, so ask GWA before allocating a shared or master meter.
- Third, for electricity: Guam Power Authority's compiled rules have no resale rule, but the same no-markup, actual-bill approach is the safe one.

title: Dividing Shared Utility Bills in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library governs dividing a master-metered or shared utility bill among tenants by a formula (ratio billing), or makes unenforceable a lease term that has the tenant pay for utilities not separately metered to the unit. What does apply: any utility charge the lease has the tenant pay you is rent under Guam's Rental Act, so it is subject to the rules on rent; Guam Waterworks Authority's rules bar retail resale of water without GWA's written approval (so allocate only your actual GWA charges, with no markup, or include water in the rent, and ask GWA before allocating a shared meter); and when a utility disconnects a master meter for your unpaid bill, it must try to inform the occupants and, if asked, give them at least five days to arrange continued service. If you allocate a shared bill, state the formula in the lease, give the tenant copies of the bills, and keep the master account current.

title: When You Hold the Utility Account in Guam
bodyText: If you hold the utility account for a tenant's home and fall behind, Guam's utility rules protect the tenant. Water: where Guam Waterworks Authority has reason to know a landlord-tenant relationship exists (or bills you at a different address) and you are the customer, GWA may not disconnect until, where feasible, it has offered the occupant, after notice, service in the occupant's own name (if the occupant declines, GWA may disconnect); it may not try to collect your arrears from the tenant or make the tenant pay them to get service. All regulated utilities: where service runs through a master meter or to someone other than the customer of record, the utility must make reasonable efforts to tell the occupants of the coming disconnection and, on request, allow at least five days to arrange continued service; and a previous customer's unpaid bill is not enough to refuse a new customer service unless the two belong to the same household. Under Guam's Rental Act, if the lease has you supply running water, electricity, gas or hot water and you willfully or negligently fail to, the tenant may, after written notice, pay to restore the service and deduct the actual and reasonable cost from the rent, or move to substitute housing with rent excused; a willful interruption lets the tenant recover possession or end the lease and recover damages. Guam has no rent-receiver remedy for a landlord's unpaid utility bill.

title: Utility Shutoff Limits in Guam
bodyText: Guam's limits on utility shutoffs are in the utilities' rules, not in a statute about tenants, and none of them is a weather or storm moratorium. Under the Public Utilities Commission's general rules, a utility may not disconnect without the required notice; except where life or property is in danger, it may not disconnect on a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday or on a day it can't restore service the same or next day; it may not disconnect while the customer pursues a remedy or appeal if undisputed amounts are paid; and where service runs through a master meter it must try to tell the occupants and, on request, give them at least five days. Guam Waterworks Authority must give at least 10 days' advance written notice, may not disconnect when conditions are especially dangerous to health, the rule listing as provisos a physician's documentation that termination would be especially dangerous to the customer's health and life-saving apparatus in the home that depends on the service (it doesn't say whether both are needed), and for elderly or handicapped customers unable to pay must first exhaust a deferred payment plan, assistance funds and a third party the customer designates. Guam Power Authority bills are past due 15 days after presentation and past-due accounts are subject to disconnection on a disconnect notice. No Guam rule found bars disconnection during a typhoon or declared emergency. For you as landlord: never cut off a tenant's water, electricity, gas or hot water yourself; a willful interruption gives the tenant the Rental Act's remedies.

title: No Utility Submetering Disclosure Rule in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library prescribes a lease disclosure, type size or separate signed page for submetered, ratio-billed or landlord-billed utilities, and none sets up a regime regulating how a landlord bills tenants for submetered electricity or water. The rules that do apply are in `edu-utility-interruption-submeter-gu` (your duties if you supply and interrupt a utility, Guam Waterworks Authority's bar on retail resale of water without its written approval, and the master-meter disconnection rule) and `edu-utility-apportionment-gu` (dividing a shared bill). Good practice: state in the lease which utilities are submetered or allocated, how each charge is calculated, when it is billed and due, and that you pass on only actual cost with copies of the utility's bills.

title: Utility Shutoff Notices: Tenant May Name You in Guam
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library gives an owner a right of its own to be told when a tenant's utility service is about to be cut off.

What exists is customer-driven: Guam Waterworks Authority's application for service lets the customer, at the customer's option, give the name and address of another party for termination notices, and GWA forwards a copy of a termination notice to designated third parties where applicable; for an elderly or handicapped customer unable to pay, GWA won't disconnect until the customer can't meet the requirements of GWA's deferred payment plan, government and social-assistance funds have been exhausted, and a third party the customer designated has been notified and can't pay the bill.

Guam Power Authority's compiled rules have no such program.

A lease may ask the tenant to name you where a utility offers it (`utility-shutoff-notice-copy-gu`); the tenant still controls the account.

The Public Utilities Commission's rule that a utility must try to inform occupants before disconnecting a master meter protects tenants on your account, not you (`edu-utility-landlord-account-gu`).

title: No Landlord Utility Cutoff for Non-Transfer in Guam
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library gives you a procedure to cut off utilities still in your name when a tenant doesn't transfer them, and a lease term giving you that power would run into the Rental Act: willfully interrupting running water, electricity, gas or hot water lets the tenant recover possession or end the lease and recover damages, and the tenant can't waive that.

Use the optional clause instead (`utility-transfer-gu`): the tenant puts listed services in the tenant's own name by a set date, reimburses you at the utility's bill amount (no markup) until then, and a failure is a lease breach you enforce with the Rental Act's written notice (`default-by-tenant-gu`).

Both Guam Waterworks Authority and Guam Power Authority take tenants as customers.

Mind the gaps at each end: the customer stays responsible until the utility gets notice to stop service (GWA asks for four working days' notice; GPA two days), and water left off can let septic and sewage systems fail, which Guam's health law makes the owner fix on short notice. Plan the hand-back of accounts at move-out.

title: Tenant Remedies When Repairs Aren't Made in Guam
bodyText: Guam's Rental Act gives tenants a closed set of repair remedies. General breach: if you don't comply with the lease or with your code and repair duties affecting health and safety, the tenant may give written notice specifying the breach and a termination date at least 30 working days after you receive it; the lease doesn't end if you remedy the breach within 14 working days (weekends and federal and Guam government holidays excluded). The tenant may also recover actual damages and get an injunction, plus attorney's fees if your noncompliance is willful. No rent withholding: a tenant may not withhold rent for repairs not done, and may not repair or deduct without your express written consent. Two exceptions: essential services (running water, electricity, gas, hot water) you willfully or negligently fail to supply, where after written notice the tenant may secure the service and deduct its actual and reasonable cost or move to substitute housing with rent excused; and a weatherhead damaged by winds over 34 knots (40 mph) that you don't begin, or make a good-faith effort to begin, repairing within 10 working days after you become aware, where the tenant may hire a master and licensed electrician and, after giving you an itemized invoice, deduct the reasonable cost from the next rent (a balance above one month's rent over no more than three months); this doesn't apply where an electrician or engineer has found the building unsafe until other repairs are made, or the tenant apparently abandoned it. Fire or casualty and unlawful lockouts have their own remedies. The tenant can't terminate, repair at your expense, or use the essential-services or casualty remedies for conditions the tenant, family or others on the premises caused (each section words this exception differently); the weatherhead rule has its own exclusions instead. Guam's older repair-and-deduct rule (up to one month's rent) yields to the Act's ban for residential leases.

title: Lock Changes for Protected Tenants in Guam
bodyText:
Guam's Safe Housing Act requires a lock change in one situation: when a person restrained by a court order from contact with a protected tenant is also a tenant of the same unit, you must change the locks of the protected tenant's unit no later than 24 hours after the protected tenant gives you a copy of the court order, pay for the change yourself, and give the protected tenant a key to the new locks.

You are not liable to the restrained person for civil damages for complying, and the restrained person stays liable to you under the lease. The 24 hours run in hours, not working days, so plan for weekend and holiday requests.

Guam law sets no lock-change duty where the abuser isn't a co-tenant, but a court's family-violence order may give the victim possession of the home to the exclusion of the abuser; honour such an order, and agree to a reasonable lock-change request from a victim.

Don't charge the victim for the required lock change (`keys-gu`), and don't share what the tenant tells you under the Act with anyone without the tenant's written consent unless the law or a court requires it. These rules can't be changed by the lease.

title: Inspections During the Tenancy in Guam
bodyText:
Inspecting the premises is one of the purposes for which a Guam tenant may not unreasonably refuse you entry. Except in an emergency or where it is impracticable, give at least 24 hours' notice of your intent to enter, enter only at reasonable hours, and don't use inspections to harass.

Guam uses the tagged `inspection-rights` clause (periodic and move-out inspections on reasonable notice consistent with the lease's entry terms) with `landlords-access-mi`. Guam has no rule on how often you may inspect and no tenant right to a pre-move-out inspection; a move-in condition record supports later deposit deductions (`move-in-condition-report-gu`).

If the tenant refuses lawful access, you may get a court order compelling it or end the lease and recover damages, costs, lost rent and attorney's fees. See `edu-landlord-entry-gu`.

title: No Key-Control Policy Mandate in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a written key-control policy, a master-key log or background checks for employees with key access, whatever the size of the property. What Guam law does require around keys: change the locks within 24 hours, at your cost, when a protected tenant gives you a court order against a co-tenant (`edu-dv-lockchange-gu`); enter only as the Rental Act allows (`edu-landlord-entry-gu`); and use the security deposit only for the purposes Guam allows, which include unreturned keys. A written key-control practice (who holds master keys, a sign-out log, re-keying at turnover) helps you show that any entry was lawful.

title: No No-Notice Entry for Scheduled Services in Guam
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library allows entry without notice for regularly scheduled services such as filter changes or pest treatment, even if the lease says so conspicuously.

Supplying services as agreed is a purpose for which the tenant may not unreasonably refuse you entry, but except in an emergency or where notice is impracticable you must still give at least 24 hours' notice of each entry and enter only at reasonable hours, and a lease can't waive that.

You may list the services you will supply on a schedule (`periodic-services-entry-gu`), which makes them agreed services; give the 24 hours' notice before each visit.

During a tenant's absence of more than 7 working days (weekends and federal and Guam government holidays excluded) you may enter at times reasonably necessary, and during any extended absence for inspection, maintenance and safe-keeping.

title: No Shortened Notice for Showings in Guam
bodyText: Showing the unit to prospective buyers, lenders or tenants is a purpose for which a Guam tenant may not unreasonably refuse you entry, but the Rental Act's notice rule applies: except in an emergency or where impracticable, at least 24 hours' notice and entry only at reasonable hours. Guam has no provision letting a tenant waive or shorten that notice in the lease or in a separate signed document, and the Act says a rental agreement may not make the tenant waive its rights, so don't put a shorter showing-notice term in a Guam lease (the shared `showing-notice-la` isn't used). A tenant may still agree to a particular showing on shorter notice at the time; keep a record of that consent. Repeated demands for entry that unreasonably harass the tenant let the tenant get an injunction or end the lease and recover damages and attorney's fees.

title: No Smart-Lock Statute in Guam; General Rules Apply
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library specifically governs smart locks, keypad or app-based entry, key fobs or other electronic access systems in rental housing. The general rules apply to them. Electronic access logs don't change Guam's entry rule: you may enter only for the listed purposes with at least 24 hours' notice (except in an emergency or where impracticable), during abandonment or extended absence, or by court order, and the tenant can't waive this. When a protected tenant gives you a court order against a co-tenant, treat changing "the locks" within 24 hours as including resetting codes and revoking the restrained person's credentials, at your cost (the Act doesn't address electronic locks; this is the cautious reading). Treat entry codes and access logs as information you shouldn't disclose, especially anything a tenant gives you under the Safe Housing Act. If a smart lock depends on the tenant's internet or power, say so in the lease, and give the tenant a working way to enter if power fails after a typhoon.

title: Duty to Re-Rent After Abandonment in Guam
bodyText: Guam's Rental Act requires you to mitigate when a tenant abandons: you must make reasonable efforts to re-rent at a fair rental. If you re-rent for a term starting before the old lease ends, the old lease ends when the new tenancy begins. If you don't make reasonable efforts, or you accept the abandonment as a surrender, the lease is treated as ended by you on the date you had notice of the abandonment. For a tenant who abandons with no intention of returning, you recover the lesser of the rent for the rest of the term, or the daily rent for the period needed to re-rent plus a reasonable commission plus any shortfall between the old rent and the fair rental value. So a Guam lease stays enforceable for rent after a tenant leaves only within that measure: a clause accelerating all remaining rent, or keeping the lease alive without re-renting, would likely conflict with the Act (whose rights can't be waived) and with Guam's rule against fixing damages in advance (no Guam case deciding this was searched). For a month-to-month tenancy the term for this purpose is one month. Keep records of advertising and showings. Details and property left behind: `edu-abandoned-property-gu`.

title: Attorney's Fees in Guam Lease Disputes
bodyText:
In Guam, any lease provision for costs or attorney's fees is construed as mutual: it entitles every party who is bound by or benefits from it to fees and costs. A one-way clause in your favour therefore works both ways, so the library's optional clause (`attorney-fees-gu`) is written as a mutual prevailing-party clause.

Without a lease clause, Guam's Rental Act awards attorney's fees only in listed cases. You may recover reasonable fees if the tenant's noncompliance is willful, if a holdover is willful and not in good faith, if the tenant refuses lawful access, or if a tenant knowingly gives a false Safe Housing Act notice. The tenant may recover fees if your noncompliance is willful, if your failure to deliver possession is willful and not in good faith, or for your unlawful or harassing entries.

No party may be awarded fees or costs in a source-of-income discrimination action, and the lease can't change that. In Small Claims, fees are awarded only where a statute or the contract provides, at the court's discretion.

title: Federal 30-Day Notice and Guam Notices
bodyText: The federal row (`edu-cares-act-notice`, tagged for Guam) explains the CARES Act 30-day notice to vacate for properties with a federally backed mortgage or in covered federal housing programs. Here is how it fits Guam's notices. For nonpayment, Guam's Rental Act notice gives the tenant 5 working days to pay and lets you end the lease no sooner than 30 working days after the tenant receives the notice (weekends and federal and Guam government holidays excluded), which on its own runs longer than 30 calendar days; the eviction chapter's 5-day notice to pay or quit is a separate requirement (`edu-nonpayment-notice-gu`). Notices for other breaches, holdovers and month-to-month tenancies can be shorter than 30 days. On a covered property, don't require the tenant to leave sooner than 30 days after a notice to vacate, whatever the Guam notice allows. Federal voucher and public-housing rules add their own notices.

title: Who May Appear in Court for an Entity Landlord in Guam
bodyText: In Guam, only a licensed Guam attorney may represent someone else in court, and preparing court documents for another, representing another in a lawsuit, or preparing a lease for another are listed as the practice of law. An individual landlord may appear for himself or herself. An entity landlord (a corporation, LLC or partnership) generally needs a Guam attorney to file or defend an eviction or damages case in the Superior Court. The exception is Small Claims: a bona fide full-time employee, officer or director of a corporation may represent the corporation there (claims of $10,000 or less), but no other non-attorney may represent another person. The rule's wording names corporations only, so an LLC or partnership should confirm with the court before sending a member or manager. Property managers who aren't attorneys may not appear in court for the owner, and shouldn't prepare court papers or leases for owners (the listed acts don't depend on being paid).

title: Early Lease Release for Victims Under the Guam Safe Housing Act
bodyText: Guam's Safe Housing Act lets a tenant who is a victim of family violence, criminal sexual conduct or stalking end the lease early. The tenant notifies you in writing that he or she is a victim, gives you the evidence the Act lists (`edu-dv-qualifying-documents-gu`), and must be seeking to vacate because of fear of imminent danger to self or children. The tenant may then end the lease and move out without further obligation except one month's rent following the move-out, due within 90 working days (weekends and federal and Guam government holidays excluded); after paying it, the tenant is released from any further rent without penalty. Rent and other amounts owed before the tenant's notice stay owed. The termination doesn't release any co-tenant who isn't a victim: the others remain bound by the lease. The right doesn't depend on whether the abuser lives in the unit or is on the lease, and it applies to every residential lease and renewal in Guam. It can't be waived or modified by the lease, so a lease early-termination fee or notice period never applies to it (`early-termination-gu`). You may not refuse to rent to, or retaliate against, someone solely because he or she ended a lease under the Act.

title: Eviction Protections for Victims in Guam
bodyText: Under Guam's Safe Housing Act you may not evict a victim because of an incident or incidents of actual or threatened family violence, criminal sexual conduct or stalking. You may still evict for reasons unrelated to the abuse, may bring an eviction case against a tenant who committed the abuse, and may get a criminal no-trespass order against a non-tenant abuser at the property. A victim isn't liable for damage to the property related to the abuse beyond the value of the victim's security deposit, where the abuser is a tenant and the victim gives you written notice of the damage and the Act's documentation within 30 working days of the damage (weekends and federal and Guam government holidays excluded); you may hold the abuser liable for the damage. You may not end a lease, refuse to renew, refuse to rent, or retaliate solely because a tenant, applicant or household member is a victim. Keep what the tenant tells you confidential. Lease clauses on criminal activity, guests or damage must preserve these protections (`criminal-activity-ky`, `tenant-caused-damage-gu`), and none of them can be waived.

title: Documents Victims Provide Under the Guam Safe Housing Act
bodyText: To end a lease early under Guam's Safe Housing Act, the tenant gives you written notice of being a victim plus one of three kinds of evidence: a police report written within the prior 30 working days; a valid restraining or protective order; or a statement written within the prior 30 working days by a licensed medical or mental health professional who examined or consulted with the victim, confirming that fact (working days exclude weekends and federal and Guam government holidays). The same documentation, given within 30 working days of the damage, limits a victim's liability for abuse-related damage when the abuser is a tenant. For the 24-hour lock change, the protected tenant gives you a copy of the court order. You may contact the issuer to verify the documents; that is not a prohibited disclosure. Otherwise, don't share the information with anyone without the tenant's written consent unless the law or a court requires it. Don't demand more than the Act lists: it sets the forms of evidence and doesn't authorize further proof (the cautious reading; no Guam case was searched). If a tenant knowingly submits a false notice or documents to end a lease, you may recover the greater of three months' periodic rent or three times your actual damages, plus costs and attorney's fees.

title: No Condominium Conversion Rules for Tenants in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library gives tenants notice, a right of first refusal or relocation help when a rental building is converted to condominiums or cooperatives, and none bars converting rental housing in general to hotel or other transient use, though Guam's zoning law requires a certificate before a dwelling unit is rented as a short-term vacation rental unit (21 GCA § 61133) and bars using an accessory dwelling unit as a bed and breakfast or short-term vacation rental (21 GCA § 61141(b)(6)). What applies: Guam's new-home warranties treat units in an existing building converted into residential condominiums as new homes for buyers (a protection for purchasers, not tenants); a sale of a unit doesn't end an existing lease, and to be relieved of liability you must give the tenant written notice of a good-faith sale to a bona fide purchaser, with the security deposit staying your responsibility unless the buyer is credited with it and everyone is notified; once a building is under Guam's Horizontal Property Act, tenants of unit owners are bound by the declaration and bylaws. Converting units to short-term vacation rentals needs the certificate and licences Guam requires for transient lodging, and advertising unlicensed transient lodging carries heavy fines. A fixed-term lease runs to its end; a periodic tenancy may be ended by the notice Guam law sets (`edu-termination-notice-gu`).

title: Criminal Activity as a Lease Breach in Guam
bodyText:
Guam has no statute making criminal or drug activity a special ground for ending a residential lease, no fast-track eviction, and no crime-free lease law.

Criminal activity is handled as a breach of the lease: Guam uses the tagged clause `criminal-activity-ky`, which makes criminal activity that threatens others, or drug activity on the property, a material noncompliance enforced with the notice the Default by Tenant terms and the law require.

That means the Rental Act's written breach notice (termination no sooner than 5 working days after receipt; weekends and federal and Guam government holidays excluded) and, for an eviction case, the eviction chapter's notice; no cure period is required for a breach that can't afterward be cured. Guam's general hiring law also lets you end a hiring when the tenant uses the property for a purpose contrary to the agreement.

You may not evict a victim because of family violence, criminal sexual conduct or stalking against them (the clause carves this out). Federal public-housing and voucher rules add their own criminal-activity terms for assisted units.

title: No Drug-Free Addendum Statute in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library authorizes, requires or prescribes a drug-free or crime-free lease addendum, and no law lets a government require landlords to join a crime-free housing program. You may include a lease term forbidding illegal drug activity (Guam uses `criminal-activity-ky`), but it doesn't change how a tenancy ends: a violation is a lease breach enforced through the Rental Act's written notice and, if needed, an eviction case, and a victim of family violence, criminal sexual conduct or stalking may not be evicted because of that abuse. Don't use an addendum that lets you end the lease without notice or on an arrest alone. Federally assisted housing has its own required lease terms.

title: No Expedited Criminal Eviction in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library sets an expedited eviction track for violent crime, drug activity or other criminal conduct, and no third party (a prosecutor, the Attorney General or a tenant organization) may bring an eviction for drug activity. A crime-related eviction follows the ordinary route: the Rental Act's written breach notice, then an unlawful-detainer case in the Superior Court (`edu-eviction-process-gu`). Two features speed every possession case: the summons gives the tenant 5 days to appear and answer, and Guam's courts must give possession cases precedence over other civil actions in setting and hearing them. No cure notice is needed for a breach that can't afterward be cured. Where criminal conduct puts people in immediate danger, call the police; a protective order or criminal no-trespass order may also exclude a non-tenant offender.

title: Typhoons and Disasters Under a Guam Lease
bodyText:
Guam has no rule that a declared disaster ends a tenancy or suspends rent; the Rental Act's fire-and-casualty rules cover it, and "casualty" expressly includes earthquake, wind, typhoon and other natural disasters.

If a typhoon or other casualty the tenant didn't cause substantially impairs enjoyment of the unit, the tenant may move out at once and give written notice within 14 working days (weekends and federal and Guam government holidays excluded) that the lease ends as of the move-out date, or, if continued occupancy is lawful, stop using the unusable part and pay rent reduced in proportion to the loss of fair rental value.

Rent is accounted for as of the date of the casualty, and any recoverable deposit must be returned. Your options as landlord are contractual (`casualty-termination-gu`).

For a weatherhead damaged by winds over 34 knots (40 mph), begin, or make a good-faith effort to begin, repairs within 10 working days after you become aware, or the tenant may hire a master and licensed electrician and, after giving you an itemized invoice, deduct the reasonable cost from rent (a balance above one month's rent over no more than three months), unless an electrician or engineer has found the building unsafe until other repairs are made or the tenant apparently abandoned it.

After a disaster that brings a declared state of emergency, you may not raise rent because of a shortage the disaster anticipated or caused; after a disaster seriously damaging 500 or more homes, a typhoon with sustained winds of 100 mph or more, or an earthquake over 7.0, the Governor may also freeze residential rents at pre-disaster levels for up to 120 days by executive order. Check each executive order issued after a typhoon.

title: No Landlord Environmental-Event Termination in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library gives a landlord a right to end a residential lease because of an environmental event or hazard (contamination, mold, a chemical release, an ordered evacuation). What exists: the tenant's fire-and-casualty remedies, where "casualty" covers insurable perils including earthquake, wind, typhoon and other natural disasters; the building official's power to order an unsafe or unsanitary building vacated and not reoccupied until a new certificate of occupancy issues; and Guam EPA's power to order cleanup. The library offers a landlord casualty-termination option (`casualty-termination-gu`). A broader landlord option to end the lease after a non-casualty environmental event is not prohibited by the Rental Act, but it isn't offered: no Guam statute frames it, it could reach conditions that are your repair or code duty, and Guam's rules against exculpation and waiver of Act rights make an open-ended trigger risky. If you want one, take advice. A government order to vacate may also give the tenant the Rental Act's remedies.

title: Eminent Domain and Your Guam Lease
bodyText:
Guam has no landlord-tenant statute saying whether a lease ends, or rent stops, when the rented property is taken by eminent domain.

Guam's condemnation law leaves it to the court: once the government files a declaration of taking and deposits its estimate of just compensation, title vests in the government, the right to compensation vests in the persons entitled to it (which can include a tenant with a valuable lease), and the court may fix when and on what terms the people in possession must surrender it. Guam's general hiring law apportions rent for the use actually made when a hiring ends early.

The lease may settle these questions: the optional `condemnation-gu` clause ends the lease on surrender (or reduces rent for a partial taking), apportions rent, and gives you the award except the tenant's own relocation and personal-property payments. Without it, expect the tenant to claim a share of the award for the lease's value.

title: Delays and Stays in a Guam Eviction
bodyText: Guam has no eviction moratorium tied to weather, typhoon season, rental-assistance applications or holidays, and no rule pausing an eviction for a tenant's hardship as such. The delays that exist come through the courts. A tenant may ask the court, within 30 days after a judgment declaring the lease forfeited, for relief against the forfeiture in case of hardship; the court may restore the tenancy only on full payment of the rent due or full performance of the lease terms, as far as practicable. An appeal doesn't stop enforcement of an eviction judgment unless the judge so directs. Guam's civil rules generally bar execution on a judgment until 10 days after its entry and let the court stay enforcement while certain post-judgment motions are pending. The Small Claims Division may, with or without bond, stop an eviction while a bona fide rent or landlord-tenant dispute is decided. Under the Rental Act, rent abates and the tenant may leave if you can't deliver possession, and casualty or essential-services failures have their own remedies. Plan move-out dates with these possible delays in mind.

title: No Eviction Record Sealing in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library seals or expunges eviction (unlawful detainer) case records, automatically or on request, and none limits how you may use eviction records in screening applicants or gives you a right to object to sealing. Guam's expungement and record-clearing laws concern criminal and juvenile records, not landlord-tenant cases. Two limits do affect screening: from October 1, 2026, you may not refuse to rent or set different terms because of an applicant's lawful source of income, and a credit check is protected from a source-of-income claim when you check every applicant (publicly subsidized housing projects and Chamorro Land Trust leases are exempt from these rules); and you may not refuse to rent to a victim of family violence, criminal sexual conduct or stalking solely because of that status or because the victim ended a lease under the Safe Housing Act. Federal consumer-reporting law limits what tenant-screening reports may contain.

title: No Lease-Named Agent for Eviction Papers in Guam
bodyText: Guam's eviction chapter sets how pre-filing notices are served (personal delivery; or, if the tenant is away from home and work, leaving a copy with a person of suitable age and discretion there and mailing a copy; or, if neither place can be found, posting at the property, delivering to a resident and mailing), and requires notices to go to any subtenant in actual occupation too. The summons is served the same way as in any civil action. Only the tenant and any subtenant in actual occupation need be named as defendants, and anyone who enters under the tenant after the case is filed is bound by the judgment. Guam's civil rules let an individual be served through "an agent authorized by appointment or by law to receive service of process", but no provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library addresses naming such an agent in a lease, and the library doesn't offer one: a lease-named agent who isn't actually authorized, or doesn't pass the papers on, puts a default judgment at risk. Serve the tenant directly by one of the methods the law lists.

title: Foreclosure and Tenants in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires you to tell tenants about a pending foreclosure, and nothing in Guam's Rental Act says what happens to a lease when the landlord's lender forecloses. What Guam law provides: after a mortgage foreclosure sale made through court proceedings and with the buyer's title perfected (the eviction chapter doesn't name a sale under a power of sale), a person holding over may be removed through the eviction chapter after a 3-day written notice to quit, served as that chapter requires; in the lender's foreclosure case the court may appoint a receiver, who may collect the rents, where the property is in danger or the security is insufficient; and a tenant who paid rent to you before notice that the rents were granted to someone else isn't liable for it again. Federal law (the Protecting Tenants at Foreclosure Act) generally lets a bona fide tenant stay until the end of the lease, or at least 90 days after notice, after a foreclosure of residential property; it was not read for this library and is not Guam law. If you sell rather than lose the property, give the tenant written notice of the sale and handle the deposit as Guam's sale rule requires (`edu-security-deposit-on-sale-gu`).

title: Saving the Lease From Forfeiture in Guam
bodyText: A Guam lease generally doesn't end the moment the tenant defaults, and a lease clause can't take away the tenant's statutory chances to save it. One exception is in the eviction chapter: assigning, subletting or committing waste contrary to the lease 'thereby terminates the lease' (21 GCA § 21103(d)), and you then serve a five-day notice to quit; how that fits with the Rental Act's notice for breaches was not settled by any Guam case searched, so the cautious course is to give the Act's notice too. Under the Rental Act, a tenant who pays the rent within 5 working days after your written nonpayment notice keeps the lease, and a remediable breach fixed before the termination date in your breach notice doesn't end it (working days exclude weekends and federal and Guam government holidays). Under the eviction chapter, the tenant, a subtenant, a lender on the leasehold or anyone else interested may, within 3 days after a notice to perform a lease term, perform it or pay the stipulated rent and so save the lease from forfeiture. If you sue, the judgment declares the lease forfeited only if your notice stated your election to declare the forfeiture. And within 30 days after a forfeiture judgment the tenant may ask the court for relief in case of hardship, granted only on full payment of the rent due or full performance of the lease terms, as far as practicable. Accepting rent after a notice may also affect your case; Guam's renewal rule presumes a renewal when you accept rent after a lease expires.

title: Guarantors and Renewals in Guam
bodyText:
Guam has no landlord-tenant rule on guarantors, but its general guaranty law (18 GCA Ch. 31, from California's Civil Code) applies to a lease guaranty.

A guaranty must be in writing and signed by the guarantor. A guarantor's obligation can't be larger or more burdensome than the tenant's.

The rule that matters most at renewal: a guarantor is released if you change the tenant's obligation in any respect without the guarantor's consent. So a guaranty that speaks only of the original term may not cover a renewal, an extension, a month-to-month continuation or a rent increase.

If you take a guarantor, use the optional Guaranty clause (`guaranty-gu`), which records the guarantor's consent to renewals and later changes, or get the guarantor's written consent each time. A guaranty of future periods can be revoked by the guarantor for periods not yet begun, so check before a renewal starts. Whether advance consent covers every later change hasn't been decided by any Guam case this library searched.

Don't take a separate deposit or other money from a guarantor when the lease starts: Guam limits what you may collect at lease commencement to the first month's rent and the security deposit (with any pet deposit).

title: No Exemption-Waiver Rule in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library lets a lease waive a tenant's exemptions from collection, or forbids it in words, and the library offers no waiver clause. Guam's exemptions protect a judgment debtor's homestead, necessary household, table and kitchen furniture (including one stove, beds and bedding), necessary clothing and three months' provisions, small amounts of trade tools, public and private pensions and retirement money, child support, and in some cases recent earnings needed for the family. A homestead under Guam law is the claimant's own dwelling, selected and recorded as the law provides; a tenant's rented unit isn't one unless it's held on a lease of 30 years or more. Guam's statutory lien for apartment keepers also leaves out household furniture, bedding and tools of the trade (`edu-landlord-lien-gu`). Whether a lease waiver of exemptions would be enforced hasn't been decided by any Guam case this library searched. Collect unpaid rent through a court judgment, and expect exempt property to stay out of reach.

title: Apartment Keeper's Lien in Guam
bodyText: Guam law gives keepers of apartment houses, apartments, cottages, mobile homes and bungalow courts a statutory lien on a tenant's belongings in the unit for unpaid rent and charges, with a right to hold them and, after 60 days unpaid, to sell them at public auction after newspaper notice and a mailed notice at least 15 days before the sale. The lien doesn't reach a musical instrument used to earn a living, prosthetic or orthopedic appliances, table, kitchen and bedroom furniture (including one refrigerator, washing machine, sewing machine and stove), beds and bedding, clothing, tools and books used to earn a living, or family paintings and portraits; other household items (such as radios, TVs and vehicles stored at the property) are also excluded, except so much of them as is reasonably sufficient to satisfy the lien. No lease clause is needed for it, and the library offers no contractual lien. Don't use it as self-help. Guam's rental law lets you enter an occupied unit only with the tenant's consent for listed purposes on at least 24 hours' notice, in an emergency, by court order, or when the unit appears abandoned or during an extended absence for inspection, maintenance and safe-keeping; removing or excluding a tenant unlawfully lets the tenant recover possession or terminate and recover damages. Whether the lien's possession and sale steps can be used against a residential tenant without a court order hasn't been decided by any Guam case this library searched. Collect through a court judgment, and handle belongings left after the tenant leaves under `abandoned-property-gu`.

title: No Health or Care-Facility Termination Right in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library lets a tenant end a fixed-term lease early because of age, illness, disability or a move to a nursing home, assisted living or a relative's care. A tenant in that position stays bound by the lease, but if the tenant leaves, you must make reasonable efforts to re-rent at a fair rental, and your damages are limited to the lesser of the rent for the rest of the term or the cost of re-renting plus any rent shortfall (`edu-early-termination-gu`). A periodic (for example month-to-month) tenancy that either side may end at will is ended by notice to the other side of the tenant's death or incapacity to contract; other hirings aren't ended that way. A tenant who is a victim of family violence, criminal sexual conduct or stalking and seeks to leave out of fear of imminent danger to self or children may end the lease under Guam's Safe Housing Act, after written notice with the evidence the Act lists and owing one month's rent after moving out (`edu-dv-lease-termination-gu`); no lease can change that. Federal fair-housing law may require a reasonable accommodation for a tenant with a disability. If a tenant asks to leave early for health reasons, put any agreement in writing.

title: Landlord's Remedies When a Guam Lease Ends for Breach
bodyText: When a Guam tenant breaches, your remedies come from the Rental Act and the eviction chapter, and you recover possession only through the Superior Court. You may recover actual damages and get an injunction for the tenant's noncompliance, with attorney's fees only if the noncompliance is willful. After ending the lease on the required notice (`default-by-tenant-gu`, `edu-nonpayment-notice-gu`), an unlawful-detainer judgment restores possession, assesses your damages and any rent found due, and may, in the court's discretion, be for three times that amount; the judgment declares the lease forfeited only if your notice stated that election. If the tenant has abandoned, you must make reasonable efforts to re-rent at a fair rental, and you recover the lesser of the rent for the rest of the term or the daily rent while re-renting plus a reasonable commission and any rent shortfall. When a lease ends early, rent is apportioned to the use actually made. A willful, bad-faith holdover adds rent owed, eviction costs and fees (`edu-holdover-gu`). Guam has no rent-acceleration statute; the library offers no acceleration clause, since a demand for all future rent sits badly with the duty to re-rent and the damages limit.

title: Fixing a Tenant's Maintenance Failure in Guam
bodyText:
Guam's Rental Act lets you fix a tenant's maintenance failure and bill the cost as rent, whether or not the lease says so.

It applies when the tenant fails to meet the tenant's duties (keeping the unit clean and safe, disposing of waste, not damaging the premises, reasonable use of utilities and common areas) in a way that materially affects health and safety and can be remedied by repair or replacement of a damaged item.

Give written notice, delivered personally or by registered or certified mail, describing the breach and asking the tenant to remedy it within 5 working days (weekends and federal and Guam government holidays excluded), or as promptly as conditions require in an emergency.

If the tenant doesn't, you may enter, have the work done in a workmanlike manner, and submit an itemized bill for the actual and reasonable cost as rent on the next rent date, or for immediate payment if the lease has ended. Give 24 hours' notice of entry unless it's an emergency.

Bill actual cost only, keep receipts, and don't charge a fixed fee. The optional clause `landlord-self-cure-gu` puts this procedure in the lease. For other damage, see `tenant-caused-damage-gu`.

title: No Self-Help Eviction in Guam
bodyText: You may not lock a Guam tenant out, remove doors or belongings, or cut off water, power or other essential services to recover possession or force payment. The only way to recover possession from a tenant who won't leave is an unlawful-detainer case in the Superior Court (`edu-eviction-process-gu`). If you unlawfully remove or exclude the tenant, or willfully interrupt running water, electricity, gas or hot water, the tenant may recover possession or end the lease, and recover actual damages, and you must return the recoverable deposit if the lease ends. Guam's forcible-entry chapter also treats turning out the person in possession by force, threats or menacing conduct as forcible entry, and the court may treble damages for a forcible or unlawful entry or detention. Your right to enter an occupied unit is limited to the tenant's consent for listed purposes on 24 hours' notice, emergencies, court orders, apparent abandonment and extended absences. A lease can't waive these protections. Belongings left after a tenant has gone are handled under `abandoned-property-gu`. The one lock change Guam requires is protective: within 24 hours after a protected tenant gives you a court order against a co-tenant (`edu-dv-lockchange-gu`).

title: No Lockouts for Unpaid Rent in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library lets a landlord lock out a residential tenant for unpaid rent, with or without a lease clause, and the library offers none. A lockout would be an unlawful removal or exclusion: the tenant could recover possession or end the lease and recover actual damages, and a lease term giving up those rights is unenforceable. For unpaid rent, give the written nonpayment notice and, if the rent isn't paid, end the lease and bring an unlawful-detainer case (`default-by-tenant-gu`, `edu-nonpayment-notice-gu`, `edu-self-help-eviction-gu`).

title: Minors as Tenants and Parties in Guam
bodyText: In Guam a minor is anyone under 18, and a minor can't make a contract relating to real property, so don't have anyone under 18 sign a lease as a tenant. Other contracts of a minor can generally be disaffirmed by the minor before turning 18 or within a reasonable time afterwards, without returning what was received. A married minor may join a spouse in a lease of the couple's own property, but that rule is about owners, not tenants. If someone guarantees a lease for a young tenant, Guam's guaranty law keeps the guarantor liable despite a merely personal inability of the tenant (`edu-guarantor-renewal-gu`). List minors in the household as occupants, not tenants. In an unlawful-detainer case you need name only the tenant and any subtenant in actual occupation, and people who move in under the tenant after you file are bound by the judgment. If a minor is a party to a case, the minor must appear through a general guardian or a guardian ad litem appointed by the court. Guam has no eviction-specific rule on naming minors as defendants.

title: No Notice-Fee Rule in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library authorizes, caps or forbids a fee for preparing or serving a notice on a tenant, and the library offers no such fee. Several rules make one a poor fit. Guam's notices to a tenant can be delivered personally at no cost, or by registered or certified mail. A flat fee charged because the tenant breached is a sum fixed in advance as damages, which Guam treats as void unless actual damage would be impracticable or extremely difficult to fix (`edu-liquidated-damages-gu`). Any amount the lease makes payable to you counts as rent under Guam's Rental Act, which can complicate a later nonpayment notice. In an eviction case, fees for service of process and marshal's fees are taxable costs the court can award to the winning party. If a tenant's breach makes you pay an actual expense, claim it as actual damages.

title: No Waiving Required Notices in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library clearly lets a lease waive or shorten the notices you must give to end a residential tenancy or bring an eviction case (on the Rental Act's breach notice, see below), and the library offers no waiver clause. The Rental Act's rights can't be waived: a lease term giving them up is unenforceable. Its nonpayment notice gives the tenant 5 working days (weekends and federal and Guam government holidays excluded) to pay, with termination no sooner than 30 working days after the tenant receives it. Its breach notice sets a termination date at least 5 working days after receipt 'unless otherwise agreed in writing by landlord and tenant' (21 GCA § 48401(a)); that wording might allow a different agreed period, but a shorter one risks the Act's waiver bar (21 GCA § 48105) and no Guam case was searched, so use it only for a longer period. The eviction chapter adds its own 5-day pay-or-quit and 3-day comply-or-quit notices, and its forfeiture election, with no provision for waiving them. A month-to-month tenancy is ended by notice at least as long as the rental period, up to one month, and a tenancy at will by at least 30 days' written notice. Apart from that uncertain breach-notice wording, the only notice Guam lets the parties shorten by agreement is the month-to-month change-of-terms notice, and only in writing when the tenancy is created (`term-change-notice-gu`). See `edu-termination-notice-gu` and `edu-cure-and-eviction-grounds-gu`.

title: Nuisance Law in Guam
bodyText: Guam's nuisance law is general, not landlord-tenant specific. A nuisance is anything injurious to health, indecent or offensive to the senses, or an obstruction to the free use of property that interferes with the comfortable enjoyment of life or property; it is public if it affects a whole community or neighborhood or a considerable number of people, and otherwise private. Anyone whose property is injuriously affected or whose personal enjoyment is lessened may sue to enjoin or abate it and recover damages, and the Attorney General may sue to abate a public nuisance. Public Health may order a public-health nuisance abated, and a person occupying or leasing another's property who keeps one going after written notice from Public Health or the Attorney General commits a misdemeanor, as does an owner who permits one. A later owner who neglects to abate a continuing nuisance created by an earlier owner is liable for it. Cannabis smoke or odor drifting onto another's property is a nuisance. No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library provides nuisance receivership of rents, building closure or a nuisance-based eviction procedure. In the lease, the tenant's duty not to disturb neighbors and the shared Disturbance clause (`no-disturbance`) cover tenant conduct; act on a breach through the default notice (`default-by-tenant-gu`).

title: Use for Another Purpose in Guam
bodyText: Guam's hiring law says that when property is let for a particular purpose, the tenant must not use it for any other purpose; if the tenant does, the tenant is liable for all resulting damages, or you may treat the lease as rescinded. You may also end the hiring early when the tenant uses the property, or allows it to be used, contrary to your agreement. Guam's tagged Residential Use clause (`residential-use-only`) states the purpose. A contract term with an unlawful object is void as to that part. No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library voids or annuls a residential lease automatically because the premises are used for a crime, or forfeits or closes a rented home for drug, gambling or prostitution use. To end a lease for illegal or prohibited use, give the written breach notice and follow the eviction steps (`default-by-tenant-gu`, `edu-cure-and-eviction-grounds-gu`), and remember that a tenant may not be evicted because of family violence, criminal sexual conduct or stalking against the tenant.

title: Ending a Lease Early to Move In
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library gives you a right to end a lease early so you or a relative can move in, or limits one the lease reserves.

Guam has no general just-cause rule for written leases (`for-cause-eviction-gu`), so an agreed owner-occupancy termination is a contract term.

If you may need the home back during a fixed term, use the optional Owner Occupancy clause Guam is tagged on (`owner-occupancy-termination-ar`): written notice at least the number of days you choose (not less than 30) before a termination date at the end of a monthly rental period, with rent only through that date.

A month-to-month tenancy can be ended without a reason by the notice Guam law sets (`edu-termination-notice-gu`).

Two limits: an oral (unwritten) lease of a tenant's primary residence entered after January 1, 1988 can't be ended in its first year except for nonpayment or damage, and after that needs 90 days' notice; and you may not refuse to renew solely because a tenant is a victim of family violence, criminal sexual conduct or stalking. If the tenant doesn't leave, recover possession only through the court.

title: No Possession Bond in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library lets a landlord require a tenant to post a bond, or sign a confessed judgment, to secure giving up possession when the lease ends, and the library offers none. Guam's eviction chapter has no possession bond, and its ban on confessed-judgment powers of attorney is written for consumer credit sales and consumer leases of goods, not leases of homes. Guam's general judgment-by-confession procedure gives only a money judgment, on a sworn statement that a specified sum is justly due, so it can't secure possession either (`edu-confession-of-judgment-gu`). A bond or other security taken at the start of the lease would also run into Guam's limit on money collected at lease commencement: only the first month's rent and the security deposit (with any pet deposit). Use the security deposit and, if you need more security, a written guaranty (`guaranty-gu`), and recover possession through an unlawful-detainer case.

title: Delay in Delivering Possession in Guam
bodyText:
If you can't deliver possession on the lease's start date, Guam's Rental Act stops the rent until you do, and the tenant may end the lease on at least 5 working days' written notice (weekends and federal and Guam government holidays excluded); if the lease ends, you must return all security deposits.

If your failure is willful and not in good faith, the tenant may recover twice the actual damages plus reasonable attorney's fees.

A lease can't take these rights away, so Guam uses the shared Delay in Possession clause `possession-delay-ca`, not `possession-delay`, which makes the tenant wait longer to end the lease.

If the delay comes from a holdover tenant, you can bring an unlawful-detainer case against that tenant, and a willful bad-faith holdover can owe you rent, eviction costs and fees. Tell the new tenant in writing as soon as you know of a delay.

title: A Tenant's Belongings After an Eviction in Guam
bodyText: After you win an unlawful-detainer case, possession is delivered under a writ of execution directed to the marshal, which requires the marshal to deliver possession to you and may also collect the costs, damages and rent in the judgment out of the tenant's personal property. No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library sets separate rules for a tenant's belongings or animals left at the removal, gives the landlord immunity for the removal, or makes returning after the writ a specific crime. Guam's Rental Act procedure for property left behind is written for a tenant who has abandoned the premises, including after a notice to quit or at the end of the term; the cautious course is to follow it after a removal too (`abandoned-property-gu`): mail notice to the forwarding address, an address the tenant designated, or the last known address; wait at least fifteen (15) working days before selling or donating; hold sale proceeds, less accrued rent and storage and sale costs, in trust for thirty (30) working days. Treat animals humanely and contact the Department of Agriculture's animal control if no one claims them.

title: Paying to Keep the Tenancy in Guam
bodyText: Guam gives a tenant behind on rent several chances to keep the tenancy. Under the Rental Act, the lease isn't ended for nonpayment if the tenant pays within 5 working days (weekends and federal and Guam government holidays excluded) after your written nonpayment notice. Under the eviction chapter, within 3 days after service of a notice the tenant, a subtenant, a mortgagee of the term or anyone interested in the lease may perform the covenants or pay the stipulated rent and so save the lease from forfeiture. After a judgment declaring the lease forfeited, the court may relieve the tenant against the forfeiture and restore the tenancy in a case of hardship, if a verified petition is filed within 30 days after the judgment, and only on condition that the rent due is paid in full (or the covenants performed, so far as practicable). Guam has no statute on accepting partial rent or requiring a reservation of rights when you do, and no right to redeem right up to the removal. If you accept a partial payment after a notice, say in writing that you're accepting it toward the amount due without waiving the notice, and see `edu-waiver-by-acceptance-gu`.

title: No Rent-into-Court Rule in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a tenant to pay rent into court, or into escrow, to defend an eviction or raise a counterclaim, and none makes the tenant's counterclaim mandatory in the possession case. Under the Rental Act an "action" includes recoupment and counterclaim, so a tenant may raise claims under the Act in your case. The Small Claims Division may hear rent and landlord-tenant disputes, may, with or without bond, stop an eviction while a bona fide rent or landlord-tenant dispute is decided, and may order an eviction as part of its final order. The Rental Act also says a tenant may not withhold rent for repairs not done, apart from its essential-services and weatherhead deduction rules (`edu-tenant-repair-remedies-gu`). Keep accepting and recording rent the tenant tenders while a dispute is pending, without waiving your notice (`edu-waiver-by-acceptance-gu`).

title: False Information in a Rental Application
bodyText:
No Guam landlord-tenant statute deals with false statements in a rental application, so general contract law applies, and Guam uses the shared clause `rental-application-accuracy`, which makes material false or misleading information a material breach.

Under Guam's Civil Code a party whose consent was obtained through fraud may rescind the contract, and actual fraud includes stating as fact what one doesn't believe true and suppressing what one knows is true, with intent to deceive or to induce the contract.

To end a tenancy for a breach, still give the Rental Act's written breach notice and follow the eviction steps (`default-by-tenant-gu`); no Guam case says rescission for application fraud avoids them.

Limits on what you may ask and rely on: since October 1, 2026, you may not refuse to rent or set different terms because of an applicant's lawful source of income, including housing assistance, though checking an applicant's credit is not unlawful under that rule when you check the credit of every applicant (the rule does not apply to publicly subsidized housing projects or Chamorro Land Trust leases) (the shared clause's last sentence keeps such information out).

Guam's housing-discrimination law and federal fair-housing law also limit screening.

Guam makes it a misdemeanor to reveal an expunged official record to anyone not entitled to it; it says nothing about how applicants answer, and the library adds no expungement sentence.

title: No Termination Because Repairs Cost Too Much
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library lets you end a lease, or refuse a repair, because a needed repair would cost too much compared with the rent or the property's value. Your duty to comply with building and housing codes relating to health and safety and to make all repairs reasonably necessary to keep the premises fit and habitable continues for the whole tenancy, and a lease can't waive it (the Act does let you and the tenant agree that the tenant will perform some of those duties, but only if the agreement is made in good faith). Guam's older hiring statute let a tenant repair defects costing up to one month's rent and deduct, or vacate; the Rental Act now bars tenant repairs and deductions without your written consent, apart from its essential-services and weatherhead rules, and prevails over that statute in a conflict. If a fire or casualty substantially impairs the tenant's enjoyment of the home, the tenant may vacate and end the lease by written notice within 14 working days or, if continued occupancy is lawful, vacate the unusable part with a rent reduction (not where the tenant, family, guests or invitees caused the damage), and a hiring ends by law if the property is destroyed; your own right to end the lease after a casualty comes from the lease (`casualty-termination-gu`). The library offers no clause letting you cancel over repair costs.

title: Retaliation Against Tenants in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library generally bars a landlord from retaliating against a tenant who complains about conditions, asks for repairs, contacts a government agency or joins a tenants' group. Two specific rules apply. Under the Safe Housing Act you may not end a lease, refuse to renew, refuse to rent or retaliate against a tenant solely because the tenant, an applicant or a household member is a victim of family violence, criminal sexual conduct or stalking, or because the tenant ended a lease under that Act; these protections can't be waived. Guam's housing-discrimination law also makes it unlawful to retaliate against anyone for opposing a discriminatory housing practice or for filing a complaint, testifying or taking part in an investigation or proceeding under that law; federal fair-housing law has a similar rule. From October 1, 2026, you also may not set rental terms or refuse to rent because of a tenant's lawful source of income (publicly subsidized housing projects and Chamorro Land Trust leases are exempt). Even where no rule applies, a rent increase or non-renewal soon after a complaint invites a dispute: keep written, neutral reasons for every such decision.

title: Seasonal and Short-Term Rentals in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library sets special rules for seasonal residential tenancies: a lease for a season is an ordinary lease with an agreed term, governed by the Rental Act. State the exact start and end dates; a hiring of a dwelling with no stated term is presumed to run for the period by which rent is set (monthly if rent is monthly). If you accept rent after the season ends, the lease is presumed renewed on the same terms and for the same time, but not more than one month when rent is payable monthly and never more than one year, so give written notice before the end if you need the home back. Shorter stays fall under separate regimes. Renting a dwelling to transient guests for no more than 30 consecutive days is a short-term vacation rental, which needs a certificate from the Department of Revenue and Taxation, an emergency contact and compliance with zoning, and its occupants pay Guam's hotel occupancy tax; advertising a lodging facility for transient guests without the proper licences carries fines of $5,000 and more. Bed and breakfast homes have their own licence and standards. An accessory dwelling unit may be rented only on a signed written lease of at least six months, never as a short-term vacation rental. A business licence for renting real property is needed in any case (`edu-landlord-registration-gu`).

title: Servicemember Tenants in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library gives servicemembers, Guam National Guard members or their families a Guam right to end a residential lease early, a shorter termination notice, or a stay of eviction. The federal Servicemembers Civil Relief Act does apply in Guam: it lets a servicemember end a residential lease on entering active duty or receiving qualifying permanent-change-of-station or deployment orders, and it limits evictions of servicemembers and their dependents during military service. Follow it, and check a tenant's military status before seeking a default judgment. With many military households renting in Guam, two Guam rules matter too: since October 1, 2026 you may not refuse to rent or set different terms because of a tenant's lawful source of income, which includes military pay and housing allowances (publicly subsidized housing projects and Chamorro Land Trust leases are exempt); and Guam's accessory-dwelling-unit law treats active military deployment as a hardship that excuses the owner's occupancy requirement.

title: Late Benefit or Voucher Payments in Guam
