bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a court to postpone a nonpayment case, or reinstate a tenancy, because a Social Security payment, other government benefit or housing-voucher payment arrived late. Guam's source-of-income law, in force since October 1, 2026, points the other way on one narrow point: if the initial payment to you under a HUD-regulated assistance program isn't made on time because of processing delays or a government shutdown, you may exercise any right or remedy the law gives you. Otherwise you may not refuse to rent, or set different terms, because rent comes from assistance or benefits (publicly subsidized housing projects and Chamorro Land Trust leases are exempt). In practice, the Rental Act's nonpayment notice gives 5 working days to pay, termination can't take effect until 30 working days after the tenant receives it, and after a forfeiture judgment the court may grant hardship relief on a verified petition filed within 30 days after the judgment, only on condition that the rent due is paid in full (`edu-redemption-gu`). Federal program rules for vouchers and public housing may add their own steps; follow them for assisted tenancies.

title: Tenant's Legal Rights to End a Guam Lease Early
bodyText: Guam law lets a tenant end a residential lease early only in these situations, and a lease can't take them away. A victim of family violence, criminal sexual conduct or stalking who gives you written notice and qualifying evidence (a police report or a professional's statement written within the prior 30 working days, or a valid restraining or protective order), and who seeks to vacate because of fear of imminent danger to self or children, may end the lease and vacate, owing one month's rent after vacating, due within 90 working days (`edu-dv-lease-termination-gu`). If you don't deliver possession on the start date, the tenant may end the lease on at least 5 working days' written notice (`edu-possession-delay-gu`). If you breach the lease or your health-and-safety repair duties, the tenant may give written notice ending the lease at least 30 working days after you receive it unless you remedy the breach within 14 working days (`edu-landlord-breach-remedy-gu`). If fire or casualty substantially impairs the home, the tenant may vacate and give written notice within 14 working days. Neither of these two exits applies to a condition or damage the tenant, the tenant's family or guests or others on the premises caused, and a breach notice doesn't end the lease if you remedy the breach in time or show reason why the date can't be met. If you unlawfully remove or exclude the tenant or willfully cut essential services, or make unlawful or harassing entries, the tenant may end the lease. Working days exclude weekends and federal and Guam government holidays. Guam's general hiring law also lets a tenant end a hiring early if, within a reasonable time after request, you don't secure the tenant's quiet possession or put the home into good condition, or if the greater part of the home (or a part that was the tenant's material inducement to rent and that you had reason to believe was, when the lease was made) perishes other than through the tenant's want of ordinary care. A tenant tricked into signing by fraud may also rescind. No provision searched for this library voids unpaid rent because a lease left out a required statement. For agreed early termination, see `early-termination-gu`.

title: Family Violence Law Citations Current in Guam
bodyText: Guam's Safe Housing Act protects tenants who are victims of family violence, criminal sexual conduct or stalking 'as defined under Guam law' (21 GCA § 48501(a)), and accepts 'a valid restraining or protective order' (21 GCA § 48501(b)(2)) as evidence, without naming a particular chapter, so no cross-reference has gone stale. The definitions it relies on are current: family violence in the Family Violence Act (9 GCA § 30.10(a)), criminal sexual conduct in the criminal sexual conduct chapter (9 GCA Ch. 25) and stalking in the Guam Stalking Law (9 GCA § 19.70). Protection orders now come from three chapters: protection from abuse (7 GCA Ch. 40), which can give the victim possession of a shared residence and order rent or mortgage payments to continue; sexual offense protection orders (7 GCA Ch. 40A, added in 2022); and stalking protection orders (7 GCA Ch. 40B, added in 2022). The Superior Court's Protection Order Rules took effect September 17, 2025. Accept an order from any of these chapters, and a valid order from another court, as evidence under the Act (`edu-dv-qualifying-documents-gu`).

title: Moving Out at the End of a Guam Lease
bodyText:
No Guam provision searched for this library requires good cause to end or not renew a written lease: a written lease ends at the end of its agreed term, and Guam uses the shared Surrender at End of Term clause (`surrender-end-of-term`), whose "unless applicable law entitles Tenant to remain" covers the cases where Guam law does.

Three rules shape the end of a tenancy. If you accept rent after the term ends, the lease is presumed renewed on the same terms and for the same time (no more than a month when rent is monthly, and never more than a year), so don't take rent if you want the tenant out.

A tenant who stays without your consent can be removed through an unlawful-detainer case, and a willful, bad-faith holdover can owe rent, eviction costs and attorney's fees (`edu-holdover-gu`).

An oral lease of a primary residence entered after January 1, 1988 runs for at least one year and then needs 90 days' notice, except for nonpayment or damage.

When the tenant leaves, return the deposit balance with an itemized statement within fourteen (14) working days (`security-deposit-return-gu`); unreturned keys and cleaning needed to restore the move-in condition, less normal wear and tear, are lawful deposit deductions.

Belongings left behind are handled under `abandoned-property-gu`. If you accept a tenant's abandonment as a surrender, the lease ends as of the date you have notice of the abandonment.

title: When a Tenant Files for Bankruptcy
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library sets a landlord-tenant rule on a tenant's bankruptcy. Guam still has its own Insolvency Law (7 GCA Ch. 50), under which a landlord proves rent owed up to the time of insolvency as if it accrued day by day, but a tenant who files for bankruptcy will almost always do so under the federal Bankruptcy Code, which controls. Under federal law a bankruptcy filing generally stops eviction and collection steps automatically until the court allows them, and a lease clause ending the lease just because the tenant files is generally unenforceable; the library offers no such clause. If a tenant files, stop collection and notices, get the case number, and take advice before going further. Rent falling due after the filing, and a separate suit against a guarantor, are treated differently under federal law; a guarantor isn't released just because the tenant's debt is discharged by operation of law (`edu-guarantor-renewal-gu`).

title: When a Tenant Dies
bodyText:
No Guam landlord-tenant provision searched for this library deals with a tenant's death.

Under Guam's hiring law, a hiring that one of the parties may end at will is ended by notice to the other party of the tenant's death; any other hiring, such as a fixed-term lease, isn't ended by death, so the tenant's estate remains responsible for the rent and other lease duties until the term ends or the lease is otherwise ended (if the unit is abandoned, you must make reasonable efforts to re-rent it at a fair rental, `edu-early-termination-gu`).

Deal with the tenant's personal representative, or, for a small estate, with the heirs who give you the sworn affidavit Guam's probate law allows; that affidavit route is available only when the decedent left no real property or interest in it in Guam, and whether a lease counts as one hasn't been decided by any Guam case this library searched.

Guam uses the optional shared Emergency Contact clause `tenant-death-contact-nh`: naming a contact gives that person no right to occupy or remove belongings.

Belongings left behind are handled under `abandoned-property-gu`; return the deposit balance with the itemized statement within fourteen (14) working days after the lease ends, to the personal representative or entitled heirs. Co-tenants who survive remain bound by the lease.

title: Removing Unauthorized Occupants in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library gives an owner a fast-track removal of squatters or other unauthorized occupants outside the courts, such as police removal on an owner's affidavit. What Guam has: a forcible-detainer action against a person who, at night or while the occupants are away, unlawfully enters real property and refuses to surrender it for five days after a demand, where the former occupant had been in peaceable possession in the five days before the entry; criminal trespass, a misdemeanor when someone knowingly enters or surreptitiously remains in a dwelling without licence or privilege, which the police may act on; and, for anyone who moved in under your tenant, the rule that everyone entering under the tenant after you file an unlawful-detainer case is bound by the judgment. A former tenant or a tenant's guest who stays isn't a squatter: use the notice and eviction steps. Don't use force or change locks on someone in possession (`edu-self-help-eviction-gu`). The Safe Housing Act also leaves you free to obtain a criminal no-trespass order against a non-tenant who commits family violence, criminal sexual conduct or stalking at the premises.

title: Accepting Rent After a Breach in Guam
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library says when accepting rent waives a tenant's breach or a notice you have served, and none requires a written reservation of rights.

The one statutory rule is about the end of the term: if the tenant stays after the lease expires and you accept rent, the lease is presumed renewed on the same terms and for the same time (no more than a month when rent is monthly, and never more than a year).

Beyond that, whether accepting rent after a breach or after a notice to pay or quit waives the breach or the notice is a question of contract law and case law.

The cautious course: before accepting rent after serving a notice, decide whether you still intend to end the lease; if you do, accept only with a written statement that you accept it toward the amount due without waiving the notice, the breach or your right to possession, or return it.

A nonpayment notice under the eviction chapter may be served any time within one year after the rent falls due.

The optional clause `non-waiver-gu` records that accepting rent after a breach or notice isn't a waiver unless you agree in writing; a lease can't make the tenant give up rights under the Rental Act.

title: When Notice Counts in Guam
bodyText:
Guam's Rental Act defines when a person has notice: when the person actually knows the fact or has received a notification of it.

A notice to you is received when delivered at your place of business or where the lease was signed; a notice to the tenant, when personally tendered to the tenant or sent by registered or certified mail to the tenant's known residence. Eviction-chapter notices are served personally or by the substitute methods that chapter lists.

No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library lets the parties agree on a different way, such as text or e-mail, to give a notice the law requires to go a particular way: Guam's electronic-transactions law keeps any delivery method another law specifies, applies only between parties who agreed to deal electronically, lets either party refuse further electronic dealings, and doesn't let a sender use an electronic record the recipient can't print or store.

So agree on e-mail or text only as an extra courtesy copy and for routine matters (Guam uses the optional shared clause `electronic-notice-ma`), and always send required notices by the legal method (`edu-notice-delivery-gu`).

Actual knowledge can still matter: a tenant who actually knows a fact has notice of it under the Act.

title: Signing a Guam Lease Electronically
bodyText:
Guam's Uniform Electronic Transactions Act lets you and the tenant sign the lease electronically: a signature or contract can't be denied effect just because it is electronic, and where a law requires a writing or a signature, an electronic record or electronic signature satisfies it.

The Act applies only when each party has agreed to do business electronically, which the shared Electronic Signatures clause Guam uses (`electronic-signatures`) records. A party who agreed may refuse other electronic dealings, and that right can't be waived. Give the tenant a copy they can print or store.

Guam's electronic-transactions law doesn't exclude eviction, default or cure notices in words, but it keeps any delivery method another law specifies, and Guam's Rental Act and eviction chapter specify personal delivery, registered or certified mail, or (for eviction notices) leaving a copy with a suitable person or posting it, each with a mailed copy, so those notices still go on paper (`edu-actual-notice-method-gu`). Federal law (E-SIGN) separately excludes electronic default and eviction notices for a primary residence.

title: Which Document Controls in a Guam Lease
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a separate document, such as an addendum of nonstandard terms, that must control over the lease, and Guam uses the shared Addendum Precedence clause (`addendum-precedence`), which lets any disclosure or addendum the law requires control over a conflicting lease term.

The rule that matters in Guam runs the other way: the Rental Act's rights and remedies control over the lease, a lease term giving them up is unenforceable, and the Act prevails over the older hiring statutes (18 GCA §§ 51101-51112) in a conflict. The Safe Housing Act (family violence) and the source-of-income rules also can't be changed by agreement.

A rule you adopt after the lease is signed binds the tenant without consent only if it meets the Act's four conditions, including thirty (30) working days' notice (weekends and federal and Guam government holidays excluded) (`rules-gu`).

title: Changing a Written Guam Lease
bodyText:
Guam uses the shared Entire Agreement clause (`entire-agreement`). Guam's contract law backs its written-changes rule: a written contract may be altered only by a written contract or by an oral agreement that has been fully carried out.

The clause's exception for changes the law lets you make by written notice fits Guam: on a month-to-month tenancy you may change the terms by written notice at least thirty (30) days before the end of the month (or as little as seven days, if the parties agreed to that in writing when the tenancy began; `term-change-notice-gu`), and you may adopt rules that meet the Rental Act's four conditions on thirty (30) working days' notice (`rules-gu`).

No Guam provision searched for this library lets a landlord amend an existing fixed-term lease by notice to comply with new laws. A new law that applies to existing leases, such as the Safe Housing Act, which applies to renewals, modifications and extensions, takes effect whatever the lease says.

title: Proceedings Against the Property in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires you to tell a tenant or applicant that the property faces foreclosure, a tax sale, condemnation or another proceeding. The duty runs the other way: a tenant who receives notice of any proceeding to recover the property or its possession must immediately tell you and deliver any written notice, and is responsible for your damages if the tenant doesn't; Guam uses the shared clause `tenant-forward-proceedings-ca` for this. If you sell, you stay liable under the lease and the Rental Act until you give the tenant written notice of a good-faith sale to a bona fide purchaser, and you stay liable for the deposit unless the buyer is credited with it and everyone is notified. A tenant may not attorn to (accept as landlord) a stranger without your consent or a court judgment. Federal law protects many tenants when a home is foreclosed; telling a tenant early about a proceeding that may affect the lease is good practice.

title: Automatic Lease Renewal in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library regulates automatic-renewal terms in residential leases: there is no consumer auto-renewal statute requiring bold terms, opt-in or a reminder before renewal, and Guam's deceptive-trade-practices law defines 'sale and purchase' (5 GCA § 32103(n)) to leave out leases of real property of ten years or less, though its definitions of goods and of trade and commerce mention leases, so whether it reaches a residential lease is unsettled (no Guam case was searched). So a lease may renew itself if it says so clearly. Even without such a term, Guam law presumes the lease renewed on the same terms, for no more than a month when rent is monthly, if the tenant stays after the term and you accept rent. If the lease renews automatically, state the renewal term, the notice either party must give to stop it, and how rent may change, and remind the tenant before the deadline; a month-to-month rent change still needs thirty (30) days' written notice before the end of the month, or at least seven (7) days if the parties agreed to that in writing when the tenancy was created (`term-change-notice-gu`).

title: Arbitration Clauses in Guam Leases
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library authorizes or regulates arbitration clauses in residential leases.

Guam's general arbitration chapter is the Guam International Arbitration Chapter (7 GCA Ch. 42A), modelled on the UNCITRAL Model Law, written for international commercial arbitration and also applied by its own terms to domestic arbitration; whether it reaches a residential lease hasn't been decided by any Guam case this library searched.

Three limits weigh against an arbitration clause. The Rental Act's rights and remedies can't be waived, and possession is recovered through the Superior Court's unlawful-detainer process, which Guam gives priority. The Small Claims Division may hear rent and landlord-tenant disputes and stop an eviction pending a bona fide dispute. And since 2022 Guam has made pre-dispute arbitration agreements unenforceable, at the claimant's election, for sexual assault and sexual harassment disputes. Federal arbitration law may also apply.

If you want arbitration, agree on it after a dispute arises, or use court-annexed alternative dispute resolution, and take advice before adding a clause.

Federal law also matters here: the Federal Arbitration Act overrides state rules that block arbitration directly or indirectly (for example, a rule against giving up a jury), and the U.S. Supreme Court has held that renting out real estate is activity it reaches. On that basis the library now offers an optional clause, `arbitration-agreement`: money claims only, with possession, small claims, security-deposit, injury, emergency and government-agency matters kept out, every remedy and the right to a lawyer kept, the arbitration fees above a court filing fee paid by you, a 30-day opt-out for the tenant, and separate initials from both of you.

Because state law points the other way, a court here could still refuse to enforce it; if one did, the dispute would simply go to court.

title: Trying to Settle Disputes First in Guam
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires, regulates or forbids a lease term asking the parties to try to resolve a dispute informally before going to court.

Guam uses the shared clause `informal-dispute-resolution-or`, which leaves possession actions out and delays no deadline or remedy the law provides; keep it that way.

Watch Guam's own deadlines: a tenant's suit to recover a deposit must start within one year after the lease ends, the Rental Act's notice periods run in working days (weekends and federal and Guam government holidays excluded), and an informal-resolution step can't stretch the five (5) working days to pay or the thirty (30) working days before a nonpayment termination takes effect.

Once a case is filed, the Superior Court may refer it to mediation, a settlement conference or other alternative dispute resolution under its own rules, and the parties may agree to binding forms of it; the Small Claims Division also hears rent and landlord-tenant disputes.

title: Business Licenses for Rentals in Guam
bodyText: No Guam provision searched for this library sets up a landlord registry, but renting out property is a licensed business. Unless exempted by law, no one may carry on a business in Guam until obtaining a business license from the Department of Revenue and Taxation, and Guam's service-license law requires anyone who rents or leases residential units to obtain an annual service license ($10 a year for one family residential unit; for multiple units, $25 or $5 per unit, whichever is greater). Failing to get a required license is a misdemeanor. It also blocks your eviction case: a person doing business without a required business license may not maintain a proceeding in any Guam court until it gets one, and the court may stay the case meanwhile, though the lack of a license doesn't stop you defending a case. Since 2025 a one-time temporary business license, valid up to one year, is available for a dwelling unit that passes a Certified Home Inspector's inspection; leases under it are subject to the Rental Act. Short-term vacation rentals and bed and breakfasts need their own certificates (`edu-seasonal-tenancy-gu`), and anyone collecting rent for others for compensation generally needs a real estate broker's license. If you rent under a name other than your own, you must file a fictitious-name certificate with the Department of Revenue and Taxation within one month of starting, and until it is filed you can't sue on any lease or other contract made under that name (18 GCA §§ 26101, 26103). An owner that is a corporation or limited liability company formed outside Guam must also register or obtain a certificate of authority before doing business here, and can't maintain a case until it does (`edu-no-nonresident-owner-agent-gu`). Get and renew your licenses before signing leases or filing any case.

title: Emergency Contacts for Guam Tenants
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires or regulates an emergency contact for a long-term residential tenant.

You may ask for one: Guam uses the optional shared clause `tenant-death-contact-nh`, under which naming a contact gives that person no right to occupy the home or remove belongings.

Keep two Guam rules separate from it. The Rental Act lets the tenant designate an address for notices about property left behind, which `abandoned-property-gu` asks for; mail those notices there, not just to the emergency contact. And the emergency contact Guam requires for a short-term vacation rental is the owner's designee who must answer complaints and appear within two hours, not the tenant's contact.

Treat a tenant's emergency contact information as private, especially anything a tenant gives you under the Safe Housing Act, which you may not disclose without written consent unless the law or a court requires it.

title: No Energy-Data Release Rule in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires energy benchmarking of residential buildings, or governs a lease term letting a utility release a tenant's energy usage data to the owner. If the tenant holds the power or water account, ask the tenant to share usage information or to authorize the utility in writing to release it; the library offers no special clause. If you supply utilities, the bills are already yours.

title: Giving the Tenant a Copy of the Lease
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a landlord who signs its own lease to give the tenant a copy, and none makes a missing copy a defense to enforcing the lease.

A licensed real estate broker or salesperson is different: one who rents property or collects rent for an owner for pay and gets the tenant's signature on a lease must give the tenant a copy when the tenant signs (an owner managing its own property, and the owner's regular employees, are outside that licensing rule).

Give a copy anyway: Guam's Legislature has declared that all residential leases should be in writing and signed by both parties, an unwritten lease of a primary residence carries extra limits (a protected first year, 90 days' notice after it, and a 5% yearly rent cap), and an electronic lease you keep the tenant from printing or storing can't be enforced against the tenant.

Guam uses the shared clause `lease-copy-receipt-hi`, which records the tenant's receipt of the lease and any rules. Keep proof of delivery of rules too: a rule adopted after signing binds the tenant without consent only on thirty (30) working days' notice and the Act's other conditions.

title: No Blank-Spaces Rule in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires every blank in a written lease to be filled in, or makes an incomplete lease a breach by you. Good practice still matters in Guam: a written contract can be changed only by another written contract or an oral agreement that has been fully carried out, and unclear terms invite disputes, so fill in or strike every blank and have both parties initial any change before signing. Some Guam options work only if the lease actually says so, such as the tenant's duty to give notice of an extended absence (`extended-absence-notice-gu`) and the seven-day notice for changing month-to-month terms (`term-change-notice-gu`); a blank left unfilled may lose them.

title: What a Guam Lease Needs to Say
bodyText: No Guam provision searched for this library lists everything a residential lease must contain, but several Guam rules work only if the lease (or another signed writing) says something, and others limit what it may say. Put these in the lease when they apply: a requirement that the tenant give notice of an extended absence of more than seven working days (`extended-absence-notice-gu`); any agreement that month-to-month terms may be changed on seven days' notice, made in writing when the tenancy starts (`term-change-notice-gu`); any written agreement letting the deposit serve as last month's rent; any good-faith agreement that the tenant will do repairs (`tenant-repair-agreement-gu`); and, for a building of four or fewer units whose owner relies on it to skip the garbage subscription, the tenant's duty to subscribe (`garbage-subscription-gu`). An accessory dwelling unit may be rented only under a written agreement signed by owner and tenant for at least six months. A written lease signed by both parties avoids the special limits on oral leases. Leases of condominium apartments under Guam's Horizontal Property Act must describe the property (with a reference to the recorded declaration), give the apartment number, state its use and use restrictions and its common interest, and note encumbrances, though whether that reaches an ordinary rental of a unit hasn't been decided by any case this library searched; identifying the unit and stating the association's rules is the cautious course. A lease can't waive the Rental Act's rights, the Safe Housing Act or the source-of-income rules, and any attorney's-fee clause works both ways. Both spouses must sign a lease of their community real property, or of real property they own together as joint tenants or tenants in common, if its term with any options or extensions may exceed five years or if it is for an indefinite term. Federal lead-paint disclosure applies to pre-1978 housing.

title: Checked Across All of Guam Law
bodyText: Checked across all of Guam's codified law, administrative rules, court rules and the 38th Legislature's public laws, not only the landlord-tenant chapters: (1) Squatters: there is no fast removal outside the courts; use a forcible-detainer or unlawful-detainer case or report criminal trespass (`edu-unauthorized-occupants-gu`). (2) Rent receipts: a tenant who pays has a general right to demand a written receipt, and a business conducting more than ten taxable cash transactions a day must give a receipt or other record of each when it has the means to; give a written receipt for every payment, especially cash. (3) Licensing before eviction: present. Renting property is a licensed business in Guam, and a person doing business without a required business license may not maintain a proceeding in any Guam court until it gets one (`edu-landlord-registration-gu`). Two other filings work the same way: a landlord renting under a fictitious name can't sue on contracts made under that name until its fictitious-name certificate is filed, and a foreign limited liability company or corporation transacting business in Guam can't maintain a case until it has registered or obtained its certificate of authority (18 GCA §§ 26103, 7103, 7308, 7313; `edu-no-nonresident-owner-agent-gu`). (4) The Organic Act of Guam, which serves as Guam's bill of rights, binds the government of Guam; none of its guarantees was found to reach a private landlord's lease terms. (5) No Guam rule sets type size, bold print, capital letters, plain-language standards or a separate-document requirement for residential leases.

title: Other Rules Guam Does Not Have
bodyText: Rules found in some other places for which no provision was found in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library, each covered in its own section of this library: no general anti-retaliation law (`edu-retaliation-gu`); no lockout or other self-help eviction (`edu-no-lockout-gu`); no possession bond (`edu-no-possession-bond-gu`); no notice-service fee rule (`edu-no-notice-service-fee-gu`); no rent-into-court requirement (`edu-no-rent-into-court-gu`); no continuance when a benefit payment is late (`edu-no-benefit-delay-defense-gu`); no early-termination right for illness or a care-facility move (`edu-no-infirmity-termination-gu`); no right to end a lease because repairs cost too much (`edu-no-repair-cost-termination-gu`); no seasonal-tenancy regime (`edu-seasonal-tenancy-gu`); no Guam servicemember lease law (`edu-servicemember-rights-gu`); no general landlord lease-copy rule (real estate licensees must give a copy at signing), and no blank-space or emergency-contact rule; no energy-data rule; no consumer auto-renewal rule. Two rules Guam does have: renting part of a room as a dwelling entitles the tenant to the whole room whatever the lease says, and letting a room to more than one family relieves every tenant in the building of rent while the double letting continues; and smoke-detector duties appear only in the bed-and-breakfast standards and the care-home rules, not for ordinary rentals, with no rule shielding a landlord from liability or making detector compliance inadmissible.

title: No Lease Initials Requirement
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a tenant to initial particular lease clauses, or makes a clause enforceable only if it is initialed, separately signed or printed conspicuously. The tenant's signature on the lease is enough as far as Guam's written law goes. What Guam does require is that some things be in writing: a lease for longer than one year must be in writing and signed by the party to be bound; a written lease signed by both parties keeps the oral-lease rules (5% yearly rent cap, one-year initial period) from applying; your agreement to let the deposit serve as last month's rent must be in writing; and the shorter seven-day change-of-terms notice for a month-to-month tenancy must be agreed in writing when the tenancy is created. Initials never rescue a term the Rental Act forbids: a clause waiving the tenant's rights or remedies under the Act is unenforceable however it is signed. Practical step: initials beside key terms (fees, the seven-day notice option, the absence-notice duty) are optional evidence that the tenant saw them, not a Guam requirement.

title: Lease Length Limits in Guam
bodyText: No Guam provision searched for this library sets a maximum term for a private residential lease, or a minimum term apart from the six-month minimum for renting an accessory dwelling unit, or the main house on the same lot when the owner (or a relative or the owner's designated representative) rents it out while living in the accessory unit (each must be on a written agreement signed by owner and tenant; after that initial period the owner may let the same tenant of the accessory dwelling unit continue month to month), and none requires a seal or deed formality for a long lease. Length matters in several places. (1) A lease for longer than one year is invalid unless it, or a note or memorandum of it, is in writing and signed by the party to be bound; a manager or other agent who signs it for the owner needs the owner's written, signed authority. (2) An unrecorded lease longer than one year is void against a later good-faith purchaser or mortgagee who records first; recording a long lease with the Department of Land Management prevents that. (3) An oral lease of a primary residence runs for an initial period of one year with the protections in 18 GCA § 51111; a written lease signed by both parties avoids that section. (4) A tenant who stays after the term while you accept rent renews for no more than one month when rent is monthly, and never more than a year. (5) If you are married and lease community property, or property you and your spouse own together, both spouses must sign a lease whose initial term, with any option or extension, may exceed five years or that is for an indefinite term; one spouse's signature alone makes such a lease void. A court order letting an estate's personal representative lease property sets a period of no more than ten years unless the court authorizes a longer one.

title: No Lease Type-Size Rule
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library sets a minimum type size or typeface for a residential lease, for any notice a landlord gives under the Rental Act or the eviction chapter, or attaches an evidentiary penalty to small print in a lease. Guam's type-size rules govern other documents: consumer notices for telemarketed goods (14-point) and used-part repair disclosures (10-point), time-share offering statements, notarial fee schedules, cannabis labels and advertising, election petitions and court filings (12-point minimum under the Superior Court's general rules). Practical step: print the lease and every notice in a readable size (11- or 12-point is common practice), because a term the tenant could not reasonably read invites a dispute over whether the tenant agreed to it; but no Guam rule fixes the size.

title: No Nonresident-Owner Agent Rule
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires an owner who lives off-island to name a Guam agent in the lease, to file an agent designation before suing a tenant, or (in that corpus) to have rent withheld for tax. Two general rules still matter. First, if you own through a corporation or limited liability company formed outside Guam, company law reaches you. A foreign limited liability company that owns income-producing real property in Guam is transacting business here, so it must obtain a certificate of registration from the Department of Revenue and Taxation, naming an agent for service of process, before it starts; until it is registered it may not maintain an eviction or any other case in a Guam court, it faces a penalty of $20 a day (up to $10,000), and it is treated as having appointed the Department as its agent for service of process on claims arising from its Guam business, though its leases stay valid (18 GCA §§ 7306(b), 7308, 7312, 7313). A foreign corporation needs both a business license and a certificate of authority before transacting business in Guam, must keep a registered office and registered agent here, and can't maintain a case until it has both; an unauthorized one is treated as having appointed the Director of Revenue and Taxation as its agent for service of process. Merely owning real property is not transacting business for a corporation, so whether renting it out is depends on the facts (18 GCA §§ 7102, 7103, 7108, 7113(e)). That is company law, not a lease term. Second, under the Rental Act a tenant gives you notice by delivering it at your place of business or where the lease was signed, so an absentee owner should name in the lease a Guam address (yours or your manager's) where notices will actually reach you. Guam's income tax mirrors the federal Internal Revenue Code; its rules on tax withholding from rent paid to nonresident owners are outside this library's corpus, so ask a tax adviser.

title: No Rule on Move-Out Notice Forms or Work During Notice
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library regulates a move-out or notice-to-vacate form you ask a tenant to sign, requires a warning when such a form adds terms the lease does not contain, or bars renovation work while a notice to vacate is pending. The Rental Act still governs until the tenancy ends. Your duty to keep the unit fit and habitable and to comply with health and safety codes continues; you may enter for repairs or alterations only on at least 24 hours' notice and at reasonable hours (except in an emergency or where notice is impracticable); and if you willfully interrupt running water, electricity, gas or hot water, the tenant may recover possession or end the lease and recover actual damages. A form the tenant signs is itself an agreement concerning use and occupancy of the unit, which the Act treats as a rental agreement, so a waiver of the Act's rights or remedies in it is very likely unenforceable (no Guam case on a later separate writing was searched). Practical step: keep a move-out form to the move-out date, the return of keys and a forwarding address (which you will need for the deposit accounting and for any notice about property left behind); put any new agreement, such as using the deposit as last month's rent, in a separate writing the tenant is free to decline.

title: The Notices Clause in Guam
bodyText:
The library's Notices clause (`notices`) works in Guam as written: it sends notices to the addresses in the lease and lets any method Guam law requires control.

Guam's Rental Act fixes when a notice is received. A notice to the tenant is received when it is handed to the tenant personally or mailed by registered or certified mail to the tenant's known residence; a notice to you is received when it is delivered at your place of business or at the place where the lease was signed.

Because most of the Act's periods run from receipt and are counted in working days (weekends and federal and Guam government holidays excluded), the date of receipt matters: keep the certified-mail receipt or a signed acknowledgment.

Notices before an unlawful-detainer case are served as the eviction chapter provides (`edu-notice-delivery-gu`); e-mail or text can be agreed only as a courtesy copy (`electronic-notice-ma`, `edu-actual-notice-method-gu`).

Practical step: name in the lease a Guam place of business where the tenant's notices will reach you or your manager (the optional `landlord-notice-address-gu` clause), and ask the tenant for a forwarding address at move-out.

title: Where Guam Law Lets Your Lease Decide
bodyText: Several Guam rules turn on what the lease says; a silent lease takes the default. (1) Rent is due at the time and place the parties agree; with no agreement, the old hiring law makes rent payable at the end of each rental period, so the lease should say rent is due in advance. (2) A hiring with no stated term is presumed to run for the rent period, monthly if nothing is agreed. (3) The tenant's duty to tell you of an absence of more than seven working days, and your remedy if the tenant willfully fails to, exist only if the lease requires the notice (`extended-absence-notice-gu`). (4) A month-to-month change of terms on seven days' notice instead of thirty needs a written agreement made when the tenancy is created (`term-change-notice-gu`). (5) The deposit can serve as last month's rent only by your written agreement (`deposit-last-month-rent-gu`). (6) The tenant may take on maintenance or repair duties only by a good-faith agreement (`tenant-repair-agreement-gu`), and may repair and deduct only with your written consent (`designated-repairer-gu`), apart from the Act's essential-services and weatherhead rules, which a lease can't remove. (7) A covenant against assigning or subletting is enforced by the eviction chapter only if the lease contains one. (8) Attorney's fees by contract are always mutual (`attorney-fees-gu`); interest above 6% needs a written contract (`interest-on-unpaid-amounts-gu`). (9) A cannabis ban binds medical patients' home growing only if you prohibit it (`cannabis-restrictions-ak`). The lease can't waive any Act right; don't use it to shorten the Act's notice and cure periods either (the noncompliance notice's 'unless otherwise agreed in writing' (21 GCA § 48401(a)) wording might allow a different period, but a shorter one risks the waiver bar, and no Guam case was searched).

title: Landlord Size Thresholds in Guam
bodyText: Guam's Rental Act has no small-landlord exemption and no duties tiered by how many units you own: it applies to every residential rental agreement for a dwelling unit in Guam. Size matters in four other places. (1) Guam's housing-discrimination article does not apply to a single-family house rented by a private individual who owns no more than three such houses, but only if the house is rented without any broker, agent or rental service and without a discriminatory advertisement or notice; nor to rooms or units in a building of no more than four families where you live in one of them. Every condition must be met; and the federal Fair Housing Act has its own, separate exemptions. (2) The source-of-income article (in force October 1, 2026) has no size exemption at all: only publicly subsidized housing projects and Chamorro Land Trust leases are exempt. (3) The annual service license fee for renting is $10 if you rent no more than one family residential unit, and the greater of $25 or $5 per unit if you rent several. (4) If your building has four units or fewer, you may skip the mandatory garbage subscription if the lease obligates the tenant to subscribe (`garbage-subscription-gu`).

title: No Renter's-Insurance Statute
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library regulates a residential lease's renter's-insurance requirement: none lets the tenant choose the carrier by statute, governs force-placed coverage or an administrative fee for it, or requires a written advisory that you do not insure the tenant's belongings.

You may require renter's insurance as a lease term (Guam uses `tenants-property-insurance-ks-oh-ca`).

Three Guam rules shape how you do it. First, any money the tenant pays to you or for your benefit under the lease is rent, so if you buy coverage for the tenant and bill for it, that charge is rent, and at lease commencement you may collect only the first month's rent and the security deposit (with any pet deposit); on move-in day you may collect only the first month's insurance charge, as part of the first month's rent, and nothing for later months or any separate set-up fee.

Second, a fixed charge for failing to show proof of coverage is a sum set in advance for a breach, void unless actual damage would be impracticable or extremely difficult to fix.

Third, the policy cannot shift your own repair duties or your liability for negligence onto the tenant (see `edu-tenants-property-insurance-gu`).

Practical step: require coverage, let the tenant pick the insurer, and ask for proof at move-in and renewal.

title: Renter's Insurance and Your Repair Duties
bodyText:
Guam uses the library's renter's-insurance clause without a liability disclaimer (`tenants-property-insurance-ks-oh-ca`): it says your insurance does not cover the tenant's belongings and requires the tenant to carry renter's insurance with a liability minimum you choose.

Guam does not use the shared clause that adds an unqualified "Landlord is not liable" disclaimer, because Guam contract law treats a term exempting anyone from responsibility for fraud, willful injury or violation of law (willful or negligent) as against public policy, and the Rental Act bars any waiver of the tenant's rights, which include your duties to comply with health and safety codes and to make the repairs needed to keep the unit fit and habitable.

No Guam provision searched for this library expressly forbids pushing your repairs onto the tenant's insurance, but the same two rules stop a lease from doing it (apart from a separate good-faith agreement that the tenant will perform repair duties, which the Rental Act allows): the tenant's policy protects the tenant; it does not take over your repair duties or your liability for your own negligence.

The tenant remains responsible for damage the tenant, family or guests cause deliberately or negligently.

Practical step: require proof of coverage, and handle damage claims through the Rental Act's repair and deposit rules rather than through the tenant's insurer.

title: Selling the Property or Changing Managers
bodyText:
Selling a rented home in Guam does not end the lease: the buyer steps into your place, gets your remedies for rent and for breaches of the lease, and the tenant keeps the tenant's remedies against the buyer.

To be relieved of liability under the lease and the Rental Act you must give the tenant written notice of a good-faith sale to a bona fide purchaser; you stay liable for the recoverable deposit unless the buyer is credited with it and everyone is notified (`edu-security-deposit-on-sale-gu`).

A manager is relieved after written notice to the tenant that its management has ended, unless otherwise agreed.

Before the sale, the tenant may not unreasonably refuse entry to show the unit to prospective buyers or lenders, on at least 24 hours' notice and at reasonable hours.

A lease for more than one year that is not recorded can be defeated by a good-faith buyer or mortgagee who records first (`edu-lease-term-limits-gu`).

A tenant's promise to recognize a stranger as landlord is void without your consent or a judgment, and the tenant must pass on to you any legal papers about the property (`edu-tenant-forward-proceedings-gu`). For a lender's foreclosure, see `edu-foreclosure-tenant-rights-gu`.

No Guam provision searched for this library lets you end a fixed term because you sell; if you want that right, the lease must reserve it (the optional `sale-termination-gu`).

Practical step: send each tenant a written notice, delivered personally or by registered or certified mail, naming the new owner or manager and where to pay rent from what date.

title: Severability in Guam
bodyText:
The library's severability clause (`severability`) works in Guam as written.

Guam's rules on improper lease terms mostly strike the offending term and leave the rest: a lease provision the Rental Act prohibits, including any waiver of the tenant's rights or remedies under the Act, is unenforceable on its own; a sum fixed in advance as damages for a breach is void only "to that extent" unless actual damage would be impracticable or extremely difficult to fix; and where a contract has several distinct objects, an unlawful one is void and the rest stands.

A severability clause cannot save a lease that fails as a whole. Guam law voids an entire contract whose single object is unlawful; makes a lease for longer than one year invalid unless it is in writing and signed by the party to be bound; and voids a lease of a married couple's community or jointly owned property signed by one spouse alone when the term with options may exceed five years or is indefinite.

Practical step: don't rely on severability to rescue a risky term; draft each term to comply, and have every owner sign.

title: When a Guam Lease Must Be in Writing
bodyText: Guam's statute of frauds makes an agreement to lease real property for longer than one year invalid unless the lease, or a note or memorandum of it, is in writing and signed by the party to be bound; if an agent signs for that party, the agent's authority must also be in writing and signed by the party. Guam's evidence code repeats that rule and adds that an interest in real property, other than a lease for a term of one year or less, can be assigned or surrendered (other than by operation of law) only by a writing signed by the party or by an agent with written authority, so an assignment or agreed early surrender of a longer lease belongs in a signed writing too. A lease of one year or less may be oral, and the Rental Act covers oral rental agreements too (it defines a rental agreement as one "written or not"). Oral leases of a primary residence carry extra limits in Guam: a 5% yearly cap on rent increases, a one-year initial period during which eviction is allowed only for nonpayment or damage, and, after that year, 90 days' notice of eviction except for nonpayment or damage; a written lease signed by both parties avoids all of them. Once a lease is in writing, it replaces the earlier negotiations, and it can be changed only by another writing or by an oral agreement that has been fully carried out. Guam's electronic-transactions law lets an electronic record and signature satisfy a writing and signature requirement where both parties have agreed to deal electronically. Practical step: put every residential lease in writing, signed by all tenants and by the owner or an agent with written authority, and put every change in a signed writing.

title: Statutory Forms and Prescribed Text in Guam
bodyText: Guam supplies no statutory lease form and prescribes no verbatim text for the lease itself; the Rental Act sets rules for what a lease may and may not say, not its wording. Verbatim or prescribed text appears only in side documents. (1) If a tenant's rent check bounces and you want Guam's bad-check remedies, your written demand (delivered personally or by certified mail) must give the tenant 30 days to pay and, to claim treble damages or the statutory attorney's fees, must contain the statements the bad-check sections set out, in capital, bold or other conspicuous type (`returned-payments-gu`). (2) Small claims cases, including rent and deposit disputes up to $10,000, start on the simple complaint form approved by the Judicial Council. (3) The Superior Court's Rules Governing Protection Order Cases prescribe the forms for those cases (POR Forms 1-5; an applicant asks for an order of protection on the petition, POR Form 1, filed with POR Form 2 and a case coversheet, POR 3(a)(1)), and the order the court issues is among the documents a family-violence victim may give you to end a lease under the Safe Housing Act (`edu-dv-qualifying-documents-gu`). (4) If you rent an accessory dwelling unit, the owner's covenant is recorded on a Department of Land Management form, and a short-term vacation rental certificate is applied for on a form the Department of Revenue and Taxation specifies. No Guam form exists for a notice to quit or an unlawful-detainer complaint; those follow the eviction chapter and the civil rules (`edu-eviction-process-gu`).

title: Tenant Portals and Electronic Documents
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library regulates a landlord's online tenant portal or bars requiring rent or signatures to go through one. Rent is payable at the time and place the parties agree, so the lease may name a portal as a way to pay (`edu-payment-methods-gu`). Guam's electronic-transactions law sets the limits on using a portal for documents. It applies only between parties who have each agreed to deal electronically; a party who agreed may still refuse to conduct other transactions electronically, and that right cannot be waived, so a lease term requiring every future signature or notice to go through the portal does not bind a tenant who later declines. A required notice must still go by the method the law specifies (personal delivery or registered or certified mail under the Rental Act; the eviction chapter's methods before an eviction), so the portal can carry only a courtesy copy (`edu-notice-delivery-gu`). A record the tenant cannot print or store is not enforceable against the tenant. Any portal or convenience fee the lease has the tenant pay to you is rent, so at move-in you may collect only the first month's share of it, as part of the first month's rent, and no one-time set-up fee; a card fee should be no more than the processor charges (`card-payment-charge-gu`). From October 1, 2026, payment rules cannot disadvantage a tenant whose rent comes from a housing-assistance program (publicly subsidized housing projects and Chamorro Land Trust leases are exempt). Practical step: offer the portal as one option, keep a paper or in-person alternative, and let tenants download every signed document.

title: Tenant Records and Data Security
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires you to keep a rent ledger, give one on request, attach one to a nonpayment notice, or let a tenant inspect your records, and none sets a retention period for tenant files. Several Guam rules still shape your records. (1) Deposit deductions must be itemized in writing with copies of receipts (or estimates if repairs can't be done within 14 working days), and you should keep the Post Office proof of mailing. (2) Information a tenant gives you under the Safe Housing Act (family violence, criminal sexual conduct, stalking) may not be disclosed to a third party unless the tenant consents in writing or the law or a court requires it. (3) If you hold applicants' or tenants' names together with unencrypted, unredacted Social Security, driver's license or Guam ID numbers, or financial account or card numbers with the code or password that opens the account, in computerized form, Guam's breach-notification law requires you to tell affected Guam residents without unreasonable delay after a breach that you reasonably believe has caused or will cause identity theft or fraud; the Attorney General enforces it, with penalties up to $150,000. (4) The Social Security Number Confidentiality Act bars any private entity from publicly displaying an SSN, printing it on mailed materials (applications and forms excepted), or requiring it to be sent over an unsecured internet connection. Guam does not require a written information-security program. Practical step: keep a ledger anyway, collect SSNs only through a secure channel, and store them encrypted.

title: No Sunset on Guam Tenant Protections
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library puts a Guam tenant-protection law on a repeal clock. The Guam Landlord and Tenant Rental Act of 2018 (21 GCA Chapter 48), including the Safe Housing Act article added in 2020 and the weatherhead-repair section added in 2024, has no expiry date; the source-of-income article took effect on October 1, 2026 and also has no end date. The time-limited Guam rules that do exist are emergency measures, not sunsets: after a qualifying disaster (serious damage to 500 or more homes, a typhoon with sustained winds of 100 miles per hour or more, or an earthquake over 7.0 on Guam), the Governor may freeze residential rents by executive order at the pre-disaster level for up to 120 days, and the freeze may not be extended; and a one-time temporary business license to rent a dwelling unit lasts no more than one year. Practical step: no action is needed for a sunset; check for any Governor's executive order after a typhoon before raising rent (see `edu-rent-escalation-gu`).

title: No Lease Translation Requirement
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a private landlord to translate a lease or a landlord notice, even when the tenancy was advertised or negotiated in another language, and no Guam rule prescribes lease text in more than one language. English and Chamorro are Guam's official languages, and where an English and a Chamorro version of a law or public document differ materially, the English version binds; that rule governs laws and public documents, not private leases. One related rule applies if you house temporary foreign (H-2) workers as their employer: the employment contract filed with the Department of Labor must be provided in English and in the worker's language of literacy, with a certification of translation; that duty attaches to the employment contract, not to a lease. Practical step: if a tenant reads another language better than English (Chamorro, Chuukese, Tagalog, Korean, Japanese, Chinese and others are common on Guam), offer a translation as a courtesy and state in the lease that the English version controls, so that a dispute over the meaning of a term is decided on one text.

title: Which Guam Notices Must Be in Writing
bodyText: Guam law requires most landlord-tenant notices to be written. Your written notices include: the deposit-retention statement with itemized costs (within 14 working days after the tenancy ends); notice of a sale or of the end of a manager's role; the Rental Act's breach and nonpayment notices; the 5-working-day notice before you repair tenant damage; a month-to-month change of terms; ending a tenancy at will; and the eviction chapter's 5-day pay-or-quit and 3-day perform-or-quit notices. The tenant's written notices include: notice of your breach; ending the lease when you fail to deliver possession; notice before securing essential services; the 14-working-day notice after vacating for fire or casualty; and a Safe Housing Act termination. A few notices are not stated to be written: your 24 hours' notice of entry, the 30 working days' notice before a new rule takes effect, the tenant's report of a defect, a periodic tenant's notice to quit, and the eviction chapter's 5-day notice to quit after an unlawful assignment, sublet or waste; a tenant may report weatherhead damage orally or in writing. Practical step: give every notice in writing anyway, delivered personally or by registered or certified mail, and the eviction chapter's notices by one of its own service methods (personal delivery satisfies both) (`edu-notice-delivery-gu`), and keep proof of delivery; the Act's periods run in working days (weekends and federal and Guam government holidays excluded), counted from the event each section names (often receipt of the notice; for the deposit, the end of the rental agreement).

title: No Landlord Entry to Care for Animals
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library gives you a special right to enter a rental to feed, check on or remove a tenant's animal, and none sets a procedure for taking custody of an animal a tenant leaves behind. The Rental Act's entry rule is a closed list: the tenant may not unreasonably refuse entry to inspect, repair, supply agreed services or show the unit, on at least 24 hours' notice (no notice needed in an emergency or where notice is impracticable); otherwise you have no right of entry except by court order, when the tenant appears to have abandoned the unit, or during an extended absence (more than seven working days) for inspection, maintenance and safe-keeping. An animal in obvious distress may make an emergency, but only for a purpose the Act allows. Intentionally, knowingly or recklessly leaving a domestic animal without minimum care is the offense of animal abandonment for whoever leaves it (a violation, not a crime, with a fine of up to $500), and the Department of Agriculture's Animal Control Division and the police enforce the animal-welfare laws; a peace officer may enter under exigent circumstances to impound an abused animal. Practical step: ask each pet-owning tenant for an emergency contact who can care for the animal, get the tenant's consent by phone or in writing when the need arises, and call Animal Control rather than removing an animal yourself; don't sell or donate an animal under the abandoned-property rules. The library does not offer a lease clause giving you or a tenant-named caretaker standing entry for animal care (see the notes).

title: Service and Assistance Animals in Guam Rentals
bodyText:
Guam uses the library's service and assistance animal clause (`assistance-animal-accommodation`), which rests on the federal Fair Housing Act; Guam's own rules are narrower.

Guam's only housing-specific animal right is old: a totally or partially blind person may be accompanied by a trained guide dog in any housing accommodation offered for rent, without an extra charge, but is liable for any damage the dog does; the rule excludes a single-family home whose occupants rent out no more than one room, and it states no direct-threat exception.

The same chapter also says it does not require a landlord who refuses tenants with dogs to accept a blind or physically disabled tenant who has a dog, including a guide dog; that sentence and the guide-dog right pull against each other, and the federal reasonable-accommodation duty governs in practice.

Guam's service-animal chapter mostly restates federal public-accommodation rules (two permitted questions, no documentation demands, no extra fees, removal only if the animal is out of control or a direct threat); those limits govern businesses open to the public, not your lease. For housing that chapter only notes that the Fair Housing Act lets a person keep a service dog under a "no pets" policy, and it directs GHURA, not private landlords, to adopt HUD's assistance-animal guidance for its own units.

Guam defines animal assistance broadly (therapy and emotional-support uses included) but gives emotional-support animals no separate housing right; that comes only from federal law. Misrepresenting an animal as a service animal is a Guam crime (`edu-service-animal-misrepresentation-gu`).

Practical step: follow the federal reasonable-accommodation rules for every assistance animal, charge no pet deposit or pet rent for one, and never charge for a blind tenant's guide dog (`edu-disability-accommodation-gu`).

title: Penalties for Refusing a Guide or Service Animal
bodyText: Guam has one landlord-facing criminal penalty in this area. Anyone who denies or interferes with the rights of a totally or partially blind or other disabled person under Guam's access rules, which include full and equal access to housing offered for rent and a blind person's right to keep a trained guide dog without an extra charge, is guilty of a misdemeanor. So charging a pet deposit or pet rent for a blind tenant's guide dog risks a criminal charge as well as federal fair-housing liability. Refusing a blind applicant because of a guide dog is risky too, though the same chapter says it does not require a landlord who refuses all tenants with dogs to accept a disabled tenant who has a dog, including a guide dog; no Guam case reconciling the two was searched (no case-law corpus), and federal law requires a reasonable accommodation regardless. Guam's other service-animal penalties are aimed at places of public accommodation: refusing access, or charging a fee for access, to a person using a service dog is a misdemeanor, and the chapter adopts fines of $1,000, $2,000 and $5,000. Guam's definition (businesses that serve the public, including any place offering lodgings to the public) doesn't say whether a private rental home is covered; a rental office or other area you open to the public is the likelier fit, and no Guam case deciding the point was searched (no case-law corpus). Separately, anyone who willfully harasses, obstructs or harms a service, therapy or working dog in its work commits a crime. Practical step: treat every request to keep an assistance animal under the federal reasonable-accommodation rules, and never charge for one (`edu-assistance-animals-gu`).

title: Misrepresenting a Service Animal Is a Crime in Guam
bodyText: Guam makes it unlawful for anyone to fraudulently misrepresent an animal as a service animal or a service animal in training. Knowingly misrepresenting it out loud, or putting a false or improper identification tag, special guide, service or hearing dog tag, or license tag on a dog, is a misdemeanor, with fines of $1,000 for a first offense, $2,000 for a second and $5,000 after that. The rule's words are not limited to particular places, so on its words it reaches a misrepresentation made to you as a landlord as well as one made to a business, though the section opens with the federal public-accommodation rule and no Guam case deciding its reach was searched (no case-law corpus). It covers service animals, not emotional-support animals, which under federal fair-housing law can be a reasonable accommodation without being service animals; a tenant who honestly asks for an emotional-support animal is not misrepresenting anything. Practical step: don't accuse a tenant or demand certificates; evaluate the request under the federal reasonable-accommodation rules (`edu-assistance-animals-gu`), and if you have evidence of a fake service-animal claim, report it to the police rather than acting on it yourself.

title: No Pet and Eviction Fact Sheet
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires you to give a tenant a government fact sheet on pets and eviction, or any other pet disclosure, when you know the tenant has a dog or cat. The only Rental Act rule about pets is the separate pet deposit (`edu-pet-fees-gu`). What happens to a pet when a tenancy ends is governed by the general rules: you may recover possession only through the court (`edu-eviction-process-gu`); you have no right to enter to remove a pet (`edu-no-animal-care-entry-right-gu`); and intentionally, knowingly or recklessly leaving a domestic animal without minimum care is the offense of animal abandonment for whoever leaves it (a violation, not a crime, with a fine of up to $500) (9 GCA § 70.50). Practical step: when a pet-owning tenant is leaving or being evicted, remind the tenant in writing to take the animal, and contact the Department of Agriculture's Animal Control Division if an animal is left behind.

title: Pet Deposits, Pet Rent and Pet Fees
bodyText:
Guam's Rental Act lets you charge a reasonable pet deposit of no more than $500 per pet, in addition to the security deposit (which is capped at one month's rent).

Because the Act lists the pet deposit with the security deposit in its move-in limit, treat it as deposit money: hold it, use it only for the deposit's purposes (pet damage beyond normal wear and tear, cleaning, unpaid rent), and account for it in writing with itemized receipts within 14 working days after the tenancy ends (`security-deposit-return-gu`).

Pet rent is rent, because the Act defines rent as every payment to you under the rental agreement; that also means a one-time "pet fee" is rent, not a deposit. At lease commencement you may collect only the first month's rent (including any first-month pet rent) and the security deposit with any pet deposit, so a non-refundable pet fee cannot be collected on move-in day (`edu-move-in-money-gu`).

A fixed pet-damage charge set in advance is liquidated damages and is void unless actual damage would be impracticable or extremely difficult to fix; charge actual repair costs instead.

Never charge a pet deposit, pet rent or pet fee for an assistance animal, and never an extra charge for a blind tenant's guide dog (`edu-assistance-animals-gu`). Guam uses the library's pet clause `pet-policy-or`.

title: No Pet Insurance Statute
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library regulates a lease term requiring a pet owner to carry liability insurance.

Guam's pet-control law makes a pet owner liable for injury or damage the pet causes to the extent the owner's negligence was the proximate cause, which is the risk pet-liability coverage insures.

Requiring renter's insurance with pet-liability coverage is a contract term you may include; Guam uses the library's clause as written (`pet-insurance-requirement`), which exempts assistance animals in line with federal fair-housing law.

Two limits apply. The premium is the tenant's own expense paid to the insurer, not a charge to you; if you bill the tenant for coverage you buy, that charge is rent, so on move-in day you may collect only the first month's share of it, as part of the first month's rent, and nothing for later months or any separate set-up fee. And the requirement cannot be used to excuse your own negligence or shift your repair duties (`edu-tenants-property-insurance-gu`).

Practical step: ask for proof of coverage when you approve the pet and at renewal.

title: Pet Rules in a Guam Lease
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires you to allow pets or gives any group of tenants (seniors included) a right to keep one, so a lease may ban pets or allow only approved ones.

Guam uses the library's pet clause `pet-policy-or`: approved pets only, pet rent stated as Rent, any pet deposit treated as deposit money, the tenant responsible for pet damage and nuisance, and an indemnity that excludes your own negligence or willful misconduct.

Guam does not use the shared clause that lets the landlord enter to remove a pet, because the Rental Act's entry rule is a closed list with no such purpose, and Guam contract law won't let a lease exempt you from responsibility for your own fraud, willful injury to person or property, or violation of law, whether willful or negligent.

To make a tenant remove a pet that breaks the lease, give the Act's written noncompliance notice (`default-by-tenant-gu`) and, if needed, go to court; don't seize the animal.

Guam's pet-control law adds owner duties a pet clause can point to: every dog or cat over three months must be licensed and wear its license tag, a license issues only on proof of rabies vaccination, and a pet owner is liable for injury or damage the pet causes to the extent of the owner's negligence. That law treats anyone who knowingly lets a pet stay on premises the person occupies as a pet owner, which matters if you live on the property.

Pet deposits are capped at $500 per pet (`edu-pet-fees-gu`), and assistance animals are not pets (`edu-assistance-animals-gu`).

title: Towing From Rental Property in Guam
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires signs (other than the accessible-space sign in (3) below), a written tow authorization or other preconditions before a landlord has a vehicle towed from rental property, and none bars kickbacks from tow companies.

Three sets of rules still apply.
- (1) Abandoned vehicles: a vehicle left on private property for more than 24 hours without the express or implied consent of the owner or the person in lawful possession or control of the property may be removed by a peace officer or an authorized Department of Public Works employee; in a single-family rental the tenant is normally the person in lawful possession, so the tenant's consent counts.
- (2) The tow-truck law: after any tow, the licensed tow business must report to the police within one hour and notify the vehicle's owners by phone and certified letter within seven days; a tow business or any other person responsible for or authorizing a tow who fails to comply with the owner-notice duty commits a misdemeanor and owes three times the resulting damages plus fees. Tow and storage rates are capped by regulation, and towed vehicles must be stored on licensed lots.
- (3) A vehicle illegally parked in an accessible space on private property made available for public use may be towed at its owner's expense; such a space must be marked by a sign with the wheelchair symbol, a statement that violators will be fined $300 to $500 and the vehicle may be towed, a reference to 16 GCA § 3401.1, and a statement that access aisles must not be blocked.

Never tow a tenant's or occupant's car to make them leave or to collect rent; that would be an unlawful exclusion.

Practical step: put vehicle rules in the lease (`parking-vehicle-rules-ny`), post your rules, use only a licensed tow company, and keep a written record of each tow you authorize.

title: No EV-Charging Right or Duty
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library gives a tenant a right to install or use an electric-vehicle charger, requires you to provide charging, or limits a lease's charging rules. Whether a tenant may charge an EV at the property is a lease matter. If you are willing to allow a tenant-installed charger, Guam uses the optional clause `ev-charger-installation-hi` (`edu-ev-charging-requirements-gu`). Guam rules that touch charging arrangements: any electricity reimbursement or charging fee paid to you is rent; any money you hold as security for a charger counts toward the one-month deposit cap and can't be collected at move-in beyond that cap; a charger installed in a condominium must comply with the association's declaration and bylaws, which bind tenants; and installation must follow the building and electrical codes and permits.

title: Tenant EV Charger Installation in Guam
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library sets requirements for a tenant's installation of an electric-vehicle charger (contractor licensing duties, insurance, association approval or cost-sharing under a landlord-tenant law).

If you are willing to allow one, Guam uses the library's optional clause `ev-charger-installation-hi`: your prior written consent to the specific system and location; installation by a licensed contractor under your specifications, the codes and any permits; compliance with condominium or association rules, which bind tenants; optional liability insurance; reimbursement of the electricity used; and an end-of-tenancy choice between removal and leaving the system.

Under Guam law, the electricity reimbursement is rent, and any money you hold to secure the system is part of the security deposit and counts toward its one-month cap. Don't charge an installation or review fee at lease commencement; only the first month's rent and the deposit may be collected then.

title: EV Chargers at the End of a Guam Tenancy
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library says what happens to a tenant-installed electric-vehicle charger when the tenancy ends. The lease decides; the optional clause `ev-charger-installation-hi` lets you choose in advance between removal with repair of any damage and leaving the system in place as your property. If the lease is silent, Guam's general fixture rule applies: a tenant may remove, during the term, anything affixed for trade, ornament or domestic use if it can be removed without injury to the premises, unless the way it was attached has made it an integral part of the premises. Damage from removal is the tenant's responsibility and may be deducted from the deposit with itemized receipts. Practical step: settle removal or surrender in writing before installation, and inspect the installation at move-out.

title: Shared EV Charging Areas
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library regulates electric-vehicle charging in a building's shared parking areas: none requires you to provide shared chargers, sets how their cost is shared, or limits rules for their use.
