If you provide shared charging, set the terms in the lease or in written rules. A rule adopted after a tenant signs binds that tenant without consent only if it promotes tenants' safety and welfare or preserves the property from deliberate abuse, applies fairly to all tenants, does not evade your obligations, and is announced at least 30 working days before it takes effect (`rules-gu`). A charging fee you collect is rent, so at move-in you may collect only the first month's share of it, as part of the first month's rent, and no separate set-up fee. In a condominium, the association's declaration and bylaws bind tenants. Guam does not use the shared clause modeled on Colorado's shared-charging statute (`ev-charging-shared-area-co`).

title: Assigned Parking Spaces in Guam
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library deals with assigned parking spaces in a residential lease: none requires you to assign a space, limits reassigning one, or sets a charge.

Guam uses the library's clause `assigned-parking-space` as written, which lets you reassign a comparable space on reasonable notice.

Two Guam rules sit behind it. If you change a space assignment by adopting a new rule during the lease, the rule binds the tenant without consent only if it meets the Rental Act's four criteria, including at least 30 working days' notice (`edu-parking-rules-notice-gu`). And in a condominium, the association's declaration and bylaws, including any limited-common-element parking assignments, bind your tenant.

Zoning requires at least one off-street space for each dwelling unit, which is a building-permit rule rather than a tenant right.

title: Parking Terms in a Guam Lease
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library regulates parking in a residential lease, so where and how a tenant may park is a lease and rules matter.

Guam uses the library's parking clause without a liability disclaimer (`parking-ks-oh-ca`), which limits parking to designated areas and says you provide no security for the parking area, and Guam's vehicle-rules clause (`parking-vehicle-rules-ny`).

Guam does not use the shared parking clause with an unqualified "Landlord is not liable" disclaimer, because Guam contract law won't enforce a term excusing your own fraud, willful injury or violation of law, and the Rental Act bars waiving the tenant's rights.

Related Guam rules: zoning requires at least one off-street space for each dwelling unit (one per accessory dwelling unit too); a parking charge you collect is rent, so at move-in you may collect only its first month, as part of the first month's rent, and no separate parking fee or deposit beyond the security deposit cap; new parking rules adopted during the lease need 30 working days' notice and must meet the Act's other criteria (`edu-parking-rules-notice-gu`); and towing is covered in `edu-towing-gu`.

title: Adopting Parking Rules in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library sets a parking-specific rule on delivering parking or towing rules before signing, on a prescribed heading, or on what vehicle information you may demand. The Rental Act's general rules provision governs parking rules. Rules in place when the tenant signs are part of the agreement, so attach or list them in the lease (`rules-gu`, `lease-copy-receipt-hi`). A parking rule you adopt after the tenant signs binds the tenant without the tenant's consent only if all four criteria are met: its purpose is the safety and welfare of tenants or protecting your property from deliberate abuse; it applies to all tenants fairly; it is not meant to evade your obligations; and the tenant gets 30 working days' notice before it takes effect (weekends and federal and Guam government holidays excluded). A rule that fails any criterion needs the tenant's consent. Practical step: deliver new parking rules in writing, personally or by registered or certified mail, at least 30 working days ahead, and keep proof of delivery.

title: No Unbundled-Parking Rule
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires you to rent parking separately from the dwelling (unbundled parking), or forbids it. If you charge separately for a parking space, the charge is rent under the Rental Act's definition (every payment to you under the rental agreement), with two consequences: at lease commencement you may collect only the first month's rent (which may include the first month's parking charge) and the security deposit, so don't take a separate parking deposit or fee on move-in day; and the charge is part of the rent for late-fee and nonpayment purposes, so state it in the lease. Zoning still requires at least one off-street space for each dwelling unit when the building is permitted.

title: Storage Space Rented With a Guam Unit
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library governs a storage space or locker rented with a dwelling or sets up a self-service storage act with lien-and-sale procedures, so apart from the Rental Act's abandoned-property procedure and the apartment-keeper's statutory lien for unpaid rent and charges (public-auction sale after 60 days with published and mailed notice, subject to a long exemption list, and not one to use as self-help, since whether it can be enforced against a residential tenant without a court order is undecided; `edu-landlord-lien-gu`), no Guam law searched lets you sell or dispose of a tenant's stored goods.

Guam uses the library's storage clause without a liability disclaimer (`storage-space-ks-oh-ca`), which assigns the space and bars hazardous, flammable or perishable materials; Guam does not use the shared clause with an unqualified disclaimer, because Guam contract law won't excuse your own fraud, willful injury or violation of law.

A storage space promised with the unit is part of the premises, which the Rental Act defines to include facilities promised for the tenant's use, so the tenant's rights in the unit extend to it.

A separate storage charge is rent. Goods left behind at the end of the tenancy follow the Act's abandoned-property procedure (`abandoned-property-gu`). If you rent warehouse storage space as a separate business, it needs its own service license.

title: Cannabis Rules in a Guam Rental
bodyText:
Adult-use and medical cannabis are both legal under Guam law. The adult-use law lets you restrict cannabis at your rental, and the medical law lets you bar a patient's home growing.

The Guam Cannabis Industry Act says nothing in it stops anyone who owns, occupies or controls private property from prohibiting or regulating the possession, use, display or growing of cannabis there. Its home-grow rules (no more than six plants, inside the residence or a locked enclosed space, out of public view) apply only on property the grower lawfully possesses or with the consent of the person in lawful possession.

A medical patient or caregiver is not authorized to grow at home if the landlord or homeowners' association prohibits it, and may never grow in the common areas of a multi-family complex. No Guam provision searched for this library protects a medical-cannabis patient from a lease restriction on possession or use, so such a restriction appears lawful.

Consuming cannabis openly in public is unlawful, and the Cannabis Control Board's rules list the common areas of apartment buildings, condominiums and other multi-family housing as public places. Cannabis smoke or odor that drifts onto another property is a nuisance, and smoking is regulated under Guam's smoke-free law (`edu-smoking-policy-gu`).

If you want restrictions, use the optional clause `cannabis-restrictions-ak`, choosing smoking or vaping, growing, or possession and use; a growing ban is what removes a medical patient's home-grow right. Federal law still treats cannabis as illegal, which matters in federally assisted housing.

title: Firearms at a Guam Rental
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library protects a tenant's right to keep a firearm in a rental, makes a lease restriction on firearms unenforceable, or bars a rule about firearms in vehicles; but Guam's concealed-carry law shapes what a rule can do.

A carry license does not authorize carrying onto private property where the property owner, lessee or business owner prohibits carrying and the prohibition is posted on the premises; knowingly and willfully violating that is a misdemeanor.

Two limits follow from the same section: a licensee may not be prohibited from carrying or storing a firearm in a vehicle for lawful purposes, and nothing in the statute prohibits a lessee of residential property from carrying a firearm within the lessee's own property with a valid firearm identification.

So a posted no-carry rule fits your common areas, not the tenant's own unit or vehicle; a lease term banning lawful possession inside the unit is a contract term whose enforceability no Guam statute settles.

Guam requires a firearms identification card for lawful possession, and storing a firearm in a locked cabinet or with a trigger lock is treated favourably where a minor gets access. The Organic Act's bill of rights binds Guam's government, not a private lease.

If you want firearm rules, use the optional `firearm-rules-gu` and post any common-area prohibition. The shared `firearm-rules-la` is not used in Guam.

title: Guest Rules in a Guam Lease
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library sets or limits a private landlord's guest rules, so the lease may include reasonable ones; Guam uses the library's clauses `guest-policy` and `guest-policy-day-limit` as written.

Guam law shapes them in four ways.
- The tenant must conduct himself, and require guests and invitees to conduct themselves, so as not to disturb neighbors or other tenants, and must not deliberately or negligently damage the premises or permit any person, guests included, to do so; and a tenant can't end the lease for fire or casualty damage caused by the tenant's family, guests or invitees.
- A guest rule adopted after the tenant signs binds the tenant only if it meets the Rental Act's rule criteria, including 30 working days' notice (`rules-gu`).
- Guest rules can't be used to evict or penalize a victim of family violence, criminal sexual conduct or stalking because of incidents of that violence, and those Safe Housing Act protections can't be waived (`edu-dv-eviction-protection-gu`).
- And letting the unit to paying transient guests is a lodging business that needs its own licenses, with fines of $5,000 and more for operating without them, so a guest clause should not let a tenant take paying short-term guests.

Apply guest rules equally to every household (`edu-permitted-occupants-gu`).

title: No Guest-Stay Limit in Guam Law
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library limits how many days a guest may stay or sets a point at which a guest becomes a tenant or occupant.

A guest-stay limit is a lease term; Guam uses the library's clause `guest-policy-day-limit` as written (14 consecutive days, or 14 days in a rolling six months, without your written consent). Because the clause fixes its own numbers, it does not depend on a later rule; if you change the limit during the lease by adopting a new rule, the rule must meet the Rental Act's criteria, including 30 working days' notice, to bind the tenant without consent.

A guest who overstays is not a tenant unless you accept them as one, and removing someone who claims a right to stay goes through the court, not self-help (`edu-unauthorized-occupants-gu`). Short-term-rental and bed-and-breakfast occupancy limits apply only to licensed transient lodging, not to a tenant's guests.

title: No Guest Access Statute
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library gives a tenant's guests or service providers (caregivers, home-health aides, delivery or repair workers) a statutory right of access to a residential building, bars a landlord from charging for guests, or makes guest access unwaivable. Guests' presence rests on the tenant's right to occupy and the lease's guest terms (`edu-guest-policy-gu`). Two Guam rules still apply: guest rules adopted during the tenancy must meet the Rental Act's rule criteria; and a charge for guests paid to you is rent, so at move-in you may collect only its first month, as part of the first month's rent, and no one-time guest fee. Federal fair-housing law may require you to allow a disabled tenant's live-in aide or caregiver as a reasonable accommodation. Practical step: don't charge guest fees, and handle caregiver requests as accommodation requests (`edu-disability-accommodation-gu`).

title: Use of Common Areas in Guam
bodyText:
Guam uses the library's clause on use of the property and common areas (`common-area-use`) as written.

The Rental Act defines common areas as areas shared with others in the same building, such as a pool, playground or laundry, and counts facilities promised for the tenant's use as part of the premises. The tenant must use common areas, and the power and water you provide, in a reasonable manner and dispose of garbage from the common areas the tenant uses in a clean and safe way.

Rules for common areas are landlord rules: one adopted after the tenant signs binds the tenant without consent only if it promotes safety and welfare or protects the property from deliberate abuse, applies fairly to everyone, does not evade your duties, and comes with 30 working days' notice (`rules-gu`). In a condominium, the association's declaration and bylaws bind your tenant too.

No Guam provision searched for this library protects a tenant's flotation bed, clothesline or drying rack, or a flag display, against a lease rule. Medical cannabis may never be grown in the common areas of a multi-family complex, and cannabis may not be consumed openly there (`edu-cannabis-gu`).

title: Grills and Open Flames at a Guam Rental
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library sets a grill-distance or balcony-cooking rule for a private dwelling that differs from the library's clause, so Guam uses `fire-safety-grilling` as written (no barbecue, grill or other open-flame device on a porch or balcony or within 15 feet of a building; no hazardous flammables beyond normal household use).

Guam has adopted the International Fire Code (2009 edition, with later amendments), whose open-flame section governs cooking devices on balconies and near buildings; check it with the Guam Fire Department if your building's layout makes the clause hard to follow.

Guam law separately bans releasing, selling or importing sky lanterns, and Guam's air-pollution rules forbid open burning of combustible material except as the rules allow (some exceptions only on application to and approval by the Administrator), but those rules expressly don't bar barbecue pits, grills or outdoor fireplaces used to cook food, so the grilling limits come from the lease and the fire code.

A no-grilling rule adopted after the tenant signs must meet the Rental Act's rule criteria, including 30 working days' notice (`rules-gu`).

Practical step: keep the clause, and add a designated grilling area if you have a safe one.

title: No Disaster-Displaced Guest Rule
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library lets a tenant house people displaced by a typhoon or other disaster despite the lease's guest or occupancy limits, bars you from enforcing those limits against them, or says when a displaced person's stay in a hotel, short-term rental or tenant's home becomes a tenancy. Ordinary rules apply: your lease's guest and occupancy terms (`edu-guest-policy-gu`, `edu-permitted-occupants-gu`), the tenant's duty to keep guests from disturbing neighbors, and court process to remove anyone who claims a right to stay. Guam's disaster rules point the other way on price: raising rent on the basis of a disaster shortage is an unfair trade practice, and after a disaster seriously damaging 500 or more permanent residential units, a typhoon with sustained winds of 100 mph or more, or an earthquake over 7.0, the Governor may by executive order freeze residential rents at pre-disaster levels for up to 120 days from the date of the disaster (no extension), so don't charge extra because a tenant takes in displaced family (`edu-disaster-duties-gu`). Guam's relocation-assistance law covers people displaced by government acquisition or code enforcement, not by natural disasters. Practical step: after a typhoon, consider giving written consent to temporary guests beyond the usual limit, with an end date.

title: No Crime-Free Lease or Police-Cooperation Statute
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires or regulates a crime-free lease addendum, requires you or your tenants to cooperate with police investigations, requires you to give police information about tenants or access to their units, or bars a lease penalty for calling the police or emergency services. One general duty can reach you: physicians, undertakers, embalmers "and other persons" must promptly notify the Office of Post-Mortem Examinations of deaths that come to their attention and that the Office investigates (violent, sudden or suspicious deaths, among others), and in an apparent homicide or suicide, or an accidental death of unclear cause, the scene may not be disturbed until law enforcement authorizes it. So if a tenant is found dead in a unit, call the police at once and leave the unit as it is (10 GCA §§ 81104, 81107(a)). Guam's child-abuse and elder-abuse reporting duties fall on people who deal with children or elderly adults in their work, though anyone may report (19 GCA §§ 13201, 13202; 10 GCA § 21003). Criminal activity is handled as an ordinary lease breach (`edu-criminal-activity-gu`), and general nuisance law applies (`edu-nuisance-gu`). Guam's Safe Housing Act sets the one firm limit: you may not evict a victim of family violence, criminal sexual conduct or stalking based on incidents of that violence, or end, refuse to renew or refuse a lease, or retaliate, solely because someone in the household is such a victim, and these protections can't be waived. So a lease must not count police or emergency calls about such violence against a tenant. Your entry rights don't expand for police: officers enter a tenant's unit with the tenant's consent, a warrant or other lawful authority, not on your permission (`edu-landlord-entry-gu`). Practical step: don't use "nuisance call" or police-call penalties; enforce actual lease breaches with the Rental Act's notice.

title: No Political Canvassing or Sign Right
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library gives candidates, campaign workers, petition circulators or tenant organizers a right to enter an apartment building or knock on tenants' doors, or gives tenants a statutory right to post political signs that a lease cannot limit. Guam's zoning law allows political signs in residential zones only on private property, set back at least eight feet from the paved roadway and placed so they don't impede traffic or visibility; that permits signs as a land-use matter but does not override a lease. Guam uses the library's clause on use of the property (`common-area-use`), which requires your consent for signs visible from outside but preserves any display the law entitles the tenant to make. The Organic Act's free-speech guarantee binds the government of Guam, not a private landlord. Practical step: if you allow political signs, apply the rule evenly to all viewpoints and require the zoning setback; don't let access rules for canvassers bar tenants from inviting visitors of their choice to their own units.

title: No Portable Cooling-Device Rule
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library gives a tenant a right to install a portable or window air conditioner or other cooling device, requires a lease that restricts them to say so, or requires you to provide air conditioning. In Guam's climate most rentals come with air conditioning, but whether you provide it, and whether a tenant may add a unit, is a lease matter. If you provide air conditioning, it is equipment you should list in the lease (`edu-appliances-included-gu`) and keep working as part of your repair duties where it is needed to keep the unit fit and habitable; Guam's essential-services list (running water, electricity, gas, hot water) does not name air conditioning, though the list is illustrative ("such as"), and no Guam case deciding whether air conditioning is an essential service was searched (no case-law corpus). A unit the tenant installs must not damage the premises, and the tenant uses the power you supply in a reasonable manner. A new rule restricting cooling devices adopted during the lease needs 30 working days' notice and must meet the Rental Act's other rule criteria (`rules-gu`). Old air conditioners can't go in household garbage; Guam's solid-waste rules treat them as special waste.

title: No Tenant Solar Device Right in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library gives a tenant a right to install a plug-in, balcony or portable solar device, limits a landlord's power to forbid one, or voids lease or deed restrictions on solar energy systems. Guam's net-metering law lets a Guam Power Authority customer connect a small renewable system located on the customer's own premises (up to 25 kilowatts for residential customers), but it says nothing about who may decide to install one at a rental. So the lease decides. Guam uses the shared Alterations clause (`no-alterations`), which requires your written consent before the tenant installs equipment; a tenant must not deliberately or negligently damage any part of the premises, and may remove domestic fixtures during the term only if that causes no injury to the premises. If you allow a device, say in writing where it may go, how it is secured against typhoon winds, who pays for wiring work by a licensed electrician, and that it comes out at move-out with any damage repaired.

title: No Recycling Notice Rule in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a landlord to tell tenants where or how to recycle, to provide recycling containers, or to post recycling instructions. What Guam does have: the Guam Solid Waste Authority collects from single-family homes and buildings of four or fewer units, its residential service includes recyclables, and a registered customer who asks gets a separate recycling cart at no additional cost, collected twice a month. Owners of residential buildings must subscribe to garbage collection unless GSWA grants an exemption on petition (renewed yearly): one lets the owner of a building of four or fewer units forgo subscription while the lease obliges the tenant to subscribe (`garbage-subscription-gu`); others cover a contract for weekly collection with a permitted private hauler, a vacant building, a building not expected to generate waste, and registered self-haulers using the transfer stations. Larger buildings use private haulers. Good practice: if you subscribe, tell the tenant the collection day and how to request or use the recycling cart; if the tenant subscribes, tell the tenant that GSWA offers recycling carts on request.

title: Religious and Cultural Displays in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library gives a tenant a right to place religious or cultural items (a mezuzah, a cross, a Santo Niño or other devotional display, holiday decorations) on a door, doorframe, balcony or common area, or limits a landlord's rules about them. Guam's only religious-display statute lets government agencies grant temporary permits for religious groups to display symbols on unused government property around their holidays; it does not reach private rentals. Two rules still apply. Guam's housing-discrimination law makes it unlawful to refuse to rent to anyone because of religion, ancestry or national origin, or to discriminate in the terms, conditions or privileges of a rental, subject to exemptions (for example an owner-occupied building of up to four families, or an owner of no more than three single-family houses renting without a broker or discriminatory advertising), and federal fair-housing law adds similar protections. And any rule you adopt after the lease is signed binds the tenant without consent only if it applies to all tenants in a fair manner and meets Guam's other rule criteria, including 30 working days' prior notice (weekends and federal and Guam government holidays excluded) (`rules-gu`). If you limit decorations, write a neutral rule (size, fire safety, no damage to doors or walls) that treats every faith and culture alike.

title: Smoke From Other Units in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library addresses tobacco smoke drifting between units or lets a lease make a tenant accept drifting smoke or give up claims over it. Don't use a drift waiver: a contract term exempting anyone from responsibility for willful injury or for violating the law is against Guam's public policy, and a lease can't waive the tenant's rights or remedies under the Rental Act, including your duty to keep the premises fit and habitable. What Guam's smoke-free law (the Natasha Protection Act, which covers e-cigarettes) does: it bans smoking in enclosed public places and within 20 feet of their entrances, but a private residence is neither a public place nor a place of employment. It does not name apartment hallways or lobbies; whether they are "public places" is unsettled, and its workplace section (which counts hallways staff frequent) asks employers to provide smoke-free areas and a written smoking policy rather than banning smoking outright. Guam's cannabis rules do count common areas of apartment buildings as public places, and cannabis smoke or odor drifting onto another real property not in the smoker's possession is a nuisance (whether a neighbouring unit in the same building counts is unsettled; no Guam case was searched). You may ban smoking throughout your building: do it in the lease (`edu-smoking-policy-gu`).

title: Snow Removal: Not Applicable in Guam
bodyText: Snow removal does not arise in Guam: the island is tropical and has no snow or ice season, and no Guam provision searched for this library mentions snow. The shared Snow Removal clause is not used for Guam leases. What matters instead is typhoon and storm readiness: say in the lease who secures shutters, clears storm debris from yards and drains, and maintains the landscaping and irrigation, and remember that the Rental Act's fire-and-casualty rules cover typhoon damage that substantially impairs the tenant's enjoyment of the unit (not damage caused by the tenant, family, guests or invitees) (`edu-disaster-duties-gu`).

title: Flags and Signs at Guam Rentals
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library gives a tenant a right to display a flag, a political sign or a religious item against the landlord's wishes, and none bars an association or landlord from restricting them. Guam's zoning law limits exterior signs on property next to a road: in residential and agricultural zones only listed signs are allowed, including one small name sign (up to three square feet) for each family living there, temporary unlighted sale or lease signs, and political signs for candidates or ballot matters, which may be posted only on private property and must stand at least eight feet from the paved roadway without blocking drivers' view. That law doesn't decide whether a tenant or the owner may put a sign on rented property; the lease does. If you restrict flags or signs, do it in the lease or by a rule that meets Guam's rule criteria (including 30 working days' prior notice, weekends and federal and Guam government holidays excluded; `rules-gu`), keep it content-neutral (size, placement, attachment, removal at move-out), and don't single out religion or national origin (`edu-no-religious-display-rule-gu`).

title: Security Cameras and Video Doorbells in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library gives a tenant a right to install a security camera or video doorbell, or regulates landlord or tenant cameras at rentals as such. Guam's criminal privacy law sets the outer limits for everyone. It is a misdemeanor to do any of the following intentionally or knowingly: without consent of the people entitled to privacy, to install or use a device that observes or records in a private place or a place where someone reasonably expects privacy; to install or use a device outside a private place, without that consent, to hear or record sounds from inside it that wouldn't ordinarily be audible outside; to peep into a dwelling's window to spy on the occupant; or to intercept a private message without the sender's or receiver's consent. So a doorbell or camera must not look into another unit or pick up sound from inside it, and no camera belongs inside a tenant's unit or a bathroom. Whether a camera's audio of a conversation in a shared hallway is an unlawful interception is a question for case law, which this library did not search. Use the lease: a camera is equipment needing your consent under the Alterations clause (`no-alterations`); state approved locations, aiming away from neighbors' doors and windows, audio off, and removal and repair at move-out.

title: Barring Non-Tenants From the Property in Guam
bodyText: Guam's criminal trespass law lets you, as owner of the common areas, bar a non-tenant from your property. A person who, knowing he isn't licensed or privileged to be there, enters or remains in a place after notice against trespass has been given (by telling him directly, by posting reasonably likely to come to intruders' attention, or by fencing designed to keep intruders out) commits an offense; it is a petty misdemeanor if he defies an order to leave given personally by the owner, another authorized person or a police officer. Entering or secretly remaining in a dwelling without license is a misdemeanor. Defenses matter: it is a defense that the premises were open to the public and the person followed all lawful conditions, or that he reasonably believed the owner or another person empowered to license access would have let him in. A tenant may invite guests to the unit, so barring a tenant's guest generally needs a specific reason (for example, a non-tenant who commits family violence, criminal sexual conduct or stalking at the premises, against whom the Safe Housing Act expressly preserves your power to obtain a criminal no trespass order). Give the notice in writing, keep a copy, and never use trespass against a tenant: removing a tenant takes an eviction case (`edu-eviction-process-gu`).

title: Waterbeds in Guam Rentals
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library deals with waterbeds or other liquid-filled furniture, so Guam neither protects a tenant's right to one nor sets conditions on it. The lease may forbid or allow them. If you allow one, you may require the tenant to carry insurance covering water damage and to follow installation rules (frame, liner, floor-load limits for upper floors). Don't collect a separate waterbed deposit at move-in: at the start of the lease you may collect only the first month's rent and the security deposit (plus a pet deposit where a pet is allowed), and the security deposit may not exceed one month's rent in total (`edu-move-in-money-gu`, `edu-security-deposit-limit-gu`). Water damage the tenant causes can come out of the deposit after move-out, with the written itemization Guam requires, or be billed as tenant-caused damage (`tenant-caused-damage-gu`).

title: Condominium and Association Information in Guam
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires you to disclose a condominium or homeowners association's obligations or deliver its documents to a tenant, or to make the tenant sign a statement that it knows the condominium law.

Two rules matter. Guam's Horizontal Property Act binds tenants of apartment owners, and anyone else who uses the property, to the Act and to the association's declaration and bylaws, so your tenant must follow them whether or not the lease says so.

And the Act says leases of apartments shall include particulars: the property's description or address with a reference to the recorded declaration, the apartment number, the intended use and use restrictions, the apartment's common interest, and encumbrances. Whether that reaches an ordinary rental hasn't been decided by any case this library searched, so Guam offers a conditional clause with those particulars (`condominium-apartment-particulars-gu`).

Practical step: give the tenant copies of the declaration, bylaws and house rules before signing; a tenant can't comply with rules it has never seen, and the association can enforce them through you.

title: Condominium Associations and Your Rental in Guam
bodyText:
Guam's Horizontal Property Act governs condominiums (horizontal property regimes). It binds tenants of apartment owners to the Act and to the association's declaration and bylaws.

It has no rules on association approval of leases, caps on approval or application fees, association-held tenant deposits, rental bans for later buyers, or limits on what tenant information an association may demand; those come from each regime's recorded documents.

Nor does it let the association collect rent directly from your tenant when you fall behind on common expenses: unpaid assessments are a lien on the apartment, which the association may foreclose like a mortgage, and in that foreclosure the owner must pay a reasonable rental if the bylaws so provide, with a receiver appointed to collect it.

A lease filed with the board may make the lessee count as the owner for purposes the lease provides, such as voting. Communities with a property regime may limit or ban family home occupations, including by rules.

If your regime requires approval of a lease, use the conditional approval clause (`association-approval-la`); any association deposit or fee is the association's, not money you collect at move-in. Keep your own assessments current: a lien foreclosure can bring a receiver collecting rent.

title: Tenants and Association Rules in Guam
bodyText:
Under Guam's Horizontal Property Act, your tenant, the tenant's household and guests are bound by the Act and the association's declaration and bylaws, and each apartment owner must comply strictly with the bylaws, the association's administrative rules and the declaration's covenants; the association may sue for damages or an injunction.

Guam uses the shared Homeowner / Condominium Association Compliance clause (`hoa-compliance`), which makes the tenant follow the association's rules and pay any fine caused by the tenant's violation; passing on a fine the association actually imposed is reimbursement of your actual loss, not a fixed penalty.

No Guam provision searched for this library says you must deliver the rules at signing or that the tenant's duty depends on delivery, or caps association fines; still, give the tenant copies before signing so the duty is fair and provable.

Rules you adopt yourself during the lease still need Guam's rule criteria (`rules-gu`). No Guam provision searched for this library addresses satellite dishes or antennas (federal rules may apply), though Guam's cable-access law limits interference with cable television service (`edu-telecom-access-gu`).

title: No Bed Bug Disclosure Rule in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a landlord to disclose a unit's bed bug history, to give a bed bug information sheet, or to treat on a set timetable. The general rules apply instead: you must keep the premises fit and habitable, the tenant must keep the unit clean and safe and dispose of garbage properly, and both of you have duties toward vermin under Guam's rodent-control law (`edu-bed-bug-cooperation-gu`). Don't hide a known current infestation: under Guam's deceit law, one who willfully deceives another, with intent to induce him to alter his position to his injury or risk, is liable for the damage caused, and deceit includes suppressing a fact one is bound to disclose or giving other information likely to mislead without it (whether a landlord is bound to disclose an infestation was not decided by any Guam case searched). Good practice: tell an applicant in writing about any infestation treated in the last year and how it was treated, and use the optional pest-cooperation clause (`pest-cooperation-pr`).

title: No Defective Drywall Disclosure Rule in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a landlord to disclose defective or corrosive ("Chinese") drywall, or sets any standard for it in rental housing. Guam's only drywall rules are a contractor licence category, quarantine inspection of imported wallboard, and the building law's exemption letting owners do minor non-structural work such as drywall repair without a building-official application. If you know of defective drywall, tell an applicant in writing before signing: Guam's deceit law covers suppressing a fact one is bound to disclose and half-truths likely to mislead, and conditions that affect health and safety also bear on your duty to keep the premises fit and habitable.

title: Submetered Electricity in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a lease disclosure for submetered or landlord-billed electricity, and reselling electricity to tenants does not make you a regulated public utility under Guam's utility-commission law, which defines public utilities as the Guam Power Authority, the Port, Guam Waterworks Authority, the Guam Solid Waste Authority and certain licensed private water, wastewater and marine-terminal operators. What applies is covered elsewhere: charges the lease makes the tenant pay you are rent, your duties if you supply and interrupt electricity, and GPA's master-meter disconnection rule (`edu-utility-interruption-submeter-gu`, `edu-no-submetering-disclosure-rule-gu`, `edu-utility-apportionment-gu`). Good practice: state in the lease that electricity is submetered, how the charge is calculated (your actual GPA cost, no markup), when you read the meter and bill, and give copies of the GPA bills on request.

title: No Flood Disclosure Rule in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a landlord to tell a tenant that a rental is in a flood hazard area or has flooded before, or gives a tenant a termination right for flooding not disclosed. Guam's flood hazard area rules govern development permits in mapped flood hazard areas, not leases, and Guam's new-home flood warranty protects buyers from developers. If the unit is in a mapped flood hazard area or has flooded, say so in writing before signing: Guam's deceit law covers suppressing a fact one is bound to disclose and half-truths likely to mislead. Flood or storm damage not caused by the tenant, the tenant's family, guests or invitees is a casualty under the Rental Act: if it substantially impairs enjoyment of the unit, the tenant may move out at once and end the lease by written notice within 14 working days afterwards (weekends and federal and Guam government holidays excluded), or, if continued occupancy is lawful, stop using the unusable part and pay rent reduced in proportion to the lost rental value (`edu-disaster-duties-gu`). Recommend renter's insurance; standard policies often exclude flood.

title: No Foreclosure Disclosure Rule in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a landlord facing foreclosure to tell a prospective or current tenant, before signing or afterward. What Guam law does say about foreclosure and tenants (removal after a foreclosure sale, receivers collecting rent, rent paid before notice of a transfer) is in `edu-foreclosure-tenant-rights-gu`; federal law gives most tenants time to stay after a foreclosure of residential property. If a foreclosure case has been filed or a sale is scheduled, tell an applicant in writing before signing: a lease that may end soon is a material fact, and Guam's deceit law covers suppressing a fact one is bound to disclose and half-truths likely to mislead.

title: Certificates of Occupancy for Guam Rentals
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires you to give a tenant a copy of the building's certificate of occupancy or to state in the lease that one exists. The building law does make the certificate a condition of using a building: no newly erected building may be occupied until the building official issues a certificate of occupancy and it is posted on the premises, and a building altered so as to change its classification or occupancy needs a new certificate (occupancy may continue during the work but no more than 30 days after completion without one). A building found unsafe must be vacated and not reoccupied until a new certificate issues. Renting a unit with the one-time temporary business licence for dwelling units requires a Certification of Suitability for Occupancy from a Certified Home Inspector, filed with the Department of Revenue and Taxation. Practical step: confirm the unit has a valid certificate (and that a converted garage or added unit was permitted) before you lease it, and keep a copy to show the tenant on request; a unit no one may lawfully occupy can't meet your duty to keep it fit and habitable (`edu-no-condemned-rent-bar-gu`).

title: No Good Cause Notice in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library sets a good-cause or just-cause eviction rule for written leases, so there is no notice telling a tenant whether the unit is covered by one. The one exception is narrow: a verbal or oral lease of a residential unit used as a primary residence (entered after January 1, 1988) runs for an initial year during which the tenant may be evicted only for nonpayment of rent or damage to the premises; after that the landlord must give 90 days' notice of eviction except for nonpayment or damage, may not raise rent more than 5% a year, and may not end the tenancy solely to raise the rent. That rule doesn't apply to written leases or rental agreements signed by both parties, which is one more reason to put every lease in writing and have both sides sign. For written leases the ordinary rules apply: a fixed term ends on its end date, and a periodic tenancy ends on the notice Guam's law requires (`edu-termination-notice-gu`), never solely because someone in the household is a victim of family violence, criminal sexual conduct or stalking, and a victim may never be evicted based on incidents of that violence, though you may still bring an eviction case against a tenant who committed it (`edu-retaliation-gu`).

title: No Contamination Disclosure Rule in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a landlord to disclose hazardous-substance contamination, a brownfield or cleanup status, or recorded environmental use limitations to a tenant, or to write them into a lease. Guam's environmental rules (solid and hazardous waste, underground storage tanks, water quality) regulate owners and operators, not lease content. Two rules still matter: you must keep the premises fit and habitable and comply with building and housing codes on health and safety, and under Guam's deceit law one who willfully deceives another, with intent to induce him to alter his position to his injury or risk, is liable for the damage, deceit including suppressing a fact one is bound to disclose or giving other information likely to mislead without it (whether a landlord is bound to disclose contamination was not decided by any Guam case searched). If you know of contamination on or under the property (fuel tanks, soil or groundwater cleanup, a Guam EPA order), tell an applicant in writing before signing and follow any use limits in the lease's rules.

title: Violation Notices and Unsafe-Building Orders in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires you to disclose outstanding building, zoning or health violation notices or condemnation orders to a prospective tenant. Guam's agencies notify occupants themselves: when the Department of Public Works finds a building unsafe it notifies the owner, occupant and lessee in writing and posts a notice at the main entrance that may not be removed until the building is vacated and repaired or demolished; zoning violation notices go to the owner, occupant and lessee, with ten working days to correct; and a dwelling rented under the one-time temporary business licence loses the licence if a notice of violation isn't corrected within 14 calendar days. Renting a unit under an unsafe-building order or that can't lawfully be occupied puts you in breach of your duty to keep it fit and habitable (`edu-no-condemned-rent-bar-gu`), and hiding a pending order risks liability under Guam's deceit law. Practical step: clear or disclose in writing any open notice before signing.

title: No Landlord Insurance Mandate in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a residential landlord to carry liability or property insurance (other than for an accessory dwelling unit or a short-term vacation rental, below), to register proof of insurance, or to tell the tenant what the landlord's policy covers; the business licence for renting real property has no insurance condition. Three narrower rules exist: an accessory dwelling unit (ADU) must be covered under the homeowner's insurance policy for the main home or under a separate policy, at the homeowner's option; an owner applying to operate a short-term vacation rental must provide proof of property insurance, including any policy for short-term rental use; and commercial leases of Chamorro Land Trust land must require the tenant to carry business liability insurance. Insurance is still prudent: a lease clause can't exempt you from responsibility for your own fraud, willful injury to person or property, or violation of law, whether willful or negligent, or make the tenant give up Rental Act rights and remedies (`edu-exculpatory-clauses-gu`). Your policy doesn't cover the tenant's belongings; Guam uses the library's no-disclaimer renter's insurance clause (`tenants-property-insurance-ks-oh-ca`), which you may use to require the tenant to carry renter's insurance. Typhoon cover deserves particular attention in Guam.

title: Lead-Based Paint Disclosure in Guam
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library sets a lead-paint rule for rentals, so the federal lead-based paint disclosure rule governs Guam rentals of housing built before 1978.

Guam uses the library's shared Lead-Based Paint Disclosure (`lead-based-paint`), which carries the federal Lead Warning Statement; under federal law you give the tenant the federal lead hazard pamphlet, disclose any known lead-based paint or hazards and available reports, and have the disclosure signed before the lease is (federal rules, not Guam law; check the current federal text and its exemptions).

Guam law adds only related rules: lead-free pipes, solder, flux and fittings are required when installing or repairing drinking-water plumbing in a residential facility (leaded joints needed to repair cast-iron pipes excepted), and lead-based paint removal and abatement falls within the Painting and Decorating Contractor (C-33) licence classification.

Renovation that disturbs paint in older housing may also trigger federal work-practice rules. Your duty to keep the premises fit and habitable applies to peeling or chipping paint as to any other hazard.

title: No Lead-Safe Certificate Rule in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a lead-safe certificate, lead clearance report or lead inspection certificate for a rental, or requires one to be attached to the lease. Guam has no lead-safe housing program of its own; the federal disclosure rule (`edu-lead-based-paint-gu`, shared clause `lead-based-paint`) is the only lead requirement tied to leasing, and it requires disclosure of known hazards and available reports, not testing. Federally assisted housing (Section 8 vouchers through GHURA, public housing) has its own federal lead rules.

title: No Guam Lead Notice Beyond Federal Law
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a Guam-specific lead notice, certificate or information packet at lease signing or renewal beyond the federal lead-based paint disclosure (`edu-lead-based-paint-gu`). The only Guam lead notice rule found is for drinking water: owners and operators of public water systems must notify people who may be affected by lead contamination of their drinking water that results from lead in the public distribution system's construction materials or from corrosive water, in the form Guam EPA prescribes. If you receive such a notice for your building's water service, pass it to your tenants promptly and keep a copy.

title: No Meter Conservation Charge Rule in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library creates an energy-efficiency or conservation charge attached to a utility meter that a later occupant must pay, or requires a landlord to tell a new tenant about one or reduce rent because of it. Guam's net-metering and virtual power plant laws give bill credits to customers who host solar systems; they don't put repayment charges on a tenant's bill. If the lease makes the tenant the Guam Power Authority customer, tell the tenant in writing before signing about anything unusual on the account (a solar host credit arrangement, a payment plan you set up, a deposit), and don't leave your own arrears for the tenant to inherit (`utility-transfer-gu`).

title: No Drug Lab Disclosure Rule in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a landlord to disclose that a property was used to make methamphetamine or other drugs, sets decontamination standards, requires reporting a suspected drug lab, or bars occupancy until cleanup. Guam's drug laws are criminal laws aimed at manufacturers and sellers. If you know a unit was used as a drug lab, don't rent it until it has been professionally cleaned and tested, and tell an applicant in writing: you must keep the premises fit and habitable and comply with codes on health and safety, and under Guam's deceit law one who willfully deceives another with intent to induce him to alter his position to his injury or risk is liable for the resulting damage; deceit includes suppressing a fact by one bound to disclose it, or giving other information that is likely to mislead without it. Report suspected drug manufacturing to the Guam Police Department; the library's criminal-activity clause makes drug activity on the property a lease breach (`edu-criminal-activity-gu`).

title: No Military Zone Disclosure Rule in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a landlord to disclose that a rental is near a military installation, airfield or flight path, or within a noise or accident-potential zone, or gives a tenant a right to end the lease for one. Guam's laws on military bases deal with base closures, reuse and contractors. Much of Guam is near Andersen Air Force Base, Naval Base Guam, Marine Corps Base Camp Blaz or the airport, so aircraft noise and training activity are common. If the unit is under a flight path or near a range, mention it in writing before signing; under Guam's deceit law one who willfully deceives another with intent to induce him to alter his position to his injury or risk is liable for the resulting damage, and deceit includes suppressing a fact by one bound to disclose it, or giving other information that is likely to mislead without it.

title: No Mold Disclosure Rule in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a landlord to disclose mold, give a mold information booklet, or meet a mold standard in a rental. Guam does license mold remediation contractors, and its public swimming pool rules require pool hygiene facilities to be kept free of visible mold. In Guam's humid climate mold is a common problem, and it falls under your general duty to keep the premises fit and habitable and to comply with codes on health and safety; the tenant must keep the unit as clean and safe as the premises permit and must not damage it. Good practice: disclose any known mold problem in writing before signing, fix leaks and moisture sources promptly, use a licensed mold remediation contractor for significant growth, and add a lease term asking the tenant to report leaks and visible mold and to run ventilation or air conditioning reasonably.

title: No Ordnance, Demolition or Shared-Meter Disclosure in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a landlord to disclose a former military ordnance or munitions site nearby, a planned demolition of the building, or a utility meter that also serves other units or common areas. Related rules: if the building official finds a building unsafe, the owner, occupants and lessees are notified in writing, a notice is posted at the entrance, and the building must be vacated and repaired or demolished (`edu-no-code-order-disclosure-gu`); and when a utility plans to disconnect a master-metered account it must try to inform the occupants (`edu-utility-apportionment-gu`). Guam has World War II-era unexploded ordnance in places; no statute in the corpus ties it to leasing. Good practice: if you plan to demolish or substantially renovate during the term, or the unit shares a meter, say so in the lease, and tell an applicant about any known ordnance finds on the property.

title: Owner and Manager Identity in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a landlord to disclose the owner's or manager's name and address to the tenant at the start of a tenancy, and none bars an eviction case for failing to. Guam's Rental Act instead ties notices to your place of business: a tenant's notice reaches you when delivered at your place of business or where the lease was signed, so say in the lease where that is (`landlord-notice-address-gu`). Written notice also matters at the end of your role: after a good-faith sale you stay liable under the lease until you give the tenant written notice of the sale (and remain liable for the deposit unless the buyer is credited with it and everyone is notified), and, unless otherwise agreed, a manager stays liable until the tenant gets written notice that the management has ended. Anyone who collects rent for an owner for compensation generally needs a real estate broker's licence (resident managers who live on site are exempt), and renting needs a business licence, without which you can't bring a court case (`edu-landlord-registration-gu`). Good practice: name the owner, any manager and an emergency contact in the lease.

title: Fumigation and Pesticide Notices in Guam
bodyText: Guam's pesticide rules put the notice duty on the pest control company, not the landlord. Before structural fumigation the operator must file a notice of intent with Guam EPA at least two days ahead, give written notice at least two days before the fumigation to each household and business within 75 feet (for a single-owner complex with multiple units, it must inform the owner and the site manager), hold an occupant's fumigation notice signed by the primary occupant or the structure's designated agent (or document its attempts), unless Guam EPA waives the two-day notice in an emergency, and post the notice of intent at the main entrance from at least one hour before until the building is safe to enter. Termite and other soil treatments need their own notice of intent to Guam EPA. No Guam provision searched for this library requires you to give tenants a general pest-control or pesticide notice at signing. Practical steps: when you schedule fumigation, give each tenant written notice with the dates and re-entry instructions as early as you can and at least the 24 hours' notice of entry Guam's Rental Act requires; coordinate the signed occupant notices; and use a licensed pest control operator. If tenants must leave during fumigation, say in the lease who bears the cost of temporary lodging.

title: No Private Well Testing Rule for Guam Rentals
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a landlord to test a private well serving a rental or give the tenant test results. Guam EPA's well rules regulate the owner: no well may be put into operation without a well operating permit, the permit application needs water analyses for individual domestic wells (which include wells serving an apartment house not on a community water system), and repaired wells must be disinfected. Guam Waterworks Authority's rules also require a GWA meter on privately operated water wells. If a rental is served by a private well, keep its permit current, test the water, give the tenant the results in writing before signing, and say in the lease who maintains the well and pump; you must keep the premises fit and habitable, and running water is an essential service under Guam's Rental Act.

title: No Chemical Warning Rule in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a chemical-exposure or cancer warning at rental property, like California's Proposition 65 warning; that California law does not apply in Guam. Guam's only consumer warning of this kind found is the cannabis law's required health warning for cannabis products. Your general duty still applies: keep the premises fit and habitable. Disclosing in writing any known hazard a tenant couldn't discover is good practice; no Guam statute searched for this library requires it, and Guam's deceit law reaches willful deception, including suppressing a fact one is bound to disclose (`edu-no-contamination-disclosure-gu`, `edu-lead-based-paint-gu`).

title: No Property Tax Rent Statement in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a landlord to tell tenants what part of the rent goes to real property tax, annually or when rent changes. Guam's real property tax falls on the owner (on Chamorro Land Trust land, on the Trust's lessee or licensee), not on a residential tenant. If the lease passes a tax increase through to the tenant, that charge is rent under Guam's Rental Act, subject to the rules on rent and rent changes (`edu-tax-escalation-gu`, `edu-rent-tax-gu`).

title: Radon Disclosure in Guam (Sales Only)
bodyText: Guam's radon disclosure law applies to sales, not rentals. When residential real property with a dwelling is sold, the selling broker must tell the buyer in writing that the property may present the potential for exposure to radon (using information Guam EPA develops), and the seller must give the buyer any radon test or inspection results in the seller's possession and notify the buyer of known radon hazards; no testing is required. No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a landlord to give a tenant radon information. The sale rule speaks of a "purchaser of any interest", so if a lease includes an option to buy, the cautious course is to give the radon information and any test results too. Good practice for every rental: if you have radon test results showing elevated levels, tell the tenant in writing.

title: Required Lease Disclosures in Guam
bodyText: Guam requires few lease disclosures. Required or needed when they apply: the federal lead-based paint disclosure for housing built before 1978 (`edu-lead-based-paint-gu`); for a condominium apartment, the particulars Guam's Horizontal Property Act lists for leases of apartments (`condominium-apartment-particulars-gu`, conditional); for an accessory dwelling unit (or the primary dwelling when the owner, a relative or a designated representative lives in the accessory unit), a written rental agreement signed by owner and tenant for at least six months; and, if the owner of a residential building of four or fewer units (or other qualifying building) petitions GSWA for the exemption from garbage subscription on the ground that the lessee is obligated by the lease to subscribe (one of five exemption grounds, renewed annually), the tenant's lease duty to subscribe (`garbage-subscription-gu`). No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a Guam-form first page, a notice of whether a unit is covered by rent or eviction-protection rules (Guam has no rent control or just-cause eviction scheme for written leases; the Article 5 victim protections and any post-disaster rent freeze apply without a lease notice), an owner-identity, flood, mold, bed bug, radon (sales only) or sex-offender disclosure for rentals, or a tenant rights statement. If a licensed real estate broker or salesman gets the tenant's signature on the lease, the licensee must give the tenant a copy at the time of signing. Notices the Rental Act requires arise during the tenancy (entry, deposit itemization, breach and nonpayment notices, sale). Beyond the statutes, under Guam's deceit law one who willfully deceives another with intent to induce him to alter his position to his injury or risk is liable for the resulting damage, and deceit includes suppressing a fact by one bound to disclose it or giving other information likely to mislead without it; disclosing known material defects in writing is the cautious course. A lease with an option to buy where rent is credited in substantial part toward the price is treated as a sale of an interest in land under Guam's consumer credit code; get advice before offering one.

title: No Rights and Responsibilities Guide in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a landlord to give a tenant a government-published rights and responsibilities guide, pamphlet or handbook before signing or at renewal, or to get a signed acknowledgment of one, and no Guam agency is directed by statute to publish one. Giving the tenant a plain summary of the main Rental Act rules (deposit return within 14 working days, 24 hours' notice of entry, how notices are delivered) is optional good practice; working days exclude weekends and federal and Guam government holidays.

title: No Code Variance Notice in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a landlord to give tenants a copy of a health, sanitary or building code variance, or to attach one to the lease. Variances in Guam are granted by agencies for their own programs: zoning variances by the Guam Land Use Commission, and Guam EPA and public-health variances for things like sewage disposal, water systems, pools and food establishments; none is tied to tenant notice. A variance doesn't change your duties under the Rental Act to comply with building and housing codes on health and safety and keep the premises fit and habitable. If a variance affects the unit (for example a sewage-system or height variance), telling the tenant in the lease is good practice.

title: No Sex Offender Registry Notice in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a landlord to tell tenants about registered sex offenders living nearby or to put a registry notice in the lease, and none sets residency restrictions for registrants in private rentals. Guam's Judiciary (Probation Division) runs a public sex offender registry website searchable by name, area and radius, showing each registrant's offenses, photograph and residential address, with a warning that the information should not be used to unlawfully injure, harass or commit a crime against anyone. The one housing rule found: no home may be licensed as a bed and breakfast at the physical address of a registered sex offender. If you screen applicants using the registry, apply the same standard to everyone, follow fair-housing law, and never use registry information to harass.

title: No Single-Family Occupancy Notice in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a single-family home lease to carry an occupancy notice, sets a font size or first-page placement for one, or presumes an occupant lacks lawful occupancy unless the lease is notarized or signed by a licensed manager. To deal with someone living in the unit without right, use the ordinary remedies: a forcible or unlawful detainer case, or a report of criminal trespass (`edu-unauthorized-occupants-gu`, `edu-trespass-notice-gu`). A written lease signed by both parties and naming every occupant is the best evidence of who has the right to be there, and it also keeps Guam's special oral-lease limits from applying.

title: Shoreline Access at Guam Rentals
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a landlord to tell a tenant about public shoreline access next to a rental.

But Guam's Ocean Shore Public Access Law of 1987 binds your tenant directly: it is unlawful for the owner, lessee or tenant of land adjacent to or abutting the ocean shore to block, impede or interfere with the public's use of any traditional right-of-way (a defined term: a road, trail, bull cart road or easement held by Spain at the Treaty of Paris or shown in a map or document of the U.S. Naval Government of Guam, unless finally adjudicated by a court), and any person may sue to stop a violation and, if successful, recover costs and reasonable attorney's fees.

If your property is beside the shore or crossed by a traditional trail or right-of-way, tell the tenant in writing and say in the lease that the tenant must not fence, gate, park on or otherwise block it (optional clause `shoreline-right-of-way-gu`).

title: No Special District Statement in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a lease to state that the property is in a special district or that the tenant knows of district charges or plans. Guam's Improvement District Law lets landowners in a village or area form an improvement district for roads, water, sewer, lighting and similar public facilities; the cost is added as a special assessment on the owner's tax list, and condominium apartments are separately assessed. These charges fall on the owner. If the lease passes any of them to the tenant, that charge is rent under the Rental Act and should be stated in the lease (`edu-tax-escalation-gu`).

title: No Sprinkler Disclosure Rule in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a landlord to tell a tenant whether a rental building has fire sprinklers, or to describe their maintenance in the lease. The explicit sprinkler requirements found are for care homes (automatic smoke detectors, fire alarm systems and an appropriate sprinkler system) and some health facilities; Guam's Waterworks rules govern private fire-protection service connections. Guam has adopted the International Fire Code and the International Building and Residential Codes (2009 editions, as amended), which contain sprinkler provisions for some buildings, and the Rental Act makes you comply with building and housing codes on health and safety; those code texts are not in this library's corpus, so check with the Guam Fire Department what applies (`edu-alarm-duties-gu`). Good practice: if the building has sprinklers, tell the tenant not to hang items from or paint sprinkler heads and to report damage at once.

title: Deaths, Crimes and Stigma at Guam Rentals
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library says whether a landlord must, or need not, disclose that a death, suicide, homicide or other crime occurred on the property, that it is reputed to be haunted, or that a former occupant had HIV or AIDS; Guam has no stigmatized-property statute either requiring or excusing disclosure. Guam's general deceit law applies: suppressing a fact one is bound to disclose, or giving other information that misleads for want of it, is deceit, and so is stating as fact something untrue that you don't believe, or have no reasonable ground to believe, is true; one who willfully deceives another to induce him to act to his injury or risk is liable for the damage. Answer an applicant's direct question truthfully. Don't refer to a former occupant's medical condition: federal fair-housing law treats HIV and AIDS as disabilities (federal law, not read for this library), and Guam's Safe Housing Act bars disclosing to a third party information a tenant gave you under its victim-protection article (family violence, criminal sexual conduct or stalking) unless the tenant consents in writing or the disclosure is required by law or court order (verifying the tenant's evidence is not a disclosure).

title: Renting to Students in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library creates a student-housing regime: no licence, lease certification or special rules for renting to college or university students. Students rent under the Rental Act like anyone else. Two other regimes can reach shared housing. Guam's health law defines a "hotel" to include any lodging house, rooming house or dormitory with four or more guest rooms occupied or meant for four or more guests, whether rent is paid in money, goods or labor; a structure converted to that use must meet the Department of Public Health and Social Services' plan and sanitation requirements. And Guam's hotel occupancy tax applies to transient occupants of a hotel, lodging house or bed and breakfast who stay less than 90 consecutive days. If you rent rooms by the room to several students, check with DPHSS and the Department of Revenue and Taxation whether either applies, and use a written lease, either one per room-renter or one lease that makes all co-tenants jointly and severally liable (`edu-joint-liability-gu`).

title: No Tenant Rights Statement in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a landlord to attach a government statement of tenant rights to the lease, have the tenant sign or acknowledge one, or make it a condition of suing the tenant. The only signed-acknowledgment rule found is for short-term vacation rentals, whose owners must file a form agreement in which occupants agree to follow the short-term rental law and acknowledge occupancy and quiet-hour limits. For ordinary leases, the Rental Act's protections apply whether or not the tenant is told of them, and the lease can't waive them.

title: No Exemption Notice Needed in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a lease statement telling tenants that a property is exempt from rent caps, just-cause eviction rules or a tenant opportunity-to-purchase law, because Guam has none of those for written residential leases (`edu-rent-control-gu`, `edu-no-good-cause-notice-gu`). The narrow rules that exist need no exemption notice: oral leases of a primary residence carry a 5% yearly rent cap and limits on eviction, which don't apply to written leases signed by both parties; after a qualifying disaster the Governor may freeze residential rents by executive order for up to 120 days; and one GHURA statute, for a 500-home development on five named Dededo and Yigo lots, gives people who lived on those lots a preference or opportunity to buy units there. A lease-to-own contract under Guam's housing-corporation program is a separate arrangement with its own terms.

title: No Rent-Cap or Just-Cause Notice in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a lease notice telling tenants that rent increases are capped or that eviction needs a stated cause, because Guam has no tenant protection act of that kind for written leases. Guam's narrower rules need no notice: an oral lease of a tenant's primary residence entered after January 1, 1988 has a 5% yearly rent-increase cap, a one-year initial period and limits on eviction, but none of that applies to a written lease signed by both parties; and it is an unfair trade practice to raise dwelling rents on the basis of a shortage anticipated or caused by any disaster (damages of five times the overcharge, among other remedies), and after a qualifying disaster (serious damage to 500 or more homes, a typhoon with sustained winds of 100 mph or more, or an earthquake over 7.0) the Governor may freeze residential rents for up to 120 days. Put every lease in writing and have both parties sign it. See `edu-rent-control-gu` and `edu-tpa-exemption-notice-gu`.

title: No Truth-in-Renting Act in Guam
