bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library has a truth-in-renting act: nothing requires you to give tenants a government statement of their rights with the lease, and nothing penalizes you simply for offering a lease that contains a term the law forbids. Guam's rule is that such a term doesn't work. A lease may include terms not prohibited by the Rental Act or other law; it may not make the tenant waive or give up rights or remedies under the Act; and a provision the Act prohibits is unenforceable. Some rights also can't be changed by agreement under any circumstances (the Safe Housing Act and the source-of-income article). Don't keep a clause you know is void: Guam's deceptive-practices law lists knowingly representing that an agreement confers rights or obligations that are prohibited by law, though whether that law reaches a residential lease is unsettled (`edu-consumer-protection-act-gu`). See `edu-no-tenant-rights-statement-gu` and `edu-prohibited-lease-terms-gu`.

title: Who Can Sign a Lease: Life Estates and Shared Ownership in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library recognizes a usufruct, so the civil-law rule about leases granted by a usufructuary doesn't arise. The closest Guam interests are a life estate and limited or shared ownership, and each limits who can sign a lease. A life tenant may use the land like an owner but must do nothing to injure the inheritance, must keep buildings and fences in repair from ordinary waste, and must pay the taxes and other annual charges (and a just share of extraordinary assessments benefiting the whole inheritance); rent on a lease for life is recoverable like rent on any lease, and rent dependent on someone's life can be recovered after that person's death. No Guam statute says what happens to a lease granted by a life tenant when the life tenant dies (no Guam case was searched), so if you hold only a life estate, have the remainder owners sign the lease or consent in writing before you rent for a term that could outlast you. Two signing rules are statutory: both spouses must join in a lease of community property (or property they co-own) if the term with options may exceed five years or the term is indefinite, and a lease one spouse signs alone in breach of that rule is void; and a Chamorro Land Trust lessee may not sublet the tract or its improvements.

title: Utility Disclosures in Guam Leases
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a general utility disclosure attachment for leases: no form explaining how a shared bill is split, no submeter statement and no fee table (`edu-no-submetering-disclosure-rule-gu`, `edu-utility-apportionment-gu`).

One older Guam rule does reach longer leases. A document transferring an interest in real property, other than a lease of less than one year, can't be recorded until the transferee signs and acknowledges a statement, in a prescribed form, saying whether water and power are immediately available on the property or within 100 feet.

Assuming the section reaches a residential lease of one year or more, you impliedly warrant the accuracy of any statement that water or power is available, and if the lease says nothing about water or power, the law implies a warranty by you that each is available on the property or within 100 feet (meaning a hookup can be made within 90 days of applying, no more than 100 feet from the property line); a breach can be enforced like any warranty, with costs and reasonable attorney's fees, and if the lease lacks the water-and-power statement and water or power is in fact not available on the property or within 100 feet, the tenant may rescind the lease within ten years of the transaction.

These rules can't be waived, and the statement belongs at the end of the document, just before the signatures.

For an ordinary home with service connected the warranty is easily met, but if you rent land or a unit without a connection, say so in the lease. The optional statement `water-power-availability-gu` uses the statute's wording. Say in the lease which utilities you provide and which the tenant pays (`edu-utilities-responsibility-gu`).

title: Renting an Accessory Dwelling Unit in Guam
bodyText:
Since April 2025, Guam allows one accessory dwelling unit (ADU: a secondary studio or bedroom unit with its own entrance, kitchen and bathroom) on a qualifying single-family lot in the A, R1 and R2 zones, and an ADU that meets Guam's codes may be rented, with conditions.

The owner, a relative by blood, marriage or adoption, or the owner's designated authorized representative must live in the main home or the ADU, except in unforeseen hardship such as active military deployment or serious illness. The ADU may only be rented long term or occupied for at least six months; it can't be a bed and breakfast or short-term vacation rental, and advertising it as one is prima facie evidence that it is operating as one.

Every rental of the ADU, or of the main home while the owner's household lives in the ADU, must be a written rental agreement signed by the owner and the tenant for at least six months; after that the same tenant may stay month to month. Use `accessory-dwelling-unit-term-gu`.

The Rental Act (21 GCA Chapter 48) applies to these leases except where the ADU rules conflict, and business-licence, fair-housing and tax rules still apply. The ADU must be covered by homeowner's insurance, under the main home's policy or separately. Utilities may be shared with the main home or separately metered; tell your village mayor when the ADU is finished.

Guam's housing-discrimination exemption for owner-occupied buildings of up to four families may reach an owner-occupied lot, but the source-of-income article and federal fair-housing law have no such exemption (`edu-fair-housing-gu`, `edu-source-of-income-gu`).

title: No Alarm-Tampering Fee Rule in Guam; Cost Recovery Only
bodyText:
No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library authorizes, sets or caps a lease fee for removing, disabling or tampering with a smoke or carbon monoxide alarm, and no Guam provision searched for this library requires alarms in long-term rentals in its own words, though the model building and fire codes Guam has adopted contain smoke-alarm requirements (`edu-alarm-duties-gu`).

Charge the cost, not a penalty. A tenant must not deliberately or negligently damage or remove any part of the premises or let anyone else do so. If a tenant's tampering materially affects health and safety and the tenant doesn't fix it within five (5) working days after your written notice (or as promptly as an emergency requires), you may have the work done and bill the actual and reasonable cost as rent on the next rent due date.

A flat tampering fee fixed in advance is liquidated damages, void under Guam contract law unless actual damage would be impracticable or extremely difficult to fix, which is hard to show for a replaceable device.

Guam uses the optional detector-care clause (`detector-care-la`), which charges the reasonable cost of repair or replacement.

title: Asbestos: No Rental Disclosure Rule in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires you to inspect a rental for asbestos, disclose asbestos to an applicant or tenant, or give tenants notice before asbestos work. Asbestos is regulated as an air-pollution and waste matter. Guam EPA has adopted the federal asbestos emission standard for demolition and renovation, amended so that in a facility being demolished or renovated on Guam its work and notice requirements apply whatever the type or quantity of asbestos-containing material; for renovation of material that is not regulated friable material, Guam EPA should be notified at least five (5) working days before abatement starts, and an asbestos removal and control plan must be submitted. Whether a small residential building is a covered facility turns on federal definitions not read here, so ask Guam EPA before renovating an older building. Asbestos abatement is a separate contractor classification, and asbestos waste needs special handling at disposal. Lead paint has its own federal disclosure rule (`edu-lead-based-paint-gu`). If you know of damaged asbestos material in a unit, tell the tenant and fix it: you must keep the premises fit and habitable and comply with health and safety codes.

title: Balconies and Lanais: No Inspection Rule in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library sets a schedule of periodic inspections, engineering reports or repair deadlines for balconies, lanais, decks, exterior stairways or other elevated parts of rental buildings. Your general duties cover them. Under Guam's building law every building and every part of it, existing or new, must be kept in a safe and sanitary condition, and the owner or the owner's designated agent is responsible; a building that is structurally unsafe, lacks adequate exits or is dangerous to life because of poor maintenance or dilapidation is declared unsafe and must be vacated and repaired or demolished under that law's procedure. Under the Rental Act you must comply with health and safety codes and keep the premises fit and habitable, and the tenant must report defects you don't know about. After a typhoon or earthquake, check railings, balconies and exterior stairs before tenants use them, and keep a record of what you inspected and repaired.

title: Casualty and Re-Renting Rules Cannot Be Waived in Guam
bodyText:
Guam's casualty and mitigation rules are both in the Rental Act, and a lease can't make the tenant waive or give up rights or remedies under the Act; a term the Act prohibits is unenforceable.

Casualty: if fire or casualty (including typhoon, earthquake, wind and other natural disasters) substantially impairs enjoyment of the unit, the tenant may move out at once and give written notice within fourteen (14) working days, ending the lease as of the move-out date, or, if staying is lawful, vacate the unusable part with rent reduced in proportion; you return the recoverable deposit, and rent is accounted for as of the date of the casualty. These rights don't apply to damage caused by the tenant, their family, guests or invitees.

The Act gives you no casualty termination right, but it doesn't stop the lease from adding one (`casualty-termination-gu`) as long as the tenant's own rights stay intact.

Mitigation: if a tenant abandons, you must make reasonable efforts to re-rent at a fair rental, and your recovery is capped at the lesser of the remaining rent or the re-letting measure (`edu-mitigation-duty-gu`).

Don't write a lease term saying you have no duty to re-rent, or that the tenant owes all remaining rent whatever you do: that would take away the limits the Act sets on the tenant's liability.

title: Children in the Household in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a lease to address occupancy by children, and Guam has no occupancy standard (persons per bedroom) for private long-term rentals (`edu-permitted-occupants-gu`); the per-room limits in Guam law are for bed and breakfast homes and short-term vacation rentals. Guam's own housing-discrimination law does not list familial status, so it does not itself bar refusing families with children. Federal fair-housing law does, and it applies in Guam: don't refuse to rent, set different terms, or advertise a preference because a household includes children under 18, a pregnant person or someone getting custody, except for housing that qualifies as housing for older persons under federal law (`edu-fair-housing-gu`). Any occupancy limit you set should be reasonable for the unit's size and apply to everyone alike, counting children and adults the same way. List every occupant, including children, in the lease's occupant clause, and don't have anyone under 18 sign as a tenant (`edu-minor-tenants-gu`).

title: No Confession of Judgment in Guam Leases
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library is aimed at confession-of-judgment clauses in residential leases. Its explicit bans protect consumer credit buyers, consumer lessees of goods, borrowers and rental-purchase customers, not tenants of homes. Guam does keep an old general procedure: a judgment by confession may be entered without a lawsuit, for money due or to become due, on a written statement signed by the defendant and verified by oath that authorizes judgment for a specified sum and states the facts showing that sum is justly due. That procedure gives a money judgment only, never possession, and the statement has to be true when sworn, which a tenant can't honestly do at lease signing for defaults that haven't happened. A lease clause appointing you or your lawyer to confess judgment for the tenant would also run into the Rental Act's bar on making a tenant waive the Act's rights and remedies (the written notices and cure periods before termination). The library offers no confession-of-judgment, cognovit or pre-signed judgment clause for Guam. Recover possession and rent through an unlawful-detainer case or Small Claims (`edu-eviction-process-gu`); if a tenant who owes money later agrees to pay, a settlement or stipulated judgment made then, after the dispute arises, is a different matter.

title: Guam's Consumer Protection Act and Leases
bodyText: Guam's Deceptive Trade Practices-Consumer Protection Act (5 GCA Chapter 32) makes false, misleading or deceptive acts or practices unlawful, lets the Attorney General or a consumer sue, and allows actual, exemplary and punitive damages, up to three times actual damages for knowing conduct that is a regular business practice. Whether it reaches an ordinary residential lease is unsettled. Its definitions point both ways: goods include real property and homes leased for use, a consumer is someone who acquires goods or services by purchase or lease, and trade and commerce include leasing; but sale and purchase, which include leasing or rental of property, do not include short-term rentals of real property or leases of real property of ten years or less. Three parts plainly reach landlords: it is an unfair trade practice for a landlord to raise dwelling rents because of a shortage caused or expected from a disaster (with damages of five times the overcharge), after a qualifying disaster (serious damage to 500 or more homes, a typhoon with sustained winds of 100 mph or more, or an earthquake over 7.0) the Governor may by executive order freeze residential rents for up to 120 days, and any lease clause on costs or attorney's fees is read as mutual (`edu-attorney-fees-gu`). The Act's list doesn't name blank spaces left at signing or failing to give a copy at signing; separately, a licensed real estate broker or salesperson (including a manager who rents or collects rent for an owner for pay) who gets a person's signature on a contract pertaining to the licensee's services or transactions, such as a lease, must give that person a copy at the time of signing (owners, their regular employees and on-site resident managers are exempt from licensing). Treat the Act as if it applies: don't misstate what the lease does, charge for services not provided, or add charges not agreed in the lease.

title: Safe Housing Act Information Is Confidential in Guam
bodyText: If a tenant gives you information under Guam's Safe Housing Act (the notice that the tenant is a victim of family violence, criminal sexual conduct or stalking, and the police report, protective order or professional's statement that goes with it), you must not disclose it to a third party unless the tenant consents in writing or the disclosure is required by law or court order. Contacting the police, court or professional who issued the evidence, only to verify what the document says, is not a disclosure. Keep these papers apart from the general tenant file, limit who can see them, and don't share them with other tenants (including the person named in the order), with screening or reference requests, or in a later court case unless the law requires it. The tenant can't waive these protections in the lease. No Guam provision searched for this library sets a separate penalty for a wrongful disclosure. Related rules: `edu-dv-lease-termination-gu`, `edu-dv-qualifying-documents-gu`, `edu-dv-lockchange-gu`.

title: Calling Police or Emergency Help in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library gives tenants an express right to call the police or emergency services, or bars a lease from penalizing a tenant who does; Guam also has no nuisance-property rule that counts police calls against a landlord. Two Guam rules point the same way. Under the Safe Housing Act you may not end a lease, refuse to renew or rent, or retaliate solely because a tenant, applicant or household member is a victim of family violence, criminal sexual conduct or stalking, and that protection can't be waived; a clause treating calls for help as a lease breach would collide with it. And Guam makes it a third-degree felony for a person who commits family violence or criminal sexual conduct (or assists in or abets criminal sexual conduct) to intentionally, knowingly or recklessly prevent, or try to prevent, a victim or witness from calling 911, getting medical help or reporting to police. Don't put any fee, fine, default or non-renewal in the lease for summoning police or emergency help, and don't treat the calls themselves as a nuisance. Federal fair-housing rules may also apply to policies that penalize crime victims.

title: No Eviction Penalty Clauses in Guam Leases
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library specifically voids a lease clause that charges the tenant a penalty because you served a notice, started an eviction or won one. Other Guam rules reach most such clauses. A flat charge fixed in advance for a breach (an "eviction fee", a notice fee, a charge for filing) is liquidated damages, void unless actual damage would be impracticable or extremely difficult to fix (`edu-liquidated-damages-gu`, `edu-no-notice-service-fee-gu`). Attorney's fees and costs come from the statute or from a fee clause, and any fee clause is read as mutual (`edu-attorney-fees-gu`); the Rental Act gives you eviction costs and fees on a holdover only if it is willful and not in good faith. In an unlawful-detainer case the court assesses damages and rent due and may, in its discretion, enter judgment for three times that amount; the lease can't set that multiplier. Write no penalty for eviction into a Guam lease; recover actual costs and court-awarded amounts only.

title: Liability Disclaimers in Guam Leases
bodyText: No Guam landlord-tenant provision searched for this library (Guam Code Annotated, Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, court rules and the 38th Legislature's public laws) names exculpatory clauses, but two rules together limit them. Under Guam's contract law, every contract whose object is to exempt anyone from responsibility for his own fraud, willful injury to the person or property of another, or violation of law, whether willful or negligent, is against the policy of the law. And the Rental Act bars any lease term making the tenant waive or give up rights or remedies under the Act, which include your duties to comply with health and safety codes and keep the premises fit and habitable; a prohibited term is unenforceable. So a clause saying you are "not liable for any damage or injury" is not used for Guam: it would try to excuse breaches of those duties and violations of law. A narrower clause is possible: it may say that you are not responsible for loss that is not caused by your (or your agents') negligence, willful act or violation of law, and it may require the tenant to insure the tenant's own belongings. The library uses no-disclaimer versions of the renters-insurance, parking and storage clauses for Guam (`tenants-property-insurance-ks-oh-ca`, `parking-ks-oh-ca`, `storage-space-ks-oh-ca`). Whether a Guam court would enforce a waiver of ordinary negligence in a residential lease was not searched (no Guam or California case was read).

title: Fair Housing in Guam
bodyText: Guam's own housing-discrimination law (9 GCA §§ 70.210-70.270) makes it a misdemeanor for an owner, manager, broker or anyone acting for them to refuse to rent, set different terms, refuse an offer, misstate availability, or advertise, use an application form or make a record or inquiry that shows discrimination, because of race, color, religion, ancestry, national origin, sex or place of birth; retaliating against someone who opposed a discriminatory practice or took part in a complaint is also unlawful. It covers rentals on the open market (advertised or listed with a broker) and public rentals. It does not list disability, familial status, age, marital status or sexual orientation. Exempt: religious organizations' non-commercial housing, private clubs, a single-family house rented by an owner of no more than three such houses without a broker and without discriminatory advertising, and units in an owner-occupied building of up to four families; Guam's advertising ban does not survive the owner-occupied exemption on its words. A person aggrieved complains to the Attorney General within 30 days of learning of the practice and no later than 60 days after it occurred; other remedies stay available. Three more rules apply with no small-landlord exemption: the source-of-income article (`edu-source-of-income-gu`), the Safe Housing Act's ban on refusing or ending a tenancy because someone is a victim of family violence, criminal sexual conduct or stalking, and federal fair-housing law, which adds disability and familial status and applies in Guam (`edu-disability-accommodation-gu`, `edu-children-occupancy-gu`). Follow the federal rules as the baseline.

title: Hunting on Rented Land in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library addresses hunting or fishing rights of a tenant of rented farmland, and its farmland-lease rules are for government and Chamorro Land Trust agricultural leases, not private ones. Two Guam rules shape residential leases with land. Guam's hunting rules say that before hunting on private property a hunter must get written permission from the landowner or the owner's agent, and bar firing a gun or bow to take wildlife within fifty yards of an occupied dwelling or other structure unless the owner, the owner's agent or the person in lawful possession (which can be your tenant) consents. And the criminal statute the private-property rule points to makes it a misdemeanor to enter cultivated or fenced land, or posted unfenced land, to hunt or shoot, or to discharge a firearm there, or to refuse to leave when asked by the owner, the owner's agent or the person in lawful possession, if done without the written permission of the owner, the owner's agent or the person in lawful possession; so under the statute a tenant in lawful possession can give written permission, while the hunting rule still asks for the owner's or agent's. If your rental includes open land, say in the lease whether the tenant may hunt or allow others to hunt there, and remember that discharging firearms is also governed by the lease's firearms terms (`edu-firearms-gu`) and Guam's hunting-area rules.

title: Fire Code Duties in Guam
bodyText: Guam has a fire code: the International Fire Code, 2009 edition (with listed appendices), adopted as amended, with some provisions replaced in 2016 by text from the 2015 edition. It is part of the Guam Building Code with the 2009 International Building, Residential and Existing Building Codes, and the Guam Building Code Council reviews updates and hears appeals. Violations are civil: up to $100 for a first offense, rising for repeats of the same provision within 12 months, and a fourth offense is a misdemeanor with suspension of the business licence for up to a year or until cured. The Rental Act requires you to comply with applicable building and housing codes relative to health and safety, so the fire code's requirements for your building type are part of your duties. The model-code texts are not in this library's corpus; the Department of Public Works and the Guam Fire Department must make Guam's amendments available free, so ask them which requirements (exits, smoke alarms, extinguishers) apply to your building (`edu-alarm-duties-gu`, `edu-code-editions-gu`).

title: Which Code Edition Applies in Guam
bodyText: Guam's building and fire codes are frozen at named editions rather than rolling forward automatically. The International Building, Residential, Existing Building, Fuel Gas, Mechanical, Plumbing and Private Sewage Disposal Codes and the International Fire Code are all adopted in their 2009 editions, as amended by Guam; a 2016 law replaced some building and fire provisions with 2015-edition text, and since 2021 the 2017 Guam Tropical Energy Code governs energy efficiency. A newer model-code edition applies only when the Legislature adopts it. Some older provisions still point to codes Guam has moved away from: building-permit fees are still figured from a table in "the latest edition" of the Uniform Building Code, and special inspections refer to the 1991 Uniform Building Code. Hotel-zoned properties will come under the International Property Maintenance Code once the Department of Public Works adopts it under a 2026 law that takes effect June 3, 2027; ordinary rentals are not covered. For a repair or renovation, ask the Department of Public Works which edition and Guam amendments apply; amendments must be made available to the public free.

title: Fire Sprinklers: No Retrofit Duty in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a residential landlord to install or retrofit fire sprinklers in an existing rental, and no Guam rule bars or limits sprinkler requirements for homes. The explicit sprinkler rule found is for care homes, which must have automatic smoke detectors, fire alarm systems and an appropriate sprinkler system; fire-sprinkler system designs need a fire-protection engineer's seal. Guam has adopted the 2009 International Fire, Building, Residential and Existing Building Codes as amended, which require sprinklers in some new construction, additions and changes of occupancy; those model-code texts are not in this library's corpus, so ask the Department of Public Works or the Guam Fire Department before building, converting or substantially renovating a multi-unit building. If the building has sprinklers, you must keep them working as part of complying with health and safety codes, and the lease can tell tenants not to hang items from, paint or block sprinkler heads (`edu-no-sprinkler-disclosure-gu`, `edu-fire-code-gu`).

title: Guam's Alien Land Law and Long Leases
bodyText: Guam still has an alien land law, and it reaches some leases. A person who is not a U.S. citizen (and has not declared an intention to become one) may not acquire title to or own land in Guam, with exceptions. Residential housing is carved out: the ban does not apply to ownership or lease of single-family, residential, apartment or condominium housing, one unit per alien family (a married couple or a widow or widower with dependent children, or an unmarried person occupying his or her own dwelling). Outside that carve-out, a lease of real property in Guam to an alien for longer than five years is prohibited and void, and each party is fined: 50% of the lease's value for each year over five, split equally between lessee and lessor, plus up to $100 more for the lessor. In practice: an ordinary lease of one home to a non-citizen individual or family is unaffected at any length; but a lease longer than five years (counting options) of a second unit to the same family, of land, or of several homes to a foreign company for its workers, needs advice first. Whether a foreign corporation counts as an alien for this rule, and whether the law survives federal and Organic Act challenges, were not decided by any case searched. Don't refuse an applicant because of national origin or place of birth (`edu-fair-housing-gu`); Guam's rule is about citizenship and lease length, not a reason to turn tenants away (`edu-immigration-status-gu`). There is no lease statement for alien tenants.

title: Habitability Cannot Be Waived in Guam
bodyText: A Guam lease can reassign who performs the habitability work but can't remove the requirement itself. The Rental Act lets you and the tenant agree, in good faith, that the tenant will perform your duties to comply with health and safety codes, make the repairs needed to keep the premises fit and habitable, and report defects (`tenant-repair-agreement-gu`, `edu-habitability-modifiable-gu`). That is the only qualifier, and it moves performance; the premises must still meet the codes and stay habitable. The Act separately bars a lease from making the tenant waive or give up rights or remedies under the Act, and a prohibited term is unenforceable, so a clause accepting the unit "as is" whatever its condition, or waiving the tenant's remedies for defects, doesn't work. The older Civil Code rule that a lessor must make a dwelling habitable "in the absence of an agreement to the contrary" yields to the Rental Act where they conflict. No Guam provision searched for this library lets a tenant accept listed defects for a stated rent reduction; if you agree on one, describe the condition, keep it consistent with the codes, and record it in the move-in condition report (`move-in-condition-report-gu`).

title: Immigration Status and Renting in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library bars a landlord from asking about an applicant's or tenant's immigration or citizenship status, protects tenants from threats to report it, or makes it unlawful to rent to someone who is not lawfully present. What Guam law does bar is discrimination in rentals on the open market because of race, color, religion, ancestry, national origin, sex or place of birth, including through application forms or a record of inquiry that shows discrimination (`edu-fair-housing-gu`). Questions about citizenship or immigration papers can look like national-origin or place-of-birth screening, so if you verify identity or income, ask every applicant for the same thing (the source-of-income article protects a credit check only if you check every prospective tenant) and accept any lawful, verifiable source of income, as that article requires except for publicly subsidized housing projects and Chamorro Land Trust leases (`edu-source-of-income-gu`). Citizenship matters under Guam law in one narrow place: a lease to a non-citizen for more than five years is void unless it is of the family's one home (`edu-foreign-ownership-gu`). Federal immigration and fair-housing law also apply in Guam and were not read here.

title: Jury Waivers in Guam Leases
bodyText: Guam gives parties a statutory right to a jury in cases at law where the amount or property value is over $20, except small claims cases, and its civil rules preserve that right. The rules say how it is given up once a case exists: by not serving and filing a written demand on time, or by a written stipulation filed with the court or an oral one made in open court. No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library addresses a jury waiver signed in advance in a lease, and no Guam case on one was searched. California, whose procedure Guam's resembles, refuses to enforce pre-dispute jury waivers, but that decision does not bind Guam and was not read. The library offers no jury-waiver clause for Guam: its enforceability is uncertain, unlawful-detainer cases are usually tried quickly without a jury demand anyway, and a one-sided waiver of procedural rights invites an unconscionability or Rental Act challenge (`edu-unconscionability-gu`). If a jury trial matters to you, raise it with your lawyer when a case starts. Guam's consumer protection law separately provides no jury in actions under that chapter, and treats an agreement to arbitrate a matter arising out of the sale of goods or services as a waiver of rights that binds a consumer only if each party has a lawyer and the lawyers sign it; that law's definition of sale and purchase leaves out leases of real property of ten years or less, so whether either rule reaches a residential lease is unsettled (`edu-binding-arbitration-gu`).

title: Using a Void Lease Term in Guam
bodyText: Guam's Rental Act attaches no special penalty to putting a prohibited term in a lease or knowingly using such a lease: the term is simply unenforceable, and the tenant keeps the Act's rights. Three other Guam rules can make a bad term costly. First, from October 1, 2026, a lease term that treats a tenant worse because of the tenant's source of income (for example, refusing housing-assistance payments or adding conditions for voucher holders) is itself unlawful discrimination (unless the unit is in a housing project subsidized by public funds or lands or is a Chamorro Land Trust lease), and a court may impose a civil penalty of up to $2,000 for a first violation and a penalty of $2,500 for each later one (`edu-source-of-income-gu`). Second, using an application form, policy or advertisement that shows discrimination because of race, color, religion, ancestry, national origin, sex or place of birth is a misdemeanor under Guam's housing-discrimination law, subject to that law's exemptions (for example, an individual owner of no more than three single-family houses who rents without a broker and without publishing, posting or mailing a discriminatory advertisement or written notice, so that exemption never covers a discriminatory advertisement) (`edu-fair-housing-gu`). Third, if Guam's consumer protection law reaches the lease, knowingly representing that an agreement creates rights or obligations that are prohibited by law is a listed deceptive practice (`edu-consumer-protection-act-gu`). Review the lease against the Guam rows before using it, and strike any term this library marks as not usable in Guam.

title: Rental Act Rights Cannot Be Waived in Guam
bodyText: Guam's Rental Act has a chapter-wide non-waiver rule that runs in the tenant's favor: a lease may not provide that the tenant waives or gives up rights or remedies under the Act, and any provision the Act prohibits is unenforceable. Two articles go further and bind both sides: the Safe Housing Act (family violence, criminal sexual conduct and stalking) and the source-of-income article can't be waived or modified by agreement of the parties under any circumstances. The Act itself names the points that may be settled by agreement: the time and place rent is paid; using the deposit as last month's rent, only if you agree in writing (`deposit-last-month-rent-gu`); a good-faith agreement that the tenant will do repairs (`tenant-repair-agreement-gu`); a manager's continuing liability; your written consent to tenant repairs or deductions; who pays for substitute housing when essential services fail; a different notice period for a breach (agreed in writing; a longer period is safe, a shorter one risks being a waiver); a lease requirement to give notice of an absence of more than seven (7) working days (`extended-absence-notice-gu`); a tenant's consent to a rule adopted later; repairs, alterations and services you and the tenant agree on, for which the tenant may not unreasonably refuse entry; and a tenant's written consent to your disclosing information the tenant gave you under the Safe Housing Act. Everything else in the Act applies whatever the lease says.

title: No Plain-Language Lease Law in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a residential lease to be written in plain language, to pass a readability test, to be divided and captioned by sections, or to use a minimum type size. Guam's type-size and plain-English rules found are for other documents (time-share offering statements, notary fee schedules, certain consumer sale notices, court filings and crime-victim notices). Write clearly anyway: a term a tenant can show was misleading may be attacked under Guam's consumer protection law if that law reaches leases (`edu-consumer-protection-act-gu`) or as unconscionable (`edu-unconscionability-gu`), and no Guam provision searched for this library requires a translation (`edu-no-translation-duty-gu`). Use headings, define terms once, and state every Guam-specific period as working days where the Rental Act counts days.

title: No Consumer Waiver Statement Required in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires a residential lease to carry a consumer statement listing the rights the tenant gives up, to meet a readability score, or to be pre-approved by the Attorney General. No Guam provision searched for this library sets a plain-language rule for leases (`edu-no-plain-language-rule-gu`). A list of waivers would serve little purpose in Guam: the Rental Act already makes any term that waives the tenant's rights or remedies under it unenforceable, and the Safe Housing Act and source-of-income article can't be modified by agreement (`edu-nonwaiver-rule-gu`).

title: Pool Safety Rules for Guam Rentals
bodyText: A pool at an apartment house or other multiple rental property is a public swimming pool under Guam law, regulated by the Department of Public Health and Social Services. Before operating one you need a posted sanitary permit (and plan approval before building or substantially altering it). The pool, chemical storage and mechanical spaces must be enclosed by a barrier at least six feet high, with self-closing, self-latching, lockable gates; access must be prevented when the pool is closed. (The barrier rules don't apply if the pool has 24-hour manned security, monitored video surveillance of the whole perimeter and posted no-entry signs.) A qualified operator with recognized training must supervise it. A qualified lifeguard must be on duty whenever it is open unless the water surface is under 2,250 square feet, and even a smaller pool needs one at all times it is open if it is deeper than five feet at any point, lets children under 14 swim unsupervised, has a diving board or other entry from above the deck, has any point more than 30 feet from the deck, or is being used by youth groups or for group training; without lifeguard service you must post "Warning -- No Lifeguard on Duty" in letters at least four inches high, plus a sign that children under 14 should not use the pool without direct adult supervision. Post resuscitation diagrams, emergency numbers, first-aid locations, behavior rules and the inspection grade placard, and report injuries as the rules require. No Guam provision searched for this library requires a pool notice at lease signing. A private residential pool under the homeowner's direct control, used by family and guests, is exempt; whether a pool at a single rented house falls in that exemption isn't settled by the rules' words, so ask the Department. Put any pool-use rules in your lease rules (`rules-gu`).

title: Lease Terms That Do Not Work in Guam
bodyText: Guam has no single list of banned lease terms. The Rental Act lets a lease include any term not prohibited by the Act or other law, rule or regulation, bars any term making the tenant waive the Act's rights or remedies, and makes a prohibited term unenforceable. Terms that don't work in a Guam lease, each covered in its own row: (1) any waiver of Rental Act rights or remedies, and any change to Safe Housing Act or source-of-income rights (`edu-nonwaiver-rule-gu`); (2) collecting more than the first month's rent and the security deposit (with any pet deposit) at lease commencement, a deposit over one month's rent, or a pet deposit over $500 per pet (`edu-move-in-money-gu`, `edu-security-deposit-limit-gu`); (3) a fixed sum for a breach unless actual damage would be impracticable or extremely difficult to fix (`edu-liquidated-damages-gu`); (4) exemption from responsibility for your own fraud, willful injury or violation of law (`edu-exculpatory-clauses-gu`); (5) a one-way attorney's fee clause, which is read as mutual, and any fee claim in a source-of-income case (`edu-attorney-fees-gu`); (6) entry rights beyond the Act's (`edu-landlord-entry-gu`); (7) a rule adopted after signing that fails the Act's four tests (`rules-gu`); (8) e-mail or text replacing a notice method the law specifies (`edu-notice-delivery-gu`); (9) letting part of a room to one family while letting it to another, which Guam forbids whatever the agreement; (10) terms that discriminate by source of income or by a protected class (`edu-fair-housing-gu`, `edu-source-of-income-gu`). Confession-of-judgment, jury-waiver and arbitration clauses are not offered for Guam (`edu-confession-of-judgment-gu`, `edu-jury-waiver-gu`, `edu-binding-arbitration-gu`). No Guam provision searched for this library says when the lease must be handed over or bans passing home-warranty charges, but charging the tenant for repairs that are your duty would undercut the Act's repair duties.

title: Questions You May Not Ask Applicants in Guam
bodyText: Separate from refusing to rent, Guam's housing-discrimination law makes it unlawful to use an application form, or to make a record of inquiry about a prospective rental, that indicates discrimination or an intent to discriminate because of race, color, religion, ancestry, national origin, sex or place of birth; announcing a policy or publishing a notice or advertisement that does so is also unlawful. It is a misdemeanor, and it applies to rentals on the open market (advertised or brokered) unless an exemption applies (`edu-fair-housing-gu`). The source-of-income article bars advertisements and notices indicating a limitation based on source of income (no "No Section 8"), except for housing projects subsidized by public funds or lands and Chamorro Land Trust leases, and treats a credit check as lawful under that article when you check every prospective tenant (`edu-source-of-income-gu`). Keep application forms to what you need to decide: identity, contact details, rental history, verifiable income from any lawful source, and consent to a credit check run on everyone. Don't ask about religion, ancestry, national origin or place of birth; federal fair-housing rules also bear on questions about disability and family status.

title: Registered Offenders: No Occupancy Rule in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library restricts where registered sex offenders may live, requires a landlord to check the registry or refuse to rent to a registrant, or makes it a crime to lease a unit where registrants live together. Registrants must report their residence (or, without a fixed address, where they habitually live), and Guam's public registry website shows each registrant's residential address with a warning that the information must not be used to unlawfully injure, harass or commit a crime against anyone. The one housing rule found is for short-term lodging: no home may be licensed as a bed and breakfast at the physical address of a registered sex offender. If you screen applicants using the registry, apply one written standard to everyone, consider the offense and how long ago it was, and follow fair-housing law (`edu-fair-housing-gu`, `edu-tenant-screening-gu`). No Guam provision searched for this library requires a lease statement about offenders (`edu-no-sex-offender-disclosure-gu`).

title: Renting Homes in Guam’s Single-Family Zone
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library limits long-term renting of a home in Guam's single-family (R1) zone or requires the owner to live on the lot. The R1 zone permits one-family dwellings, bed and breakfasts and accessory uses (including accessory dwelling units), and allows duplexes and short-term vacation rental units only as conditional uses; a one-family home may be rented to one household like any other. Owner-occupancy rules apply only to the special uses: a bed and breakfast's owner-proprietor must live in the home full time; and when a lot has an accessory dwelling unit, the owner (or a relative or designated representative) must live in the main home or the ADU (except in unforeseen hardship such as active military deployment or serious illness), and every rental there must be a written agreement signed by owner and tenant for an initial period of at least six months, after which the same tenant may stay on month to month (`edu-accessory-dwelling-unit-gu`). Renting rooms or the whole home for short stays needs its own licence or certificate. Condominium declarations and recorded covenants may limit renting; read them before you lease (`edu-hoa-compliance-gu`).

title: Source-of-Income Discrimination Ban in Guam
bodyText: Since October 1, 2026, Guam law bars discrimination in housing because of a person's source of income: any lawful and verifiable money paid to or for the person, including wages, government or private assistance, grants and loans (such as Section 8 vouchers and other rental assistance), pensions, annuities and investment income. You and anyone acting for you may not refuse to rent or show a unit, refuse an offer, say a unit is unavailable when it isn't, or advertise a limitation (no "No Section 8") because of source of income, and you may not set different terms because a person receives public housing assistance or takes part in a contract the assistance program requires. One exception: if a housing-assistance program's first payment is late under federal HUD rules because of processing delays or a government shutdown, you keep your ordinary rights and remedies. Checking credit is not unlawful under the article if you check every prospective tenant, so check everyone or no one. The rule has no small-landlord or owner-occupied exemption; it does not apply to publicly subsidized housing projects or leases of Chamorro Land Trust property. GHURA enforces it; a court may impose a civil penalty of up to $2,000 for a first violation and a penalty of $2,500 for each later one, and order an injunction, but no party may recover attorney's fees or costs. It can't be waived or modified by agreement. Older guidance, including GHURA's online Section 8 landlord FAQ, says refusing Section 8 is not discrimination; under Guam law that is no longer true. Apply the same screening criteria to all applicants, and measure any income requirement against the share of rent the applicant will pay (no Guam provision searched for this library says how; this is the cautious course).

title: Steam Radiator Covers: Not Applicable in Guam
bodyText: This topic does not arise in Guam. Guam's tropical climate means rental housing has no steam or hot-water radiator heat, and no provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library mentions radiator covers, steam heat in dwellings or a radiator lease rider. No Guam provision searched for this library sets a heating standard for rentals (`edu-heating-na-gu`). Hot surfaces that do exist in Guam rentals, such as water heaters and cooking appliances, fall under your general duties to comply with building and housing codes relative to health and safety and to make the repairs needed to keep the premises fit and habitable.

title: Voucher Inspections and Source-of-Income Rules in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library addresses refusing to rent because a housing-assistance program requires an inspection, or sets a deadline for program approval like some states' rules. Since October 1, 2026, though, Guam's source-of-income article bars refusing to rent because of a person's source of income, including housing assistance, and bars setting different terms because a person receives public housing assistance or takes part in a contract the program requires (`edu-source-of-income-gu`). A refusal to let the program inspect, or to sign the program's required contract, can therefore look like refusing the voucher holder, so cooperate with the program's inspection and paperwork as you would with any applicant's screening. If the program's first payment is late under HUD rules because of processing delays or a government shutdown, Guam law keeps your ordinary rights and remedies. Guam law itself recognizes program inspections in one place: a dwelling unit seeking Guam's one-time temporary rental business licence may use a HUD-certified or GHURA-authorized inspector where it is or will be rented to tenants receiving federal housing assistance. Inspections inside an occupied unit need the usual notice of at least 24 hours to the tenant (unless an emergency or impracticable) and must be at reasonable hours (`edu-landlord-entry-gu`). Publicly subsidized housing projects and Chamorro Land Trust leases are outside the source-of-income article. Federal voucher-program rules apply and were not read.

title: Protecting Tenant Information in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library generally bars you from disclosing information about a tenant or requires the tenant's consent before you share it, with one exception: information a tenant gives you under the Safe Housing Act (family violence, criminal sexual conduct or stalking) may not be disclosed to a third party unless the tenant consents in writing or the law or a court requires it (`edu-dv-confidentiality-gu`). Two data laws also reach tenant files (`edu-tenant-records-gu`): Guam's breach-notification law, if you keep names with Social Security, driver's licence or Guam ID numbers, or financial account or card numbers with any code or password needed to access the account, unencrypted, in computerized form; and the Social Security Number Confidentiality Act's limits on displaying and transmitting Social Security numbers. Good practice: share tenant information only with people who need it (your manager, contractors who need a phone number for a repair, a court), get written consent before answering reference or credit inquiries beyond confirming tenancy dates, and keep application papers secure.

title: Housing Your Employees in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires an employer who houses an employee to give a signed disclosure of occupancy and vacating terms, or to offer a rental agreement when the job ends. Three Guam rules matter. First, the eviction chapter expressly reaches a person who became the occupant as an employee once the employment has lawfully ended or the agreed occupancy period has expired, so an employer-landlord recovers possession through an unlawful-detainer case, never by lockout. Second, the Rental Act has no exclusion for employee housing (unlike some states' acts); it applies to any agreement, written or not, about use and occupancy of a dwelling unit, so if the employee pays rent or the occupancy is a rental agreement, its notice and deposit rules apply, and no Guam case on employer housing was searched. Third, housing for temporary (H-2B and similar) workers is regulated: an employer certified for more than five temporary alien workers must make lodging available, temporary workforce housing needs a Public Health sanitary and workers' dormitory permit, and an employer may deduct housing or meal costs from those workers' wages only with permits in place and the worker's written consent filed with the Department of Labor. If you house an employee, put the terms in a signed writing: whether rent is charged or the housing is part of pay, how long the occupancy lasts, and what notice ends it when the job ends.

title: Tenant Organizing: No Guam Statute
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library protects tenants' right to form or join a tenant organization, meet in common areas or distribute materials, or bars a landlord from interfering with organizing, and no Guam provision searched for this library is a general anti-retaliation law (`edu-retaliation-gu`). Two narrow protections exist: you may not retaliate against anyone for opposing a practice Guam's housing-discrimination law forbids or for taking part in a complaint under it, and you may not retaliate against a tenant solely because the tenant or a household member is a victim of family violence, criminal sexual conduct or stalking or ended a lease under the Safe Housing Act. A lease rule limiting meetings or flyers in common areas must still meet the Rental Act's test for rules: it must promote tenant safety and welfare or preserve your property from deliberate abuse, apply to all tenants fairly, not evade your obligations, and be adopted on thirty (30) working days' notice (`rules-gu`). Treat tenant groups like any other residents.

title: Screening Applicants in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library is a tenant-screening statute: no rule on the timing of criminal-history checks, look-back periods, minimum-income tests, reusable screening reports or a liability shield for renting to someone with a record. The rules that shape screening are elsewhere. (1) Source of income: since October 1, 2026 you may not refuse an applicant, or set different terms, because of a lawful and verifiable source of income such as wages, housing assistance, pensions or investments, and a credit check is lawful under that article when you check every prospective tenant; publicly subsidized housing projects and Chamorro Land Trust leases are exempt (`edu-source-of-income-gu`). (2) Discrimination: on the open market you may not refuse, or use a form or inquiry that shows discrimination, because of race, color, religion, ancestry, national origin, sex or place of birth (`edu-fair-housing-gu`, `edu-protected-class-inquiry-gu`); federal fair-housing rules, including those on criminal-record policies, also apply and were not read. (3) Victims: you may not refuse to rent solely because an applicant or household member is a victim of family violence, criminal sexual conduct or stalking, or ended a lease under the Safe Housing Act. (4) Expunged records: revealing an expunged official record to someone not entitled to it is a misdemeanor, so don't use or pass on one. Write down your criteria (income relative to the applicant's share of rent, rental history, credit standard, any criminal-history standard with a reasonable look-back), apply them to everyone, and keep the reasons for each decision. Application fees: `edu-application-fees-gu`.

title: Unconscionable Lease Terms in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library lets a court refuse to enforce an unconscionable lease clause. Guam's unconscionability statutes are for other transactions: sales of goods under Guam's Uniform Commercial Code, and consumer credit sales, consumer leases of goods and consumer loans under Guam's consumer credit code; Guam's consumer protection law reaches unconscionable conduct only in non-land transactions. One general rule does reach leases: damages must in all cases be reasonable, and where an obligation appears to create a right to unconscionable and grossly oppressive damages, contrary to substantial justice, no more than reasonable damages can be recovered. Guam courts may also apply common-law unconscionability to a lease, but no Guam case was searched. No Guam provision searched for this library lets a court revise or end a running lease because circumstances have made it excessively onerous. Practical effect: the Rental Act's own limits (`edu-prohibited-lease-terms-gu`) do most of the work, and any charge or remedy in the lease should be one you could justify as reasonable. The library gives no Guam clause declaring a particular term enforceable.

title: No Veterans Rental Incentive in Guam
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library gives private landlords a tax credit, payment, deposit guarantee or other incentive for renting to veterans. Guam's veterans rules point elsewhere: the Guam Office of Veterans Affairs is directed to streamline access to housing assistance through agreements with other agencies; GHURA must give a veteran who is the named applicant a preference for public housing; and veterans have mortgage-loan programs and a property-tax exemption for 100% disabled veterans who own their homes. Rental help a veteran receives from a government or private program is a source of income you must treat like any other (`edu-source-of-income-gu`), and servicemembers have their own early-termination rights under federal law (`edu-servicemember-rights-gu`). Ask the Guam Office of Veterans Affairs about current programs.

title: Water Heater Temperature: No Guam Rule
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires you to set a water heater to a maximum temperature before a new tenant moves in, or to give a scald-prevention notice. The maximum-temperature and mixing-valve rules found are for handwashing sinks in schools, food establishments and similar regulated facilities, and Guam's amended plumbing code addresses hot-water temperature maintenance in piping as an energy matter; neither is a move-in setting rule for dwellings. Hot water is an essential service under the Rental Act: if, contrary to the lease, you willfully or negligently fail to supply it, the tenant may, after written notice, secure it and deduct the actual and reasonable cost from rent or obtain substitute housing with rent excused for that period (you don't pay for the substitute housing unless you both agreed in writing); these rights don't apply if the condition was caused by the deliberate negligent act or omission of the tenant, a member of the tenant's family or other persons on the premises. Good practice: check the thermostat at each turnover (about 120°F is a common safe setting), make sure gas water heaters are vented and fitted with automatic shut-off, and show the tenant where the heater's shut-off is.

title: Window Guards: No Guam Rule
bodyText: No provision in the Guam Code Annotated, the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations, the court rules or the 38th Legislature's public laws searched for this library requires window guards, window stops or other fall-prevention devices in rentals, or a window-guard notice in the lease. Your general duties apply: comply with health and safety codes, keep the premises fit and habitable, and keep every part of the building, including windows, screens, louvers and railings, in a safe condition; the 2009 International Building and Residential Codes adopted by Guam contain window-sill and guard provisions for new construction, but their texts are not in this library's corpus. Many Guam homes have typhoon shutters and security grilles on windows: if you install bars or grilles on a bedroom window, make sure they open from inside without a key or tool so the window can still be used as an emergency exit, and check with the Department of Public Works. If a tenant with young children asks for window stops, installing them is a low-cost safety step.

title: Checks Marked 'Paid in Full'
bodyText: Guam never adopted the revised Uniform Commercial Code rule on checks marked 'paid in full': its commercial-paper law is the older version, with no section on settling a claim by cashing such a check. Its reservation-of-rights rule (13 GCA § 1207) also lacks the later sentence saying it does not apply to an accord and satisfaction, and courts elsewhere have split on whether cashing a full-payment check 'under protest' under that older rule keeps the balance. Guam's Civil Code supplies the rule instead: an accord is an agreement to accept less than you are owed, it does not end the obligation until it is carried out, and your acceptance of what the accord offers is satisfaction and ends the obligation (18 GCA §§ 82401-82403); part performance ends an obligation only when you expressly accept it in writing, in satisfaction (18 GCA § 82404). How Guam's courts apply these to a cashed check is case law. The cautious course: don't cash a check for less than you claim that is marked as payment in full of a disputed amount; return it uncashed.

title: Duty of Good Faith
bodyText: Guam's landlord-tenant statutes impose no general duty of good faith of the kind in the Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act (the Guam Landlord and Tenant Rental Act and the Civil Code's lease chapter searched); good faith appears only in specific rules. The Rental Act defines 'good faith' as a transaction done honestly and objectively with no deliberate intent to defraud the other party (21 GCA § 48102(i)), the standard its specific good-faith rules use. Courts in many states read a covenant of good faith and fair dealing into every contract, a lease included; whether and how Guam's courts do is case law, so act as if the duty applies. In practice: give notices, enter, handle the deposit, enforce lease terms and end a tenancy honestly and for the purpose the law or the lease gives you the right, not as a pretext.

title: Chamorro Land Trust Homes Can't Be Rented Out
bodyText: Guam has no tribal land, and a private owner leasing private land needs no government approval. Guam's closest equivalent to communal land is Chamorro Land Trust land, and it carries its own rule: the Chamorro Land Trust Commission leases tracts to eligible beneficiaries (native Chamorros, under the older chapter) for 99 years at $1 a year, title stays with Guam, and every such lease is deemed to say that the lessee shall not sublet his interest in the tract or the improvements on it (21 GCA §§ 75107(a)-(b), 75108(b), (e); 21 GCA § 75A108(e)). The lessee also may not transfer, mortgage or pledge the interest except to an eligible beneficiary, and then only with the Commission's approval (21 GCA § 75108(e); 21 GCA § 75A108(e)). Leases approved before January 1, 2021 stay under chapter 75; later ones fall under chapter 75A (21 GCA ch. 75, 2021 Note). The Commission may allow commercial leases to be subleased, but that permission is for commercial leases only (21 GCA § 75A107(g)). So if you hold a Chamorro Land Trust residential or agricultural lease, you can't rent the house or the land to a tenant, and a tenant who signs such a rental gets no lease from the Trust. Check whether a property is Trust land before you lease it. A lease of private land to a non-citizen for more than five years has its own limit (see `edu-foreign-ownership-gu`).

title: Recording a Lease in Guam
bodyText: Guam doesn't require you to record a residential lease, and an unrecorded lease is valid between you and the tenant and anyone who knows of it (21 GCA § 37105). Recording matters for leases longer than a year. Every conveyance of real property, other than a lease for a term not exceeding one year, is void as against a later good-faith buyer or mortgagee for value whose own conveyance is recorded first (21 GCA § 37102), and 'conveyance' includes every written instrument creating an interest in real property (21 GCA § 37103). A recorded conveyance is notice to later buyers and mortgagees from the time it is filed with the Director of Land Management (21 GCA § 37101). Before a lease of one year or more can be recorded, the tenant must sign and acknowledge a statement, in the form the statute sets, that the tenant knows whether water and power are available on the property (21 GCA § 60314(a)); the library's optional Water and Power Availability Statement clause (`water-power-availability-gu`) does this. If the land is registered land (with a certificate of title), a lease other than one of a year or less with the tenant in actual possession takes effect only as a contract between you and the tenant until it is filed with the Registrar of Titles (21 GCA § 29155), and a registered owner takes free of unregistered interests except a lease of up to one year where the tenant actually occupies the land (21 GCA § 29135(a)). No Guam statute ties notice to a relative's lease the way Nebraska's does. Practical step: for a lease longer than a year, include the water and power statement and record the lease (or register it, for registered land).
